1.1.0: I meditate in my mind on Śaṅkara, the lord of Ambikā: he who is auspicious at the beginning and the end, whose nature has no equal ever born, the noble Lord, unaging and immortal, the god who is the Self, the five-faced one, whose nature is to sport in the five mighty acts.
1.1.1: Vyāsa said: At Prayāga, the field of dharma, the great sacred field, the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Kālindī (Yamunā), supremely holy, on the path to the world of Brahmā— ॥1॥
1.1.2: sages of disciplined minds, devoted to vows of truth, of great vigour and great fortune, performed a great sacrificial session. ॥2॥
1.1.3: Hearing of the session there, Sūta—the great sage, disciple of Vyāsa, foremost of Purāṇa-reciters—came to see the sages. ॥3॥
1.1.4: Seeing Sūta arrive, the sages were then delighted, and with very gladdened hearts they honoured him according to rule. ॥4॥
1.1.5: Then those great-souled ones, full of humility and very pleased, with joined palms, having offered praise according to rule, spoke: ॥5॥
1.1.6: O Romaharṣaṇa, all-knowing one, through the greatness of your good fortune you have indeed received from Vyāsa the entire lore of the Purāṇas, in every sense. ॥6॥
1.1.7: Therefore you are the vessel of wondrous stories, as the ocean is the mine of precious jewels. ॥7॥
1.1.8: Whatever has been, whatever will be, and whatever else exists—there is nothing in the three worlds unknown to you. ॥8॥
1.1.9: By the power of our good fortune you have come here to see this sacrifice; you ought not to leave in vain without doing us some good. ॥9॥
1.1.10: All truth, auspicious and inauspicious, we have heard before; yet we reach no satisfaction—the desire to hear arises again and again. ॥10॥
1.1.11: Now there is just one thing to be heard, O Sūta of good mind; tell it, even though it is a secret, if you have favour toward us. ॥11॥
1.1.12: When the dreadful Kali age has come, men will be devoid of merit, all given to wicked conduct, averse to truthful speech; ॥12॥
1.1.13: intent on slandering others, coveting others' wealth, their minds attached to others' wives, devoted to harming others; ॥13॥
1.1.14: regarding the body as the self, deluded, unbelievers, with the intellect of beasts, hostile to mother and father, treating women as gods, servants of lust. ॥14॥
1.1.15: Brāhmaṇas will be seized by the demon of greed, living by selling the Veda, having studied learning only to earn wealth, deluded by pride; ॥15॥
1.1.16: having abandoned the duties of their own caste, mostly deceivers of others, lacking the thrice-daily sandhyā rites, devoid of knowledge of Brahman; ॥16॥
1.1.17: pitiless, thinking themselves learned, neglecting their proper conduct and vows, devoted to the labour of farming, cruel by nature, impure of heart. ॥17॥
1.1.18: Likewise all kṣatriyas will be inclined to abandon their own dharma, keeping evil company, delighting in sin, devoted to adultery; ॥18॥
1.1.19: cowardly, fond of avoiding battle, given to flight, living like base thieves, like śūdras, their minds slaves to lust; ॥19॥
1.1.20: lacking skill in weapons and missiles, having abandoned the protection of cows and brāhmaṇas, failing to protect those who seek refuge, always hunting for the pleasures of women; ॥20॥
1.1.21: devoid of the true dharma of protecting subjects, intent on enjoyment, destroyers of their subjects, wicked, gladly doing violence to living beings. ॥21॥
1.1.22: The vaiśyas will be without sacraments, inclined to abandon their own dharma, on evil paths, intent on their own gain, dishonest in their trade with scales; ॥22॥
1.1.23: lacking devotion to gurus, gods and the twice-born, evil-minded, mostly not feeding brāhmaṇas, miserly, close-fisted; ॥23॥
1.1.24: greatly delighting in affairs as paramours of women, impure of heart, their minds confused by greed and delusion, devoid of dharma in pious works such as pūrta. ॥24॥
1.1.25: Likewise, whatever śūdras there are will be intent on brāhmaṇical conduct, of splendid appearance, deluded, inclined to abandon their own dharma; ॥25॥
1.1.26: performing austerities in abundance, robbing the twice-born of their splendour, causing early death of children, devoted to the utterance of mantras; ॥26॥
1.1.27: worshippers of the śālagrāma stone and the like, intent on fire-offerings, of hostile thinking, crooked, reviling the twice-born. ॥27॥
1.1.28: The wealthy will do evil deeds, the learned will be quarrelsome; speakers on stories, worship and dharma will be destroyers of dharma; ॥28॥
1.1.29: some with the appearance of good kings, hypocritical, lavish givers, greatly arrogant, considering brāhmaṇas and others as servants and regarding themselves as masters; ॥29॥
1.1.30: devoid of their own dharma, deluded, of mixed caste, cruel-minded, always extremely proud, destroyers of the four varṇas; ॥30॥
1.1.31: thinking themselves of noble birth, mingling with all four varṇas, causing the degradation of all varṇas, deluded, yet performing what they call good rites. ॥31॥
1.1.32: Women too will mostly be fallen, showing contempt for their husbands, hostile to their fathers-in-law, fearless, eating impure food; ॥32॥
1.1.33: given to wanton coquetry, of bad character, overwhelmed by passion, always delighting in the company of paramours, and turned away from their own husbands. ॥33॥
1.1.34: Sons will lack devotion to mother and father, evil-minded, always studying false learning, their bodies seized by disease. ॥34॥
1.1.35: For these, whose intellect is ruined and who are inclined to abandon their own dharma, how, O Sūta, can there be a good destiny in the next world and in this one? ॥35॥
1.1.36: Thus our minds are constantly troubled with anxiety; for surely there is no other dharma equal to helping others. ॥36॥
1.1.37: Since you know all doctrines, kindly tell us now that easy means by which the destruction of their sins may quickly come about. ॥37॥
1.1.38: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of the sages of purified souls, Sūta remembered Śaṅkara in his mind and spoke to those sages. ॥38॥
1.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The questions of the sages, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
1.2.1: Sūta said: Well asked, O virtuous ones, is your question, which brings benefit to the three worlds. Remembering my guru, out of affection for you I shall tell it; listen to it with attention. ॥1॥
1.2.2: It is the Purāṇa, supreme in this way, the whole essence of Vedānta, which lifts away the entire flood of sins and grants the highest good in the next world. ॥2॥
1.2.3: It destroys the impurities of the Kali age; in it the supreme glory of Śiva ever shines forth, O brahmins; it grants the fruit of the four aims of life. ॥3॥
1.2.4: O best of the twice-born, merely by studying that Purāṇa, the Śaiva one which is the best of all, they will attain an excellent, blessed state. ॥4॥
1.2.5: Sin, headed by the killing of a brahmin, flourishes only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥5॥
1.2.6: The great calamities of Kali will roam about fearlessly only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥6॥
1.2.7: All the scriptures dispute with one another only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥7॥
1.2.8: The true nature of Śiva remains hard to understand even for the great only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥8॥
1.2.9: The cruel servants of Yama will roam about fearlessly only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥9॥
1.2.10: All the Purāṇas roar loudly on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥10॥
1.2.11: All the holy places dispute their superiority on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen in the world — ah! ॥11॥
1.2.12: All the mantras gleefully dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥12॥
1.2.13: All the sacred regions dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥13॥
1.2.14: All the sacred seats (pīṭhas) dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥14॥
1.2.15: All the forms of giving dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥15॥
1.2.16: And all those gods dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥16॥
1.2.17: And all the doctrines dispute on the earth only so long as the Śiva Purāṇa has not arisen on the earth. ॥17॥
1.2.18: O twice-born, O best of sages, I cannot describe in full the fruit of reciting and hearing this Śaiva Purāṇa. ॥18॥
1.2.19: Nevertheless, O sinless ones, I shall tell you a little of its greatness, as Vyāsa told it to me long ago; listen with concentrated mind. ॥19॥
1.2.20: Whoever, filled with devotion, reads even a single verse or half a verse of this Śiva Purāṇa is freed from sin in an instant. ॥20॥
1.2.21: Whoever reads this Śiva Purāṇa every day, untiringly, with devotion and according to his ability, is called liberated while living. ॥21॥
1.2.22: Whoever always worships this Śiva Purāṇa with devotion obtains, day after day, the fruit of a horse-sacrifice, without doubt. ॥22॥
1.2.23: Whoever hears this Śiva Purāṇa from another, or from me, even with a desire for ordinary worldly ends, he too would be freed from sin. ॥23॥
1.2.24: Whoever bows to this Śiva Purāṇa from nearby obtains the fruit of worshipping all the gods; there is no doubt. ॥24॥
1.2.25: Hear the meritorious fruit of one who, having himself written out this Śiva Purāṇa as a book, gives it to devotees of Śiva. ॥25॥
1.2.26: The fruit, rare in the world, that comes from having studied the scriptures and expounded the Vedas — that fruit would be his. ॥26॥
1.2.27: Whoever, fasting on the fourteenth lunar day, expounds this Śiva Purāṇa in an assembly of Śiva's devotees is the best of men. ॥27॥
1.2.28: For each syllable he would obtain the fruit of a puraścaraṇa of the Gāyatrī; having enjoyed all desires here, at the end he would attain nirvāṇa. ॥28॥
1.2.29: I shall tell the merit of one who, fasting on the fourteenth day and keeping vigil at night, reads or even hears it. ॥29॥
1.2.30: Whatever fruit one gains by giving, many times over at all the holy places beginning with Kurukṣetra, wealth equal to oneself during a total solar eclipse, ॥30॥
1.2.31: — the fruit one enjoys by giving that to brahmins headed by Vyāsa — that fruit would be his; it is true, true, without doubt. ॥31॥
1.2.32: Whoever chants this Śiva Purāṇa day and night — the gods led by Indra would await his command. ॥32॥
1.2.33: For one who regularly reads and hears this Śiva Purāṇa, whatever good deed he does becomes multiplied ten-million-fold. ॥33॥
1.2.34: But whoever, with collected mind, reads the holy Rudra Saṃhitā therein — even a brahmin-slayer becomes pure of soul in just three days. ॥34॥
1.2.35: Whoever, observing silence, reads that Rudra Saṃhitā three times daily near an image of Bhairava obtains all his desires. ॥35॥
1.2.36: For whoever recites that Rudra Saṃhitā while circumambulating a banyan and a bilva tree, the sin of brahmin-slaying departs. ॥36॥
1.2.37: The Kailāsa Saṃhitā therein is held to be even higher than that; it is Brahman itself in form, illuminating the meaning of the Praṇava (Om). ॥37॥
1.2.38: Śaṅkara knows the greatness of the Kailāsa Saṃhitā fully; Vyāsa knows half of it, and I know half of that, O twice-born. ॥38॥
1.2.39: Of it I shall tell a little; it cannot be told in full. Knowing it, people would at that very moment attain purity of mind. ॥39॥
1.2.40: O twice-born, a sin which that Raudrī Saṃhitā does not destroy — such I do not see in the world, though I search for it always. ॥40॥
1.2.41: Having drunk that nectar, which Śiva joyfully produced by churning the ocean of the Upaniṣads and offered to Kumāra, one becomes immortal. ॥41॥
1.2.42: One who is intent on making expiation for sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa, having recited that saṃhitā for just a month, is thereby released. ॥42॥
1.2.43: That saṃhitā, by being recited even once, destroys the sin arising from accepting improper gifts, eating improper food, evil speech and the like. ॥43॥
1.2.44: Whoever recites that saṃhitā in a Śiva temple or in a bilva grove — the fruit he obtains lies beyond the range even of speech. ॥44॥
1.2.45: Whoever, reciting that saṃhitā with devotion, feeds brāhmaṇas at a śrāddha — all his ancestors go to the supreme abode of Śambhu. ॥45॥
1.2.46: Whoever, fasting on the fourteenth lunar day, recites that saṃhitā at the foot of a bilva tree is Śiva himself and is worshipped by the gods. ॥46॥
1.2.47: There are other saṃhitās too in it, bestowing the fruits of all desires; but two should be known as distinguished, filled with Śiva's divine play and knowledge. ॥47॥
1.2.48: This is the Śaiva Purāṇa so declared, equal to the Veda; it was first composed by Śiva himself, equal to Brahman. ॥48॥
1.2.49: The Vidyeśa, likewise the Raudra, the Vaināyaka, then the Aumika, the Mātra, the Rudraikādaśaka, the Kailāsa, the Śatarudraka, ॥49॥
1.2.50: the Koṭirudrasahasrādya, and likewise the Koṭirudra, the Vāyavīya, and the one named Dharma — thus the Purāṇa by its divisions. ॥50॥
1.2.51: These saṃhitās, twelve in number, are held to be supremely meritorious. O brāhmaṇas, I shall tell their count; listen to it all attentively. ॥51॥
1.2.52: The Vidyeśa has ten thousand verses; the Raudra, likewise the Vaināyaka, the Auma and the one called Mātṛ-purāṇa have eight thousand each. ॥52॥
1.2.53: O twice-born ones, the Rudraikādaśaka has thirteen thousand; the Kailāsa six thousand, and the Śatarudra half of that. ॥53॥
1.2.54: The Koṭirudra is three times that (nine thousand); the one called Sahasrakoṭirudra is declared to have eleven thousand by the count of verses. ॥54॥
1.2.55: The Vāyavīya has forty hundred (kha = 0, abdhi = 4), that is, four thousand, the Dharma twelve (ravi) thousand; thus the Śaiva Purāṇa, by its divisions of number, totals a hundred thousand. ॥55॥
1.2.56: That was abridged by Vyāsa to twenty-four thousand verses; the Śaiva, the fourth Purāṇa among them, has seven saṃhitās. ॥56॥
1.2.57: Formerly, at the creation of old, the Purāṇa composed by Śiva was vast, measuring a hundred crore verses by count. ॥57॥
1.2.58: When, in the Dvāpara and other ages, the Purāṇa was divided eighteenfold and abridged to four hundred thousand verses by Dvaipāyana and others, ॥58॥
1.2.59: the Śiva Purāṇa was proclaimed as having twenty-four thousand by count of ślokas, with seven saṃhitās, equal to Brahman. ॥59॥
1.2.60: Among them the first is called Vidyeśvara; the second should be known as Raudrī; the third is called Śatarudra; the fourth is Koṭirudra; ॥60॥
1.2.61: the fifth likewise is called Aumī (Umā); the sixth is named Kailāsa; the seventh is called Vāyavīya — thus seven saṃhitās are recognised. ॥61॥
1.2.62: The divine Purāṇa named Śiva, with its seven saṃhitās, stands supreme, equal to Brahman, bestowing the state above all. ॥62॥
1.2.63: Whoever reverently recites this Śiva Purāṇa of seven saṃhitās in its entirety is called liberated while living. ॥63॥
1.2.64: Even hundreds of Śrutis, Smṛtis, Purāṇas, Itihāsas and Āgamas are not worth even a small fraction of this Śiva Purāṇa. ॥64॥
1.2.65: That spotless Śaiva Purāṇa, proclaimed by Śiva and compiled in brief by Vyāsa, devoted to Śiva, benefits the qualities of all beings, destroys the three afflictions, is incomparable, and indeed bestows auspiciousness on the good. ॥65॥
1.2.66: Here is sung the dharma free of deceit, the foremost, consisting of Vedāntic knowledge; here is the reality to be known by the wise whose hearts are free of envy; it is endowed with a host of well-arranged mantras and the three aims of life. ॥66॥
1.2.67: The Śaiva, the ornament of Purāṇas, is truly a genuine Purāṇa, in which the supreme reality shining in Vedānta and Veda is sung. Whoever reads or hears it with the utmost reverence becomes dear to Śambhu and indeed attains the supreme goal. ॥67॥
1.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The answer to the questions of the sages, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
1.3.1: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of Sūta, those supreme sages said: Recite to us the wondrous Purāṇa, which is the whole essence of Vedānta. ॥1॥
1.3.2: Hearing these words of the sages, Sūta, greatly delighted, remembering Śaṅkara, spoke to those best of sages. ॥2॥
1.3.3: Sūta said: Let all you sages, remembering Śiva the untroubled one, listen to the Śaiva Purāṇa, excellent among Purāṇas, born from the essence of the Vedas, ॥3॥
1.3.4: in which the triad of devotion, knowledge and detachment is lovingly sung, ॥4॥
1.3.5: and in which the true Reality, knowable through Vedānta, is especially described. ॥5॥
1.3.6: Let all you sages listen to the Purāṇa born of the essence of the Vedas. Long ago, after a great span of time, when kalpas had passed again and again, ॥6॥
1.3.7: when this present kalpa had arrived and the work of creation had begun, among the sages of the six lineages, as they spoke with one another, ॥7॥
1.3.8: a very great dispute arose: this is supreme; no, this is not. They went to Brahmā, the imperishable Ordainer, to ask him. ॥8॥
1.3.9: With folded hands, all of them spoke in words full of humility: You indeed are the sustainer of the whole world, the cause of all causes. ॥9॥
1.3.10: Who is the Person, ancient, beyond all principles, higher than the highest? Brahmā answered: That from which words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching it— ॥10॥
1.3.11: from whom all this, beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Indra, together with all the elements and senses, is first brought forth— ॥11॥
1.3.12: this God is Mahādeva, the all-knowing Lord of the world. He is seen only through supreme devotion, never in any other way. ॥12॥
1.3.13: Rudra, Hari and Hara, and likewise the other lords of the gods, constantly long to see him through supreme devotion. ॥13॥
1.3.14: What need is there to say much here? Through devotion to Śiva one is liberated. From grace comes devotion to the deity, and grace arises from devotion, just as here a seed comes from a sprout, or a sprout from a seed. ॥14॥
1.3.15: Therefore, O twice-born ones, to gain the Lord's grace, go to the earth and perform a long sacrificial session lasting a thousand years. ॥15॥
1.3.16: By the grace of that very Śiva, the Lord of sacrifice, the goal and the means—the essence of the knowledge taught in the Vedas—become known. ॥16॥
1.3.17: The sages said: Then what is the supreme goal, and what is the supreme means to it? What kind of person is the practitioner in this? Tell us this truly. ॥17॥
1.3.18: Brahmā said: The goal is attainment of Śiva's state; the means is service to him; the practitioner is one who, through his grace, is free from desire for the fruits of obligatory and other rites. ॥18॥
1.3.19: Having performed the action enjoined by the Veda, with its great fruit offered to him, one then attains the state of the Supreme Lord in the sequence of sālokya and the rest. ॥19॥
1.3.20: The supreme fruit comes to all according to their respective devotion. The means to it are of many kinds, taught directly by the Lord himself. ॥20॥
1.3.21: Summarizing, I shall tell you the essential means among them: hearing about him with the ear, and likewise praising him with speech, ॥21॥
1.3.22: and reflecting on him with the mind—this is called the great means. Maheśvara is to be heard of, to be praised, and to be reflected upon: ॥22॥
1.3.23: this scriptural statement is our authority. By this means, wholly devoted to this one means that accomplishes all aims, attain the supreme goal. ॥23॥
1.3.24: People engage in things they have seen directly with the eye; but what is not directly perceptible, everywhere, they act upon having known it through the ear. ॥24॥
1.3.25: Therefore the wise one should first take up hearing, listening from the mouth of the guru; then the intelligent one should accomplish the others, praising and reflection. ॥25॥
1.3.26: When this means has been well accomplished step by step up to reflection, union with Śiva arises through it gradually, in the sequence of sālokya and the rest. ॥26॥
1.3.27: Afterwards the ailments of all the limbs dissolve, and all worldly pleasure too dissolves. This path is indeed arduous in practice at first, but afterwards auspicious from beginning to end. ॥27॥
1.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named An inquiry into the goal and the means, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
1.4.1: The sages said: O Brahmā, what is reflection (manana) like, and what is hearing (śravaṇa) like? And how is his praise (kīrtana) done? Tell us this properly, each as it is. ॥1॥
1.4.2: Brahmā said: The constant purifying examination, by a mind that delights in reasoning, of his worship, of japa, and of the Lord's qualities, forms, sports and names — that is manana. It is attained through the Lord's gracious glance, and among all the excellent means it is the very foremost. ॥2॥
1.4.3: The clear and delightful praise of Śambhu's majesty, qualities, forms, sports and names, uttered with the voice — in the form of song, in Vedic words, or in ordinary speech — that is kīrtana; here it is the middle means. ॥3॥
1.4.4: When, by whatever means and wherever, a mass of words devoted to Śiva is fixed very firmly in the mind through the sense of hearing — as firmly as attention to amorous play with a woman — that, O wise ones, is śravaṇa, well known here in the world. ॥4॥
1.4.5: Through association with the good, hearing comes first; then praise of Paśupati, and that becomes firm; at its end comes reflection, which is the highest of all. Indeed everything comes about when Śaṅkara's glance falls upon one. ॥5॥
1.4.6: Sūta said: O lords among sages, concerning the greatness of this means I shall relate for your sake what happened long ago. Listen attentively. ॥6॥
1.4.7: Long ago my teacher Vyāsa, son of the sage Parāśara, troubled in mind, performed austerities on the auspicious bank of the Sarasvatī. ॥7॥
1.4.8: The blessed Sanatkumāra, travelling there by chance in an aerial car bright as the sun, saw my teacher. ॥8॥
1.4.9: He Vyāsa, who was absorbed in meditation, awoke and saw that son of Brahmā. Bowing down, the sage, flustered, spoke with great eagerness. ॥9॥
1.4.10: Having offered him water of welcome (arghya), he gave him a seat fit for a god. The lord, pleased, spoke in a deep voice to him as he stood bowing. ॥10॥
1.4.11: Sanatkumāra said: O sage, you should meditate on the true reality. That Śiva is within the range of direct realisation and is the helper here. For what purpose are you performing austerities? ॥11॥
1.4.12: Thus addressed by Kumāra, the sage told his intention: Dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, honoured in the Vedic path, ॥12॥
1.4.13: have been established by me in the world in many ways, likewise through your grace. Yet even for me, who am thus, a teacher in every respect, ॥13॥
1.4.14: the supremely wondrous knowledge that is the means to liberation does not arise. I perform austerity for the sake of liberation; I do not know the reason for that failure. ॥14॥
1.4.15: Thus entreated by the sage Vyāsa, the blessed and capable Kumāra, O best of brahmins, declared the definite cause of liberation: ॥15॥
1.4.16: Hearing, praising, and the still greater reflection on Śambhu — this triad is declared the means, and it is approved by the Veda. ॥16॥
1.4.17: Long ago I too, perplexed and bewildered about other means, performed austerities on the immovable mountain Mandara. ॥17॥
1.4.18: Then, by Śiva's command, the blessed Nandikeśvara arrived — that compassionate lord, witness of all, chief of the gaṇas. ॥18॥
1.4.19: He affectionately told me the supreme means to liberation: hearing, praising and reflecting on Śambhu, approved by the Veda. ॥19॥
1.4.20: This triad, the means to liberation, was told to me by Śiva. O brahmin, practise the triad beginning with hearing — so he said again and again. ॥20॥
1.4.21: Having thus spoken to Vyāsa, the son of Brahmā, with his attendants, then went in his own aerial car to his supremely splendid abode. ॥21॥
1.4.22: Thus the excellent ancient account has been told in brief. The sages said: O Sūta, you have declared the triad beginning with hearing as the means to liberation. ॥22॥
1.4.23: A person incapable of the triad beginning with hearing — by doing what is he liberated? By what action, by what cause, may liberation come even without effort? ॥23॥
1.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
1.5.1: Sūta said: One who is unable to practise the triad beginning with hearing (śravaṇa, kīrtana, manana) should install Śaṅkara's liṅga and image, worship them daily, and so cross the ocean of worldly existence. ॥1॥
1.5.2: He should indeed bring materials according to his means, without holding back, offer them for the sake of the liṅga and image, and worship continually. ॥2॥
1.5.3: A pavilion, a gateway tower, a sacred bathing place, a monastery, a sacred precinct, and likewise a festival; cloth, fragrance, garlands, incense and lamps, with devotion; ॥3॥
1.5.4: food offerings of various kinds with cakes and relishes; an umbrella, a banner, a fan and a chowrie with all their accessories — ॥4॥
1.5.5: all this he should provide for the liṅga and image, as in the services rendered to a king; likewise circumambulation, prostration and japa according to his capacity. ॥5॥
1.5.6: He should daily perform the rites from invocation to dismissal with deep devotion. Worshipping the god in this way in Śaṅkara's liṅga and image, ॥6॥
1.5.7: he attains perfection through Śiva's grace even without hearing and the rest. Great persons of old were liberated merely by worshipping the liṅga and image. ॥7॥
1.5.8: The sages said: Everywhere the hosts of deities are worshipped only in images; how is it that Śiva is everywhere worshipped in both the liṅga and the image? ॥8॥
1.5.9: Sūta said: Ah, lords of sages, this question is holy and most wondrous! The one to answer it is Mahādeva; there is no other being anywhere. ॥9॥
1.5.10: I shall tell in order what was spoken by Śiva, as heard from my teacher's mouth. Śiva alone, being of the nature of Brahman, is proclaimed as partless (niṣkala). ॥10॥
1.5.11: Likewise, because he has form, he is with parts (sakala); therefore he is both with and without parts. Because he is partless, the formless liṅga belongs to him; ॥11॥
1.5.12: and likewise, because he has parts, the image with form is appropriate to him. Being of a form both with and without parts, the Supreme is designated by the word Brahman. ॥12॥
1.5.13: So he is constantly worshipped by people in both the liṅga and the image. Since others than he are not Brahman, partlessness never belongs to them. ॥13॥
1.5.14: Therefore those lords of the gods are not worshipped in the partless liṅga; and likewise the other hosts of deities, because they are not Brahman and are individual souls (jīva), ॥14॥
1.5.15: are worshipped quietly only in images, since they possess only the form with parts. Individual-soul-hood belongs to those other than Śaṅkara, and Brahman-hood to Śaṅkara — ॥15॥
1.5.16: this is established as the essence of Vedānta, being revealed in the meaning of the praṇava (Oṃ). Just so, long ago, Nandikeśvara was asked on Mount Mandara ॥16॥
1.5.17: by the wise sage Sanatkumāra, son of Brahmā. Sanatkumāra said: For all those devoted to gods other than Śiva, everywhere, ॥17॥
1.5.18: only an image for worship has been heard of and seen many times; but in the worship of Śiva alone both liṅga and image are seen. ॥18॥
1.5.19: Therefore, O auspicious one, tell me that truth, which gives right understanding. Nandikeśvara said: This question is unsurpassed, a secret, marked by the nature of Brahman; ॥19॥
1.5.20: I shall tell you, O sinless one, endowed with devotion, what was spoken by Śiva. Because Śiva is of the form of Brahman and is partless, the partless ॥20॥
1.5.21: liṅga is approved in all the Vedas for his worship alone. And because he alone also has parts, so he is both with and without parts; ॥21॥
1.5.22: and likewise the image with parts is accepted by the world for worship. As for those other than Śiva, because they are individual souls and in every way have parts, ॥22॥
1.5.23: only the image is approved for their worship in the Vedic determination. Indeed, when the gods manifest themselves, their form is only one with parts; ॥23॥
1.5.24: but in Śiva's manifestation both liṅga and image are indeed seen. Sanatkumāra said: O illustrious one, you have explained the use of liṅga and image, ॥24॥
1.5.25: distinguishing, in truth, that of Śiva and that of the others. Hence that supreme liṅga, arising before images and the rest — ॥25॥
1.5.26: O lord of yogins, I wish to hear the account of the manifestation of the liṅga. Nandikeśvara said: Listen, child; out of affection for you I shall tell it as it truly is. ॥26॥
1.5.27: Long ago, in a former kalpa, when the great age renowned in the worlds had arrived, the two great-souled ones, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, fought with each other. ॥27॥
1.5.28: To dispel their pride, the Supreme Lord revealed his own nature between them in the form of a partless pillar. ॥28॥
1.5.29: Then, since the pillar bore the mark of his liṅga, Śiva, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds, showed from the pillar his own partless liṅga. ॥29॥
1.5.30: From that time on in the worlds, the partless liṅga of the Lord, and likewise the image with parts, were ordained for Śiva alone. ॥30॥
1.5.31: For gods other than Śiva only an image was ordained. The image of each of those gods is auspicious and grants its respective enjoyments; but Śiva's worship as liṅga and image is auspicious and grants both enjoyment and liberation. ॥31॥
1.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The glory of Śiva's liṅga, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
1.6.1: Nandīśvara said: Long ago, once, O lord of yogins, Viṣṇu, whose couch is the serpent, lay asleep in supreme splendour, surrounded by his own attendants. ॥1॥
1.6.2: Brahmā, foremost among the knowers of Brahman, having come there by chance, asked the lotus-eyed one, who was lying there, all-beautiful: ॥2॥
1.6.3: Who are you, lying there like an ordinary man, arrogantly, even after seeing me? Get up, child, look at me—your lord, who has come here. ॥3॥
1.6.4: For the deluded, hostile one who, seeing a venerable elder who has arrived, behaves arrogantly, an expiation is prescribed. ॥4॥
1.6.5: Hearing these words, Viṣṇu, angry yet outwardly behaving calmly, said: Welcome to you, good health to you, child. Stay; come here and take a seat. ॥5॥
1.6.6: Why does your face look as if agitated, with eyes askew? Brahmā said: Child Viṣṇu, know me as the one of great dignity, who has come through the course of time, ॥6॥
1.6.7: the grandfather of the world and your protector too, little child. Viṣṇu said: This world rests in me, child; yet you, like a thief, think it yours. ॥7॥
1.6.8: You are a son born from the lotus of my navel; you speak in vain. Nandikeśvara said: As the two deluded unborn ones were speaking thus there, ॥8॥
1.6.9: I alone am supreme, not you; I am the lord, I am the lord — each wishing to kill the other, they made ready for battle. ॥9॥
1.6.10: The two heroic immortals, whose mounts were the swan and the king of birds Garuḍa, fought; and likewise the followers of Brahmā and of Viṣṇu then fought one another. ॥10॥
1.6.11: Meanwhile all the classes of gods, travelling in aerial cars, assembled, eager to see that most wondrous battle, ॥11॥
1.6.12: showering flowers and watching freely from the sky. There the one whose mount is Suparṇa Viṣṇu, enraged, at Brahmā's chest ॥12॥
1.6.13: released unbearable arrows and many weapons of various kinds. Then Vidhi Brahmā, enraged, released at Viṣṇu's chest unbearable ॥13॥
1.6.14: arrows resembling fire, and weapons in great numbers. Then, clearly seeing that wonder taking place in the battle between the two, ॥14॥
1.6.15: the hosts of gods, greatly agitated, praised it. Then Viṣṇu, exceedingly enraged, breathing hard, worn down by distress, ॥15॥
1.6.16: the wise one fitted the Māheśvara missile against Brahmā. Then Brahmā, greatly enraged, making the whole universe tremble, ॥16॥
1.6.17: fitted the terrible Pāśupata missile against Viṣṇu's chest. Then it rose up in the sky, like ten thousand suns, ॥17॥
1.6.18: thousand-mouthed, extremely fierce, frightful like a violent storm—this pair of missiles of Brahmā and Viṣṇu there was terrifying. ॥18॥
1.6.19: Thus the battle between Brahmā and Viṣṇu took place. Then all the hosts of gods, dejected and greatly agitated, spoke to one another, dear one, as brāhmaṇas do when the king is in turmoil. ॥19॥
1.6.20: To him from whom creation, preservation, destruction, concealment and grace proceed—to that Brahman, the trident-bearer, we bow. ॥20॥
1.6.21: He without whose grace even the destruction of a blade of grass here is impossible for others, anywhere, of their own will. ॥21॥
1.6.22: Thus, seized by fear, the gods, searching for Śiva's abode, went to the peak of Kailāsa, where the moon-crested one dwells. ॥22॥
1.6.23: Seeing thus that abode of the Supreme Lord, the immortals rejoiced; they bowed to it, shaped like the Praṇava Oṃ, and entered that dwelling. ॥23॥
1.6.24: There, in the midst of the assembly, in the pavilion, upon a jewelled seat, they beheld the foremost of gods shining together with Umā, ॥24॥
1.6.25: with his left foot placed over the other, his lotus-hand resting upon it, attended on all sides by his own gaṇas, marked with every auspicious sign, ॥25॥
1.6.26: being fanned by skilled women of intense devotion, ever praised by the Vedas—the Lord, bestowing grace. ॥26॥
1.6.27: Seeing the Lord thus, the immortals, their eyes wet with tears of joy, together with the great gaṇas, prostrated like a staff from afar, dear one. ॥27॥
1.6.28: Seeing those gods, the Lord summoned them near through his gaṇas. Then the god, crest-jewel of the gods, gladdening the gods, spoke words deep, sweet and auspicious. ॥28॥
1.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The journey of the gods to Kailāsa, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
1.7.1: Īśvara said: Dear children, is all well with you? Under my command, are the world and the race of gods continuing in their own duties, or not? ॥1॥
1.7.2: O gods, the battle of Brahmā and Viṣṇu was already known to me; yet because of your distress it has been told to me again and again. ॥2॥
1.7.3: Thus, O Kumāra, with smiling, sweet speech, he, the husband of Ambā, gladdened that host of gods. ॥3॥
1.7.4: Then the overlord of Hari and Brahmā, intending to go to the battlefield, commanded a hundred chiefs of the gaṇas right there in the assembly. ॥4॥
1.7.5: Then there arose music of many kinds for the departure of the supreme Lord, and the lords of the gaṇas stood equipped, with various vehicles and ornaments. ॥5॥
1.7.6: The Lord, husband of Ambikā, mounted the auspicious chariot shaped like the praṇava (Oṃ), complete from beginning to end, adorned with five circles. All the gods, Indra and the others, followed him along with his sons and gaṇas. ॥6॥
1.7.7: Honoured with multitudes of bright banners, fans, chowries, showers of flowers, songs and dances, and with bands of musical instruments, Paśupati, together with the supreme Goddess, went with his army to the battlefield of those two. ॥7॥
1.7.8: Having observed their battle, he stationed himself, hidden, in the sky, the sound of the instruments ended and the din of the great hosts stilled. ॥8॥
1.7.9: Then the two heroes Brahmā and Acyuta, desiring to kill each other, fought with the Māheśvara weapon and likewise with the Pāśupata. ॥9॥
1.7.10: Then, by the flames of the weapons of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, the three worlds were burnt. The Lord too, having seen that untimely dissolution, grew intensely... ॥10॥
1.7.11: ...he, the partless one, took on a terrifying form like a great pillar of fire in the ground between them. ॥11॥
1.7.12: And those two weapons, flaming and capable of destroying the worlds, fell down in a single instant when the great fire appeared. ॥12॥
1.7.13: Having seen that wondrous, strange, auspicious sight that quelled the weapons, they said to one another, what is this of wondrous form? ॥13॥
1.7.14: What is this pillar, beyond the senses and in the form of fire, that has arisen? Its top and its bottom must indeed be our goal to discover. ॥14॥
1.7.15: Thus resolved, the two heroes, proud of their valour, joined together and, intent on it, quickly set out to investigate it. ॥15॥
1.7.16: If we two stay together, the single task cannot be accomplished there. Having said this, Viṣṇu, in the body of a boar, went towards its base. ॥16॥
1.7.17: Likewise Brahmā, in the body of a swan, went to see its end. Hari, having pierced through the realm of Pātāla and gone very far, ॥17॥
1.7.18: did not see the base of that pillar of fiery splendour. Exhausted, that boar-Hari returned to the former battlefield. ॥18॥
1.7.19: Then, dear child, Vidhi, your father, travelling through the sky, saw a wondrous ketakī flower that had fallen somewhat, ॥19॥
1.7.20: exceedingly fragrant and unwithered, though it had been falling for many years. And having observed the doings of those two, the blessed Supreme Lord ॥20॥
1.7.21: laughed in jest; from the shaking his head moved, and from it the excellent ketaka fell, in order to show favour to those two. ॥21॥
1.7.22: Brahmā asked: Why are you falling, O lord of flowers? King of flowers, by whom were you held? The flower replied: I have been falling for a long time from the middle of the pillar of the primeval, immeasurable one. ॥22॥
1.7.23: I do not see its end; therefore give up hope of seeing the end. Brahmā said: I have come here in the form of a swan for the sake of reaching its end. ॥23॥
1.7.24: From now on, friend, you must today do what I desire: together with me you must say this in the presence of Viṣṇu: ॥24॥
1.7.25: The end of the pillar was seen by the Creator; I am the witness to that, O Acyuta. Having said this, he bowed to the ketaka there again and again. Even untruth is approved in a time of distress — such is the precept. ॥25॥
1.7.26: Seeing Acyuta there, long wearied and with his joy gone, he danced for joy; and then that Vidhi, having taken up false, unmanly speech, spoke to Acyuta as though it were the truth: ॥26॥
1.7.27: The top of this pillar has been seen, O Hari; and this ketaka here is surely the witness to it. Then the ketaka falsely said there, in his presence, it is so, confirming the Creator's words. ॥27॥
1.7.28: And Hari, thinking it to be true, himself paid homage to Vidhi, and worshipped that Vidhi with the sixteen offerings. ॥28॥
1.7.29: To punish the deceitful Vidhi, the Lord there emerged with a form from the fiery liṅga. Then Viṣṇu, rising up at the sight of the Master, with trembling hands clasped his feet and said: ॥29॥
1.7.30: Regarding you, whose body has neither beginning nor end, great inquiry born of desire, pursued with a deluded mind, does not save one here. So be gracious, O mine of compassion; forgive our fault and let it be wiped away — it was brought about by you yourself in play. ॥30॥
1.7.31: Īśvara said: Child Hari, I am pleased, since you, though desiring lordship, spoke truthful words. Therefore among people you shall have equality with me, and honour too has been obtained by you. ॥31॥
1.7.32: From now on, for you as a separate self, there shall be establishment of sacred sites, festivals, and worship. ॥32॥
1.7.33: Thus long ago the God, greatly pleased by his truthfulness, granted Hari supreme equality with himself, while the host of gods looked on. ॥33॥
1.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The appearance of the pillar of fire, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
1.8.1: Nandīśvara said: Then Mahādeva created, from between his brows, a certain wondrous being called Bhairava, with the intent of destroying Brahmā's pride. ॥1॥
1.8.2: Then, there in the courtyard, having bowed to his lord Śiva, he said: What task shall I do here? Command me quickly, O Lord. ॥2॥
1.8.3: Śiva said: Child, this Vidhi Brahmā here, who is in person the primal deity of the worlds — surely worship him, the supreme one, swiftly with a sharp sword. ॥3॥
1.8.4: He, seizing with one hand the hair of that fifth head — arrogant and speaking falsehood — cut off the head and was ready to kill him, brandishing the sword conspicuously in his hands. ॥4॥
1.8.5: Your father, his ornaments, garments, garland, upper cloth and mass of clean hair all fallen away, trembling like a plantain tree in the wind or like a creeper, fell at Bhairava's lotus feet. ॥5॥
1.8.6: Meanwhile, dear one, the compassionate Acyuta, wishing to see Vidhi safe, bathed the tender feet of our lord with tears and, with joined palms, spoke in sweet faltering syllables, as a child to his own father. ॥6॥
1.8.7: Acyuta said: O Lord, since it was you who formerly, with care, gave him this five-faced mark, therefore forgive him; he deserves grace today — show favour to this Vidhi. ॥7॥
1.8.8: Thus entreated by Acyuta, the Lord, pleased, in the courtyard thronged by the hosts of gods, then restrained Bhairava from punishing Brahmā. ॥8॥
1.8.9: Then the god said to the cheat Vidhi, whose fifth head was gone: O Brahmā, craving worship, you assumed lordship by deceit. ॥9॥
1.8.10: Therefore may there be no honour for you in the world — no shrines, festivals and the like. Brahmā said: Master, be gracious today, O one of great glory; I regard the sparing of my remaining heads as a boon. ॥10॥
1.8.11: Salutation to you, the Blessed One, the kinsman of all, source of the universe, forbearing of faults, Śambhu, whose bow is a mountain. ॥11॥
1.8.12: Īśvara said: Without fear of a ruler this whole world will perish. Therefore you, child, strike down those deserving punishment and bear the burden of the world. ॥12॥
1.8.13: I grant you a boon in this; accept it, rare and supreme: in śrauta and domestic rites and in sacrifices you shall be the presiding priest. ॥13॥
1.8.14: Without you a sacrifice, even complete with its subsidiary parts and fees, is fruitless. Then the god spoke to the cheat Ketaka, the false witness: ॥14॥
1.8.15: O Ketaka, you are wicked. Deceiver, go far from here. From now on let there be no love of mine for your flower in worship. ॥15॥
1.8.16: When the god had said this, all the classes of gods then drove Ketaka away from his side to elsewhere. ॥16॥
1.8.17: The ketaka flower said: Salutation to you, Lord. By your command my birth has become fruitless. Let it be made fruitful, father; let my sin be forgiven. ॥17॥
1.8.18: Remembrance of you destroys sin committed knowingly or unknowingly. Now that I have seen such a one as you, how could the fault of falsehood remain in me? ॥18॥
1.8.19: Thus praised by Ketaka in the assembly hall, the Lord said: It is not proper for me to wear you; I, the Lord, am truthful of speech. ॥19॥
1.8.20: My own devotees will wear you; thereby your birth will be fruitful. And you shall be above me in the form of a canopy. ॥20॥
1.8.21: Having thus shown grace to Ketaka, Vidhi and Mādhava, the Lord shone in the midst of the assembly, praised by all the gods. ॥21॥
1.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named Śiva's grace, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
1.9.1: Nandīśvara said: Meanwhile the two, Vidhi (Brahmā) and Mādhava (Viṣṇu), bowed to the Lord and stood silent with palms joined in reverence, one on his right and one on his left. ॥1॥
1.9.2: There, having seated the god together with his family on an excellent seat, the two worshipped the worshipful one with holy articles of the puruṣa kind. ॥2॥
1.9.3: A pauruṣa article and a prākṛta article should be understood as long-lasting and short-lasting respectively. With necklaces, anklets, armlets, crowns and jewelled earrings, ॥3॥
1.9.4: with sacred threads, upper garments, garlands, silk cloths, wreaths and rings; with flowers, betel, camphor, and unguents of sandal and aguru, ॥4॥
1.9.5: with incense, lamps, white umbrellas, fans, banners and chowries, and with other divine offerings whose splendour is beyond speech and mind, ॥5॥
1.9.6: with things fit for the Lord and unattainable by bound souls (paśu), the two worshipped the Lord (Pati). Whatever most excellent article was fit for the Lord, O Hitadhvaja, ॥6॥
1.9.7: all those articles the Lord, delighted, wishing to establish a tradition, gave away there to the members of the assembly, separately and in due order. ॥7॥
1.9.8: A great clamour arose there: Let this article be taken. There itself Śaṅkara, earlier worshipped by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, ॥8॥
1.9.9: pleased, the increaser of devotion smilingly spoke to the two, who were bowing humbly. The Lord said: I am pleased with you today, dear children, by your worship on this great day. ॥9॥
1.9.10: Therefore this day will become supremely holy. This lunar day, famed as Śivarātri, is dear to me. ॥10॥
1.9.11: Whoever performs worship of my liṅga and my image at this time, that man would, as it were, perform the work of the world—maintenance, creation and the rest. ॥11॥
1.9.12: On Śivarātri, fasting day and night, with senses subdued, one should worship according to rule and according to one's strength, without deceit. ॥12॥
1.9.13: The fruit that comes from worshipping me continuously for one year—that fruit one obtains at once by worshipping me on Śivarātri. ॥13॥
1.9.14: This is the time for the growth of my dharma, like the moon's time for the ocean; in it should be held my festival of installation and the like, a home of auspiciousness. ॥14॥
1.9.15: Moreover, the time when I formerly manifested myself in the form of a pillar—that time, O children, is in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa under the asterism Ārdrā. ॥15॥
1.9.16: Whoever, on Ārdrā in Mārgaśīrṣa, sees me as the companion of Umā, or even my image or liṅga, is dearer to me than even Guha. ॥16॥
1.9.17: On that auspicious day the fruit from mere sight is ample; if there is worship, the fruit is greater still, beyond the reach of words. ॥17॥
1.9.18: Since on this battlefield I expanded in the body of a liṅga, like a liṅga, therefore this shall be the place of the liṅga. ॥18॥
1.9.19: This pillar without beginning or end will become small in size, for the worlds to see it and to worship it, O dear sons. ॥19॥
1.9.20: This liṅga brings enjoyment and is the sole means to worldly enjoyment and liberation; through seeing, touching and meditating on it, creatures are released from birth. ॥20॥
1.9.21: Since this liṅga rose up resembling a mountain of fire, it will gain fame as Aruṇācala. ॥21॥
1.9.22: Here there will be many great holy places, and here too creatures will obtain liberation by residing and by dying. ॥22॥
1.9.23: There will be auspicious events such as chariot festivals and habitations of people all around. Whatever is given, offered in fire, or recited here will become ten-million-fold. ॥23॥
1.9.24: This sacred field is greater than all my other sacred fields. Here embodied beings attain liberation by mere remembrance. ॥24॥
1.9.25: Therefore this sacred field is greater, exceedingly beautiful, full of every auspiciousness, auspicious, and the bestower of liberation on all. ॥25॥
1.9.26: By worshipping here me alone, the Lord who abides in the liṅga, within the liṅga, one attains sālokya (same world), sāmīpya (proximity), sārūpya (same form), sārṣṭi (equal power), ॥26॥
1.9.27: and sāyujya (union)—these five are held to be the fruits of ritual action and the rest. All of you will swiftly obtain your every desire. ॥27॥
1.9.28: Nandikeśvara said: Having thus blessed the humble Vidhi and Mādhava, the Lord—the armies of the two which had earlier struck each other down in battle— ॥28॥
1.9.29: those he fully revived by a stream of nectar, his own power. And to remove their delusion and enmity he spoke to the two: ॥29॥
1.9.30: I have two forms, with parts (sakala) and without parts (niṣkala). No one else has them; therefore all others are not Lord. ॥30॥
1.9.31: First in the form of a pillar, and afterwards in embodied form, O children: the partless is declared to be Brahman-hood, and the form with parts likewise Lordship. ॥31॥
1.9.32: Both are established in me alone, not in anyone other than me. Therefore Lordship belongs nowhere to others, not even to you two. ॥32॥
1.9.33: Through ignorance of this, your most astonishing pride of lordship arose; to dispel it I thus rose up here on the battlefield. ॥33॥
1.9.34: Abandon your own pride and fix your mind on me, the Lord. By my grace every object in the worlds becomes manifest. ॥34॥
1.9.35: In that, the teacher's word is what reveals, or is the authority, again and again. Out of affection for you I declare this hidden truth of Brahman. ॥35॥
1.9.36: I alone am the supreme Brahman; my nature is both with parts and without parts. Because of being Brahman I am also Īśvara; my functions are grace and the rest. ॥36॥
1.9.37: Because of vastness (bṛhattva) and expanding (bṛṃhaṇatva) I am Brahman, O Brahmā and Keśava; likewise, because of sameness and all-pervasiveness I am the Self (Ātman), O children. ॥37॥
1.9.38: All others are not the Self; they are only individual souls (jīva), without doubt. And the fivefold work of the world, beginning with grace and ending with creation, ॥38॥
1.9.39: is always mine, by virtue of my Lordship, and not anyone else's. In the beginning, the partless liṅga rose up so that my Brahman-hood might be understood. ॥39॥
1.9.40: Then, to make clearly manifest to you the Lordship that was unknown to you, I at once became embodied (sakala), the Lord in person. ॥40॥
1.9.41: Therefore my lordship (Īśa-hood) should quickly be understood as my embodied (sakala) aspect, while this formless (niṣkala) pillar makes known my Brahman-nature. ॥41॥
1.9.42: Because it possesses the characteristics of a liṅga (mark), this shall be my liṅga. Therefore, dear sons, this should be worshipped by you two here constantly. ॥42॥
1.9.43: This is ever of my very nature and the means of my presence. It is always to be greatly worshipped, because there is no difference between the liṅga and the one it signifies (the liṅgin). ॥43॥
1.9.44: Wherever and by whomever such a liṅga of mine is installed, there I myself am installed, though I am in truth beyond installation, O dear children. ॥44॥
1.9.45: Equality with me is declared to be the fruit of installing one liṅga; when a second liṅga is installed, the fruit is indeed oneness with me. ॥45॥
1.9.46: The liṅga is to be installed as the principal object of worship, while the image (bera) is secondary. Where there is no liṅga, that place is not a sacred site, even if it has images on all sides. ॥46॥
1.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The naming of Śiva as Maheśvara, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
1.10.1: Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: O Lord, tell us the defining nature of the five tasks beginning with creation. Śiva said: Out of compassion I shall explain to you both the secret teaching about my tasks. ॥1॥
1.10.2: Creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment and grace — these five alone are my eternally established tasks concerning the world, O Aja (Brahmā) and Acyuta (Viṣṇu). ॥2॥
1.10.3: Creation is the setting in motion of saṃsāra; its establishment is considered maintenance. Dissolution is its crushing; concealment is its removal. ॥3॥
1.10.4: Liberation from it is grace. Thus indeed my task is fivefold. Another carries this task silently, like the figure on a gateway tower. ॥4॥
1.10.5: The four tasks beginning with creation are the unfolding of saṃsāra; the fifth is indeed the cause of liberation, and it is ever firmly established in me. ॥5॥
1.10.6: This is seen by my people in the five elements: creation in earth, maintenance in water, and likewise dissolution in fire, ॥6॥
1.10.7: concealment in wind, and similarly grace here in space. Everything is produced by earth; everything grows by waters; ॥7॥
1.10.8: everything is consumed by fire and carried away by wind; everything is graced by space. Thus indeed should it be understood by the wise. ॥8॥
1.10.9: To carry out these five tasks I have a set of five faces: four faces in the four directions and a fifth face in their middle. ॥9॥
1.10.10: O sons, you two obtained through austerity these two tasks called creation and maintenance — a very dear good fortune — from me, who was pleased. ॥10॥
1.10.11: Likewise the other pair of tasks was obtained by Rudra and Maheśa; but the supreme one called grace cannot be obtained by anyone at all. ॥11॥
1.10.12: All that former deed has been forgotten by you two through time; such a deed has not been forgotten by Rudra and Maheśa. ॥12॥
1.10.13: Therefore, for that reason, I have granted them equality with me in form, attire, task, vehicle, seat, weapons and the like. ॥13॥
1.10.14: O dear ones, through lack of meditation on me this delusion has come upon you two. When there is knowledge of me, there would not be such pride, even having a form like Maheśa's. ॥14॥
1.10.15: Therefore, for the attainment of knowledge of me, from now on repeat my mantra named Oṃkāra, which breaks pride. ॥15॥
1.10.16: I have taught you my own mantra, the greatly auspicious Oṃkāra. The Oṃkāra arose first from my mouth, revealing me. ॥16॥
1.10.17: This is the signifier, I am the signified; this mantra is indeed of my very nature. Its constant remembrance would be constant remembrance of me. ॥17॥
1.10.18: First the syllable a arose from the northern face, u from the western face, m from the southern face, and likewise the bindu from the eastern face, ॥18॥
1.10.19: and the nāda from the middle face. Thus it unfolded fivefold; then, becoming unified again in the same way, it became the single syllable Oṃ. ॥19॥
1.10.20: Everything consisting of name and form — the two groups of Veda (words) and beings — is pervaded by this mantra; and it reveals Śiva and Śakti. ॥20॥
1.10.21: From this was born the five-syllabled mantra, which reveals all — in the order of a and the rest, its syllables beginning with na in due sequence. ॥21॥
1.10.22: From this five-syllabled mantra arose the mātṛkās (the letters of the alphabet) in five divisions; from that, from the head and the four faces, arose the three-footed Gāyatrī. ॥22॥
1.10.23: From that the whole Veda was born, and from that indeed crores of mantras. By each particular mantra comes its particular accomplishment; from this Oṃkāra comes every accomplishment. ॥23॥
1.10.24: By this root of mantras both enjoyment and liberation are accomplished. All the other auspicious royal mantras directly grant enjoyment. ॥24॥
1.10.25: Nandīśvara said: Then there the Guru, together with Ambikā, having arranged a screen for the two of them, and gently placing his lotus-hand on their heads as they sat facing north, imparted the supreme mantra. ॥25॥
1.10.26: The mantra having been uttered three times, each received the mantra along with the explanation of yantra and tantra; and the two disciples offered themselves as the teacher's fee. ॥26॥
1.10.27: With joined hands, standing near him, the two of them spoke to him, the best of gods, the Guru of the world. ॥27॥
1.10.28: Brahmā and Acyuta said: Salutation to the one whose form is without parts; salutation to the one whose radiance is without parts; salutation to the Lord of all; salutation to you, the Self of all. ॥28॥
1.10.29: Salutation to the one signified by the Praṇava; salutation to the one whose emblem is the Praṇava; salutation to the maker of creation and the rest; salutation to you, the five-faced one. ॥29॥
1.10.30: Salutation to you, whose nature is the five Brahmans, who perform the five tasks; to you, the Self, Brahman, whose power consists of endless qualities; ॥30॥
1.10.31: salutation to Śambhu, the Guru, whose form is both with parts and without parts. Having thus praised the Guru with verses, Brahmā and Viṣṇu bowed down. ॥31॥
1.10.32: Īśvara said: O dear children, the whole truth has been told and shown to you both. Repeat the Praṇava mantra, taught by the Goddess, which is of my very nature. ॥32॥
1.10.33: Knowledge becomes firmly established, and all good fortune becomes everlasting. Repetition of it on the fourteenth lunar day when the asterism is Ārdrā becomes inexhaustible in merit. ॥33॥
1.10.34: On the Mahārdrā, determined by the sun's course, a single repetition becomes a crore-fold. The last part of Mṛgaśīrṣa and likewise the first part of Punarvasu ॥34॥
1.10.35: should always be known as equal to Ārdrā for worship, fire-offering, libations and the like. The viewing of the deity is best at dawn, in the early-morning and saṅgava (forenoon) periods. ॥35॥
1.10.36: Likewise the fourteenth lunar day to be adopted should be one that extends through midnight; one extending through the evening twilight (pradoṣa), joined with the following day, is also commended. ॥36॥
1.10.37: The liṅga and the image are equal for me; yet for worshippers the liṅga is superior. Therefore those seeking liberation should worship the liṅga as higher even than the image. ॥37॥
1.10.38: The liṅga should be installed with the Oṃkāra mantra, and the image with the five-syllabled mantra, with good materials, by oneself or even by others. ॥38॥
1.10.39: One should worship with the ritual offerings; then my abode becomes easy to attain. Having thus instructed the two disciples, Śiva vanished right there. ॥39॥
1.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The teaching of Oṃkāra, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
1.11.1: The sages said: How should the liṅga be installed, and what are its characteristics? And how, at what place and time, and by whom, should it be worshipped? ॥1॥
1.11.2: Sūta said: For your sake I shall explain; let it be understood attentively. At a favourable, auspicious time, at a holy sacred place or on a riverbank, ॥2॥
1.11.3: a liṅga should be set up as one wishes, where there may be daily worship, made of earth, of water-born substance, or of fiery metal, according to one's liking. ॥3॥
1.11.4: A liṅga endowed with the marks prescribed in the ritual manuals obtains the fruit of worship; one endowed with all the marks gives the fruit of worship immediately. ॥4॥
1.11.5: For a movable liṅga a small one is preferred; for a fixed one, a large one indeed. One should install a liṅga fashioned for Śiva, with the proper marks and with a pedestal. ॥5॥
1.11.6: The liṅga pedestal—circular, square, or else triangular—narrow in the middle like the leg of a bedstead (khaṭvāṅga), yields great fruit. ॥6॥
1.11.7: First, the liṅga is made from clay, stone and the like, or made of metals and the like. For a fixed liṅga, the pedestal made of the same material as the liṅga is preferred. ॥7॥
1.11.8: In a movable liṅga, liṅga and pedestal are one piece, except for the bāṇa-liṅga. The best measure of a liṅga is twelve finger-breadths of the maker. ॥8॥
1.11.9: If it is smaller, the fruit will be small; larger is not faulty at all. For a movable one too, likewise, it should be one finger-breadth of the maker less. ॥9॥
1.11.10: First a temple (vimāna) adorned with hosts of deities should be built by craftsmanship; there, in a sanctum that is beautiful, firm, and gleaming like a mirror, ॥10॥
1.11.11: adorned with the nine gems, with doors in the cardinal directions and a principal door—the nine gems being sapphire, ruby, cat's-eye, dark-blue stone, emerald, ॥11॥
1.11.12: pearl, coral, gomeda and diamond—these are the nine gems. In the centre is placed the liṅga; one should deposit precious substances along with the Vedic rites. ॥12॥
1.11.13: Having worshipped the liṅga with the mantras beginning with Sadyojāta in the five places in due order, and having offered oblations of ghee in many ways into the fire to me together with my retinue, ॥13॥
1.11.14: having honoured the guru and the preceptor with wealth, and kinsmen with desired things, one should give riches to supplicants, both inanimate and animate gifts. ॥14॥
1.11.15: Having carefully satisfied every living being, stationary and moving, in a pit filled with gold and filled with the nine gems, ॥15॥
1.11.16: having uttered the Brahma mantras beginning with Sadyojāta, having meditated on the supreme auspicious god, and having pronounced the great mantra Oṃ resounding with nāda, ॥16॥
1.11.17: having installed the liṅga there, one should join the liṅga to the pedestal; having set the liṅga with its pedestal, one should fix it with permanent cement. ॥17॥
1.11.18: In the same way a supremely auspicious image (vera) should be installed right there, with the five-syllable mantra; and likewise an image for festivals outside. ॥18॥
1.11.19: One should receive the image from gurus, or one worshipped by holy men. Thus worship of the liṅga and of the image grants the abode of Śiva. ॥19॥
1.11.20: Again, the liṅga is said to be of two kinds, stationary and moving. They call trees, shrubs and the like the stationary liṅga; ॥20॥
1.11.21: they call worms, insects and the like the moving liṅga. Tending the stationary and satisfying the moving— ॥21॥
1.11.22: with delight in the well-being of each, the wise know this as worship of Śiva. The whole pedestal is of the nature of the Mother (Ambā), and the Śiva-liṅga is of the nature of consciousness. ॥22॥
1.11.23: Just as Śaṅkara abides holding the goddess Umā on his lap, so this liṅga abides constantly, holding the pedestal. ॥23॥
1.11.24: Having thus installed the great liṅga, one should worship it with the services; there should be daily worship according to one's ability, and likewise the setting up of banners and the like. ॥24॥
1.11.25: In this way one should install the liṅga, which directly grants the abode of Śiva. Or else a movable liṅga, with the sixteen services, ॥25॥
1.11.26: one should worship according to rule; it gradually grants the abode of Śiva. The services are: invocation, seat, arghya-water and foot-water likewise, ॥26॥
1.11.27: sipping water as part of that, bath preceded by anointing with oil, garment, fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, food-offering, ॥27॥
1.11.28: waving of lights, betel, obeisance and dismissal. Or else, having performed the services from arghya up to the food-offering according to rule, ॥28॥
1.11.29: or else one should always perform, according to ability, ablution, food-offering, obeisance and libation; it gradually grants the abode of Śiva. ॥29॥
1.11.30: Or else, at a liṅga installed by men, by sages, by gods, or self-manifested, or at a newly installed liṅga, with services in whatever way one can, ॥30॥
1.11.31: when articles of worship are given, one obtains some fruit; with circumambulations and obeisances, it gradually grants the abode of Śiva. ॥31॥
1.11.32: Or merely seeing the liṅga as a regular observance grants Śiva's state. With clay, flour, cow-dung, flowers, karavīra, or fruits, ॥32॥
1.11.33: with jaggery, fresh butter, sacred ash, or grains, as one likes—having carefully made a liṅga, one should then worship it accordingly. ॥33॥
1.11.34: Some likewise prefer worship on the thumb and the like. In the rites of the liṅga there is never any prohibition anywhere. ॥34॥
1.11.35: For Śiva everywhere gives fruit in proportion to the effort. Or else the gift of a liṅga, or even the price of a liṅga, ॥35॥
1.11.36: given with faith to a devotee of Śiva, grants the abode of Śiva. Or else one should daily repeat the praṇava ten thousand times, ॥36॥
1.11.37: or a thousand times at the two twilights; this should be known as granting the abode of Śiva. At the time of japa, the praṇava ending in m purifies the mind. ॥37॥
1.11.38: In meditative absorption mental repetition is prescribed; whispered repetition is for all times. This they know as the even praṇava, joined with bindu and nāda. ॥38॥
1.11.39: Or one should daily repeat the five-syllable mantra ten thousand times with reverence, or a thousand times at the two twilights; this should be known as granting the abode of Śiva. ॥39॥
1.11.40: For brāhmaṇas, the mantra joined with the praṇava at the beginning is preferred. And to obtain the fruit, the mantra should be received from a guru together with initiation. ॥40॥
1.11.41: For the pot-bath (kumbha-snāna), mantra initiation and also mātṛkā-nyāsa, a brāhmaṇa guru who is wise and whose self is purified by truth is preferred. ॥41॥
1.11.42: For the twice-born the mantra is recited with namaḥ first; for others, ending with namaḥ. For women too, some prefer it ending with namaḥ, according to rule. ॥42॥
1.11.43: For brāhmaṇa women, some prefer this with namaḥ first. Having performed japa of five crores, one becomes equal to Sadāśiva. ॥43॥
1.11.44: By one, two, three or four crores one reaches the abode of Brahmā and the others. Or one should repeat a lakh for each syllable, separately for each syllable. ॥44॥
1.11.45: Or else, a lakh per syllable should be known as granting Śiva's abode. A thousand thousands of repetitions over a thousand days— ॥45॥
1.11.46: —by such japa of the mantra, together with daily feeding of brāhmaṇas, comes the attainment of what one desires. A thousand and eight Gāyatrīs, in the morning indeed, ॥46॥
1.11.47: a brāhmaṇa should repeat daily—the Gāyatrī which in due course grants Śiva's abode. Keeping to discipline, he should also repeat Vedic mantras and hymns (sūktas). ॥47॥
1.11.48: The ten-syllabled mantra is to be repeated one time, or a hundred less one, or more than that; ten thousand, a thousand, or a hundred less one may be the count. ॥48॥
1.11.49: Recitation of the entire Veda (veda-pārāyaṇa) too should be known as granting Śiva's abode. Other, more numerous mantras one should repeat at a lakh per syllable. ॥49॥
1.11.50: Likewise monosyllabic mantras one should repeat at a crore per syllable. Beyond that one should also repeat a thousand more with devotion. ॥50॥
1.11.51: Thus one should act according to one's capacity; in due course one attains Śiva's abode. Daily, one single mantra that one likes, until death, ॥51॥
1.11.52: one should repeat Om a thousand times; by Śiva's command it yields all that is desired. Also making flower gardens and the like, and likewise sweeping and the like— ॥52॥
1.11.53: having done these for Śiva, for the sake of Śiva's service, one attains Śiva's abode. Likewise one should always dwell in a Śiva-kṣetra with devotion. ॥53॥
1.11.54: Such residence grants enjoyment and liberation to all, the dull and the not-dull alike. Therefore the wise should dwell in a Śiva-kṣetra until death. ॥54॥
1.11.55: In a kṣetra whose liṅga was installed by humans, they know the area for a hundred cubits from the liṅga to be holy; in a kṣetra installed by sages, the area of a thousand aratnis is holy. ॥55॥
1.11.56: For a liṅga installed by the gods, likewise, it should be known by the measure of a thousand aratnis; in a self-manifested (svayambhū) kṣetra, the area of a thousand bow-lengths is holy. ॥56॥
1.11.57: A tank, a well and the like, and ponds situated in a holy kṣetra should be known as Śiva-Gaṅgā, according to Śiva's word. ॥57॥
1.11.58: Having bathed there, likewise having given gifts and done japa, one goes to Śiva. Taking refuge in a Śiva-kṣetra, one should likewise dwell there until death. ॥58॥
1.11.59: The second-day rite, the tenth-day rite, the monthly rite, or the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, or the annual rite in a Śiva-kṣetra, or even offering a piṇḍa in the kṣetra— ॥59॥
1.11.60: thereby one is freed from all sins and at once attains Śiva's abode. Or one may dwell there for seven nights, or five nights, ॥60॥
1.11.61: or three nights, or one night; in due course one attains Śiva's abode. In the world, a man obtains fruit in accordance with his own varṇa through his own proper conduct. ॥61॥
1.11.62: Through elevation of varṇa and through devotion, a man obtains an excess of that fruit. Everything done with desire yields its fruit at once. ॥62॥
1.11.63: Everything done without desire directly grants Śiva's abode. Morning, midday and evening—the day is divided into three, one after another in order. ॥63॥
1.11.64: The morning should be known as suited to prescribed rites, the midday to desire-oriented rites, and the evening should be known as for pacificatory rites; at night too, likewise indeed. ॥64॥
1.11.65: The time called niśītha is declared to be the two middle watches of the night. Śiva-worship at that time especially grants the attainment of what is desired. ॥65॥
1.11.66: Knowing thus, a man who acts accordingly becomes a sharer of the fruit as stated. Especially in the Kali age, attainment of fruit comes through action— ॥66॥
1.11.67: —through any action that has been stated, according to the differences of eligibility. If one is of good conduct and fearful of sin, one obtains the respective fruit. ॥67॥
1.11.68: The sages said: Now tell us briefly about the holy kṣetras, resorting to which all women and men may attain the supreme state. ॥68॥
1.11.69: O Sūta, best among excellent yogins, tell us likewise the traditions (āgamas) of the Śiva-kṣetras. Sūta said: Listen with faith to the account of all the kṣetras and their traditions. ॥69॥
1.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The worship of Śiva's liṅga and other matters, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
1.12.1: Sūta said: Listen, O wise sages, to the account of Śiva's sacred regions, which grant liberation. After that I shall tell their traditions, indeed only for the protection of the world. ॥1॥
1.12.2: The earth, extending over fifty crores of yojanas, with its mountains, woods and forests, stands by Śiva's command, bearing the world. ॥2॥
1.12.3: Here and there are Śiva's sacred places; for the liberation of those who dwell in those various places, the Lord God out of compassion fashioned the sacred region. ॥3॥
1.12.4: Some arose through being taken up by the sages, and some through being taken up by the gods; others again are self-manifested, indeed only for the protection of the world. ॥4॥
1.12.5: At a holy ford or sacred region one should always perform bathing, giving, recitation and the like; otherwise a man may incur disease, poverty, dumbness and so on. ॥5॥
1.12.6: Now, if a man meets death in this land of Bhārata, by having dwelt in a self-manifested sacred place he will attain human birth again. ॥6॥
1.12.7: Sin committed in a sacred region becomes firmly fixed, O brahmins; so while dwelling in a holy region one should not commit even the slightest sin. ॥7॥
1.12.8: By whatever means possible a man should dwell in a holy region. On the banks of the hundred streams of the Sindhu there are sacred regions in great number. ॥8॥
1.12.9: The river Sarasvatī is declared holy and likewise sixty-mouthed; a wise man should dwell on its various banks, and in due course he will attain the state of Brahmā. ॥9॥
1.12.10: The Gaṅgā, born of the Himalaya mountain, is a holy river with a hundred mouths; on its banks too are many holy regions, Kāśī and others. ॥10॥
1.12.11: There the bank is especially praised in the month of Makara, when Jupiter is in Makara. The Śoṇabhadra, ten-mouthed and holy, grants desired fruits. ॥11॥
1.12.12: By bathing and fasting there one attains the realm of Vināyaka. The Narmadā, too, is a holy great river with twenty-four mouths. ॥12॥
1.12.13: By bathing in it and dwelling by it one attains the realm of Viṣṇu. The Tamasā has twelve mouths; the river Revā has ten mouths. ॥13॥
1.12.14: The Godāvarī is supremely holy, destroying the sin of killing a brahmin or a cow; it is declared twenty-one-mouthed and grants the world of Rudra. ॥14॥
1.12.15: The Kṛṣṇaveṇī is a holy river that brings about the destruction of all sins; it is declared eighteen-mouthed and grants the world of Viṣṇu. ॥15॥
1.12.16: The Tuṅgabhadrā, ten-mouthed, grants the world of Brahmā; the holy Suvarṇamukharī is likewise declared nine-mouthed. ॥16॥
1.12.17: Right there those fallen from Brahmā's world are born well. The Sarasvatī, the Pampā, the Kanyā and the auspicious Śvetanadī— ॥17॥
1.12.18: —by dwelling on the banks of these one attains the world of Indra. The great river called Kāverī, born of the Sahya mountain, is supremely holy. ॥18॥
1.12.19: It is declared twenty-seven-mouthed, granting all desires; its banks bestow heaven and grant the states of Brahmā and Viṣṇu. ॥19॥
1.12.20: The Śaiva places there grant Śiva's world and likewise the desired fruits. One should bathe at Naimiṣa and Badarī when Jupiter and the Sun are in Meṣa (Aries). ॥20॥
1.12.21: One should know that this grants Brahmā's world, and likewise worship and so on there. Likewise bathing in the river Sindhu when Jupiter is in Siṃha and the Sun in Karkaṭa— ॥21॥
1.12.22: —and drinking the water of Kedāra and bathing there, they know to bestow knowledge. One should bathe in the Godāvarī in the month of Siṃha, when Jupiter is in Siṃha; ॥22॥
1.12.23: that it grants Śiva's world was thus declared by Śiva of old. One should bathe in the Yamunā and Śoṇa when Jupiter and the Sun have entered Kanyā (Virgo); ॥23॥
1.12.24: they know it to grant great enjoyments in the world of Dharma and the world of the elephants. Likewise one should bathe in the Kāverī when the Sun and Jupiter are in Tulā (Libra); ॥24॥
1.12.25: by the greatness of Viṣṇu's word they know it to grant all desires. When the month of Vṛścika (Scorpio) has arrived, with the Sun and Jupiter in Vṛścika, ॥25॥
1.12.26: by bathing in the river Narmadā one attains Viṣṇu's world. Bathing in the Suvarṇamukharī when Jupiter and the Sun are in Dhanus (Sagittarius)— ॥26॥
1.12.27: grants Śiva's world, according to Brahmā's word. Likewise in the month of Makara one should bathe in the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā) when Jupiter is in Makara; ॥27॥
1.12.28: it grants Śiva's world, according to Brahmā's word; having enjoyed the pleasures in the realms of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, at their end one attains knowledge. ॥28॥
1.12.29: In the Gaṅgā in the month of Māgha, when the Sun has entered Kumbha (Aquarius), a śrāddha, or an offering of rice-balls, or else water mixed with sesame— ॥29॥
1.12.30: they know to uplift ten million generations of the family of the ancestors of both lineages. They praise bathing in the Kṛṣṇaveṇī when Jupiter and the Sun are in Mīna (Pisces). ॥30॥
1.12.31: Bathing at each such holy ford in its proper month grants the state of Indra. A wise man should dwell resorting to the Gaṅgā or the Sahya-born Kāverī; ॥31॥
1.12.32: thereby the destruction of sins committed at that time certainly comes about. There are many sacred regions which grant Rudra's world. ॥32॥
1.12.33: The Tāmraparṇī and Vegavatī bestow the fruit of Brahmā's world; on their banks there are indeed sacred regions that grant heaven. ॥33॥
1.12.34: Between them there are abundant sacred regions bestowing merit; a wise man dwelling in each of them would obtain the corresponding fruit. ॥34॥
1.12.35: With good conduct, right livelihood and constant devout contemplation, the compassionate wise man should dwell there; otherwise he will not obtain that fruit. ॥35॥
1.12.36: Merit done in a holy region attains manifold increase; sin done in a holy region, even if minute, becomes great. ॥36॥
1.12.37: If the sin was committed at that time for the sake of livelihood, it will be destroyed by merit. They declare that merit grants prosperity; merit of body, likewise of speech, ॥37॥
1.12.38: and likewise of mind, destroys sin of the same kind, O brahmins. But mental sin is like an adamantine coating, following one from kalpa to kalpa. ॥38॥
1.12.39: It perishes only through meditation; otherwise it is not destroyed. Verbal sin perishes by abundant recitation, bodily sin by mortifying the body, ॥39॥
1.12.40: and sin committed through wealth perishes through giving, not otherwise even in millions of kalpas. Sometimes merit too is destroyed by sin that has grown beyond it. ॥40॥
1.12.41: Of merit and sin there are a seed-portion, a growth-portion and an enjoyment-portion. The seed-portion is destroyed by knowledge; the growth-portion is destroyed in the manner already stated. ॥41॥
1.12.42: But the enjoyment-portion is destroyed only by experiencing it, not otherwise, not even by millions of meritorious acts. When the sprouting of the seed has been destroyed, the remainder serves only for being experienced. ॥42॥
1.12.43: By the worship of the gods, by gifts to brahmins, and by intense austerity, in the course of time the experience of karmic fruit becomes bearable for men. Therefore one who desires happiness should dwell in the sacred place without committing sin at all. ॥43॥
1.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named Śiva's sacred regions, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
1.13.1: The sages said: Quickly make us hear about right conduct, by which a wise man may win the worlds. Tell us also about the practices made up of dharma and adharma, which likewise give heaven and hell. ॥1॥
1.13.2: Sūta said: A learned man endowed with right conduct is called by name a Brāhmaṇa; one endowed with Vedic practice is a Vipra; one who has only one of these is a Dvija. ॥2॥
1.13.3: One of little conduct and little Vedic learning, who serves a king, is a Kṣatriya -brāhmaṇa; one with some conduct who engages in agriculture and trade is likewise a Vaiśya -brāhmaṇa. ॥3॥
1.13.4: One who himself ploughs is called a Śūdra-brāhmaṇa; one who is envious and injures others is called a Caṇḍāla-dvija. ॥4॥
1.13.5: Among Kṣatriyas, the protector of the earth is a king; the others are regarded as Kṣatriyas. One who trades in grain and the like is a Vaiśya; the other is called a merchant. ॥5॥
1.13.6: One who serves Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas is called a Śūdra; a ploughman should be known as a Vṛṣala, and the others as Dasyus. ॥6॥
1.13.7: Everyone, at dawn, facing east, should reflect on the duties, beginning with those toward the gods, and on wealth, its troubles, income and expenditure. ॥7॥
1.13.8: Long life, enmity, death, sin, fortune, disease, nourishment and strength — these are the results of the direction faced on rising in the morning. ॥8॥
1.13.9: The last watch of the night should be known as Uṣā; half a watch at the junction is called Sandhi. Rising at that time, the twice-born should void excrement and urine. ॥9॥
1.13.10: Then, going far from the house, outside, covered with a cloth, he should sit facing north; if there is an obstacle, facing another direction, ॥10॥
1.13.11: not facing water, fire, Brāhmaṇas and the like, or the gods; covering the genital with the left hand and the mouth with the other hand. ॥11॥
1.13.12: Having voided the excrement and risen, he should not look at that excrement. He should perform cleansing outside the water, with water drawn out from it. ॥12॥
1.13.13: Or else, without entering the tīrthas of the gods, ancestors and sages, he should cleanse the anus with earth seven, five or three times. ॥13॥
1.13.14: For the genital, an amount of earth the size of a karkoṭa fruit is prescribed; for the anus, a handful. Then, rising, he should do the cleansing of feet and hands and eight mouth-rinsings. ॥14॥
1.13.15: Tooth-cleaning is declared to be done outside the water with any leaf or twig, avoiding the forefinger. ॥15॥
1.13.16: Having saluted the water-deities, he should bathe with mantra. If unable to immerse fully, entering water neck-deep or else waist-deep, ॥16॥
1.13.17: or entering knee-deep water, he should perform the mantra-bath. There the wise man should offer libations to the gods and others with the water of the tīrtha. ॥17॥
1.13.18: Taking a washed cloth, he should wear it with five tucks; and an upper garment too must be worn in all rites. ॥18॥
1.13.19: When bathing at a tīrtha such as a river, one should not wash the bathing cloth there; but at a tank, well, house and the like, the wise man should take it away after bathing and wash it. ॥19॥
