1.13.20: On stone, wood or the like, or in water, or on the ground, having washed the cloth one should wring it for the satisfaction of the ancestors, O twice-born ones. ॥20॥
1.13.21: He should apply the tripuṇḍra with ash, with the mantra taught in the Jābāla Upaniṣad. If it is done otherwise, and the ash falls into water, then he goes to hell. ॥21॥
1.13.22: With the mantra āpo hi ṣṭhā he should sprinkle the head to remove sin; with the mantra yasya the feet. This is called the sandhi-sprinkling. ॥22॥
1.13.23: Sprinkling on the heart, head and feet; on the head, heart and feet; and on the heart, feet and head — this the wise know as the mantra-bath. ॥23॥
1.13.24: In case of a slight impure contact, of ill health, of danger from the king or the realm, and when one must travel with no other option, one should perform the mantra-bath. ॥24॥
1.13.25: Having sipped water with the Sūrya-anuvāka in the morning and with the Agni-anuvāka in the evening, and likewise at midday, he should again perform the sprinkling. ॥25॥
1.13.26: At the end of reciting the Gāyatrī mantra, he should cast water upward three times toward the east; and at midday, one arghya to the Sun, along with the mantra, O twice-born ones. ॥26॥
1.13.27: When evening has come, he should offer it on the ground, facing west; in the morning he should offer it lifting the water up, and at midday likewise with the fingers. ॥27॥
1.13.28: Through the gap between the fingers he should look at the sun as it hangs in the sky; then, having turned around himself clockwise, he should perform pure ācamana. ॥28॥
1.13.29: The sandhyā performed in the evening before the proper muhūrta is futile. Only the right time is called time, as opposed to the wrong time. When the day has passed without it, expiation is in due order: ॥29॥
1.13.30: If a day of the daily rite has lapsed, he should recite the Gāyatrī a hundred times in order; if it has lapsed beyond ten days, he should practise the Gāyatrī a hundred thousand times. ॥30॥
1.13.31: If the daily rite has lapsed for a month, he must undergo the upanayana again. Īśa, Gaurī, Guha, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Candra and Yama — ॥31॥
1.13.32: such gods he should satisfy with libations for the accomplishment of his aims. Then, having made the offering to Brahman, he should perform pure ācamana. ॥32॥
1.13.33: To the south of the tīrtha, in an approved hermitage or a hall for mantras, or there in a temple, or at home in a fixed place, the wise man — ॥33॥
1.13.34: having saluted all the gods, steady in mind and steady in posture, should first practise the praṇava and then practise the Gāyatrī. ॥34॥
1.13.35: Understanding that it has as its subject the oneness of the individual self and Brahman, he should practise the praṇava. Its meaning is: The creator of the three worlds, the sustainer Acyuta, ॥35॥
1.13.36: and likewise the destroyer Rudra, the self-luminous, we worship. May he direct the organs of knowledge and action, the functions of the mind, and the intellects ॥36॥
1.13.37: ever impel them towards dharma, which grants enjoyment and liberation, and towards knowledge. Meditating thus on this meaning with his intellect, one certainly attains Brahman. ॥37॥
1.13.38: Or he may simply recite it daily, for the fulfilment of his brāhmaṇa-hood. The foremost of brāhmaṇas should practise it a thousand times daily in the morning. ॥38॥
1.13.39: For others, according to their ability. At midday he should recite it a hundred times; in the evening twenty times should be known as the rule, together with eight more (śikhāṣṭaka). ॥39॥
1.13.40: Beginning with the mūlādhāra, he should contemplate likewise those situated in the twelve stations: Vidyeśa, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Īśa, the individual self and the Supreme Lord — ॥40॥
1.13.41: With the understanding that it is Brahman, and with the meditation I am he (so'ham), realising identity with it, one should do japa. One should contemplate those very mantras at the brahmarandhra and other centres, and also outside the body. ॥41॥
1.13.42: Beginning from the mahat-tattva, the bodies are a thousand; by each single round of japa, passing beyond one of them gradually, ॥42॥
1.13.43: one should unite the individual soul with the Supreme; this is declared to be the essence of japa. The body is counted as a hundred and twenty, together with an eightfold śikhā; ॥43॥
1.13.44: such indeed is the japa of mantras; they understand japa according to the initial order. One should know that a thousand repetitions bestow Brahmā's state; a hundred, they know, bestow Indra's. ॥44॥
1.13.45: The other lesser number serves for self-protection; by it one is born in brahmin families. Having worshipped the Sun, one should do thus daily. ॥45॥
1.13.46: One endowed with twelve lakhs of Gāyatrī japa is declared a complete brahmin. One who lacks even a lakh of Gāyatrī should not be employed in Vedic rites. ॥46॥
1.13.47: Up to seventy years one should keep the observance; afterwards one should take up renunciation. The renunciant should do japa of the praṇava twelve thousand times in the morning. ॥47॥
1.13.48: If a day lapses, one should make it up day by day by doing japa thus in due order; if a month or more has gradually lapsed, it is made up by japa of a lakh and a half. ॥48॥
1.13.49: If the lapse extends beyond this, one should perform the praiṣa, the rite of renunciation, again. Doing so, the fault is pacified; otherwise one goes to Raurava hell. ॥49॥
1.13.50: Then one who has desires should strive for dharma and wealth, not the other the desireless. A brahmin should be desirous of liberation and should always practise knowledge of Brahman. ॥50॥
1.13.51: From dharma comes wealth, from wealth enjoyment, and from enjoyment arises dispassion. Through enjoyment of wealth earned by dharma, dispassion is born. ॥51॥
1.13.52: Through enjoyment of wealth gained in the contrary way, only attachment arises. Dharma is said to be twofold, by way of the pair: substance and body. ॥52॥
1.13.53: Dharma of substance takes the form of sacrifice and the like; bathing at tīrthas and the like is bodily. By dharma one obtains wealth; by austerity, a divine form. ॥53॥
1.13.54: The desireless one attains purity, and through purity knowledge, without doubt. In the Kṛta and following ages austerity is praised; in the Kali age, the dharma of substance. ॥54॥
1.13.55: In Kṛta, knowledge is attained through meditation; in Tretā, likewise through austerity; in Dvāpara, knowledge through sacrifice; in Kali, through worship of images. ॥55॥
1.13.56: Whatever the merit or sin, such indeed is the fruit; there is diminution, increase, loss and so on according to the difference of substance, body and limb. ॥56॥
1.13.57: Adharma has the nature of harm; dharma has the nature of happiness. From adharma one obtains sorrow; from dharma one indeed thrives in happiness. ॥57॥
1.13.58: One should know that sorrow comes from bad conduct and happiness from good conduct. Therefore one should acquire dharma for the accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation. ॥58॥
1.13.59: To a brahmin with a family of four persons one should give a livelihood for a hundred years; that bestows Brahmaloka. ॥59॥
1.13.60: A thousand cāndrāyaṇa fasts, they know, bestow Brahmaloka. A kṣatriya should establish the livelihood of a thousand families; ॥60॥
1.13.61: one should know that this bestows Indra's world; ten thousand families bestow Brahmaloka. Whatever deity a man places foremost when he makes a gift, ॥61॥
1.13.62: he attains that very deity's world — so the knowers of the Veda know. One who lacks wealth should likewise always acquire merit through austerities. ॥62॥
1.13.63: Through tīrthas and austerity one enjoys imperishable happiness that is to be gained. Now I shall speak of acquiring wealth justly; listen attentively. ॥63॥
1.13.64: From his own work, from receiving gifts and from officiating at sacrifices — by pure means, without servility and without excessive hardship — a brahmin should earn wealth. ॥64॥
1.13.65: A kṣatriya should earn by the might of his arms, a vaiśya by agriculture and cattle-keeping. By giving away wealth justly earned one attains success. ॥65॥
1.13.66: Through the attainment of knowledge comes the attainment of liberation for all, by the guru's grace. From liberation comes realisation of one's true nature; one enjoys supreme bliss. ॥66॥
1.13.67: All this arises for men from the company of the good, O brahmins. All wealth, grain and the like should be given by the householder. ॥67॥
1.13.68: Whatever goods, fruit or grain appear in whatever season — all that should be given to brahmins by one who desires his own welfare. ॥68॥
1.13.69: Water should always be given, and food for allaying hunger and illness. Field, grain, uncooked food and cooked food — thus food is fourfold. ॥69॥
1.13.70: For as long as one who has eaten that food thrives in hearing sacred teaching, half the merit earned during that time belongs to the giver, without doubt. ॥70॥
1.13.71: The receiver, for what he has received, should purge his sin by giving and likewise by austerity; otherwise he goes to Raurava. ॥71॥
1.13.72: One should divide one's wealth into three: for dharma, for growth and for one's own enjoyment. One should perform the obligatory, occasional and desire-motivated rites from the dharma portion. ॥72॥
1.13.73: The practitioner should increase his wealth by means of the growth portion; with the enjoyment portion he should enjoy what is wholesome, moderate and pure. ॥73॥
1.13.74: Of what is earned by agriculture, a tenth should be given for the purification of sin; with the remainder one should perform dharma and the rest; otherwise one goes to Raurava, ॥74॥
1.13.75: or he becomes sinful-minded, or the crop will go to ruin. In moneylending and trade, the wise should give a sixth part. ॥75॥
1.13.76: From a pure acceptance of gifts, the best of brahmins should give a fourth part; from wealth that comes unexpectedly, the best of brahmins should give half. ॥76॥
1.13.77: In an improper acceptance of gifts, one should cast that entire bad gift into the ocean. Gifts should be made after inviting the recipients, for the prosperity of one's own enjoyment. ॥77॥
1.13.78: Whatever is asked for should always be given, according to one's own capacity. If a thing asked for is not given, one becomes a debtor in another birth. ॥78॥
1.13.79: The wise man should not proclaim the faults of others; likewise, O brahmin, he should not out of hatred repeat what he has heard or seen. ॥79॥
1.13.80: The wise man should not say what provokes anger in the heart of any creature. At the two twilights one should perform the fire-rite for the attainment of prosperity. ॥80॥
1.13.81: Or, if unable to do so twice, one should worship the Sun and Fire once a day according to rule, offering rice grains, other grain, ghee, fruit, roots, or other oblation material likewise. ॥81॥
1.13.82: Likewise one should perform the sthālīpāka pot-cooked offering properly and according to rule; or, in the absence of oblation material, one should perform just the principal homa. ॥82॥
1.13.83: This is called the constant kindling (nityasandhāna); the wise know it as the perpetual fire. Or else one may do mere japa, or just salutation to the Sun. ॥83॥
1.13.84: Thus should those who seek the Self act, and also he who seeks wealth, according to rule. Those always devoted to the Brahmayajña Vedic study, likewise devoted to the worship of the gods, ॥84॥
1.13.85: always intent on fire-worship, and likewise devoted to the worship of the guru, and those who satisfy brāhmaṇas — all are sharers in heaven. ॥85॥
1.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named Right conduct, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
1.14.1: The sages said: O lord, tell us in due order about the fire-sacrifice, the sacrifice to the gods, the Brahma-sacrifice, the worship of the guru, and the satisfaction of Brahman. ॥1॥
1.14.2: Sūta said: Whatever substance one offers into the fire is called the fire-sacrifice. For those in the stage of celibate studentship it is simply the laying of fuel-sticks on the fire. ॥2॥
1.14.3: In the fuel-stick fire are performed vows and the like, and special worship and so on; thus it is for those of the first stage of life, O brahmins, until they take up the aupāsana domestic fire. ॥3॥
1.14.4: For forest-dwellers and renunciants who have deposited the fires within themselves, O brahmins, the eating of wholesome, measured and pure food at the proper time is their oblation. ॥4॥
1.14.5: Beginning from the kindling of the aupāsana fire, the fire well guarded in a fire-pit or in a vessel—that is called perpetual (ajasra). ॥5॥
1.14.6: When, through compulsion of the king or of fate, out of fear of abandoning the fire, one firmly places the fire in oneself or in the kindling-stick, it is said to be deposited (samāropita). ॥6॥
1.14.7: The evening oblation to Agni, O brahmins, should be known as bringing prosperity; likewise the morning oblation to Sūrya should be known as bestowing long life. ॥7॥
1.14.8: This is called the fire-sacrifice, since by day the sun enters the fire. That which one offers into the fire with all the gods, Indra and the rest, in view— ॥8॥
1.14.9: —that one should know as the sacrifice to the gods, namely, rites such as the sthālīpāka; likewise the tonsure and similar rites should be known as established in the ordinary fire. ॥9॥
1.14.10: A twice-born should perform the Brahma-sacrifice repeatedly for the satisfaction of the gods. What is called the Brahma-sacrifice is the study of the Veda. ॥10॥
1.14.11: It is done after the daily rites up to evening; after that it is not prescribed. Now hear with faith and reverence the worship of the gods without fire. ॥11॥
1.14.12: At the first creation Mahādeva, the omniscient Lord, the mine of compassion, devised the days of the week for the benefit of all the worlds. ॥12॥
1.14.13: The physician of worldly existence, the omniscient one, the medicine of all medicines, the Lord first made his own day, which grants health. ॥13॥
1.14.14: Then he made the day of his own Māyā, which brings prosperity. After that, for those whose birth is beset by misfortune, the day of Kumāra— ॥14॥
1.14.15: —the Lord devised a day for overcoming sloth and evil. Likewise, desiring the welfare of the worlds, the day of Viṣṇu the protector— ॥15॥
1.14.16: —the Lord devised a day for nourishment and for protection. Then the life-giving day of the very maker of life-spans— ॥16॥
1.14.17: —of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, the creator of the three worlds, the Lord devised a day for securing the longevity of the world. ॥17॥
1.14.18: In the beginning, merit and sin having been devised for the growth of the three worlds, then the days of their two agents, Indra and Yama— ॥18॥
1.14.19: —granting enjoyment and removing death for the worlds, were devised. Then Āditya and the others, his own forms, indicators of pleasure and pain— ॥19॥
1.14.20: —having first fashioned them as lords of the days, established in the circle of luminaries; worship of them on their respective days grants their respective fruits. ॥20॥
1.14.21: Health, prosperity, the cure of diseases, nourishment, long life, enjoyment and the warding off of death, in that order— ॥21॥
1.14.22: —they declare to be the fruits of the days in sequence, preceded by the gods' pleasure. Śiva is the giver of the fruit of the worship of the other gods as well. ॥22॥
1.14.23: For the pleasure of the gods worship is devised in five ways: the repetition of their respective mantras, fire-offering, gift, and austerity, ॥23॥
1.14.24: and worship on a prepared altar-ground, in an image, in fire, or in the person of a brahmin, with the sixteen services. ॥24॥
1.14.25: Each later one is superior to the earlier; in the absence of the earlier, the later may be used. For diseases of the eyes and head, and for the cure of leprosy, ॥25॥
1.14.26: one should worship Āditya and then feed brahmins, for a day, a month, a year, or even three years. ॥26॥
1.14.27: If the karma already begun (prārabdha) is strong, then by this, disease, old age and the like would be destroyed. They know japa and the rest addressed to one's chosen deity as the fruit of the days and so on. ॥27॥
1.14.28: On Sunday especially one should make offering for the pacification of sins; worship of Āditya, of the gods and of brahmins bestows special benefit. ॥28॥
1.14.29: On Monday the wise man should worship Lakṣmī and the others for wealth, and should feed brahmins together with their wives with food prepared with ghee. ॥29॥
1.14.30: On Tuesday one should worship Kālī and the others for the alleviation of disease, and feed brahmins with food of black gram, green gram and pigeon pea. ॥30॥
1.14.31: On Wednesday likewise the wise man should worship Viṣṇu with curd-rice; thereby the nourishment of sons, friends, wife and others always comes about. ॥31॥
1.14.32: One desiring long life should, on Thursday, for attaining nourishment, worship the gods with a sacred thread, cloth, and milk with ghee—so should the wise man do. ॥32॥
1.14.33: For enjoyments, on Friday one should worship the gods with a collected mind, and give food endowed with the six flavours for the satisfaction of brahmins. ॥33॥
1.14.34: Likewise, for the satisfaction of women, auspicious garments and the like should be given. On Saturday, which removes untimely death, the wise man should worship Rudra and the others, ॥34॥
1.14.35: with sesame oblations and gifts, and should feed brahmins with sesame food. Worshipping the gods in this way one would obtain fruits such as health. ॥35॥
1.14.36: In the daily worship of the gods and in special worship too, in bathing, giving, japa, fire-offering, and in the satisfying of brahmins, ॥36॥
1.14.37: at conjunctions of lunar days and constellations, in the worship of the respective deities, on Sunday and the other days, the omniscient Lord of the world— ॥37॥
1.14.38: —in the form of each deity, grants to all the fruits such as health, according to place and time, and likewise according to the recipient, ॥38॥
1.14.39: according to the materials and the faith, and likewise according to the people; in graded measure the god bestows health and the rest. ॥39॥
1.14.40: At the start of auspicious events and at the end of inauspicious ones, and on birth-star days, the householder should worship at home the planets Āditya and the rest for abundance of health and the like. ॥40॥
1.14.41: Therefore the worship of the gods, which grants all desired fruits, performed with Vedic mantras for brāhmaṇas, and in the Tantric manner for others, ॥41॥
1.14.42: should always be performed by men according to their capacity, on all seven days of the week, by men desiring auspicious fruits. ॥42॥
1.14.43: A poor man should worship the gods through austerity, a wealthy one through wealth. And again he performs such dharma with faith, ॥43॥
1.14.44: and again, having enjoyed various pleasures, he is born on earth. Shade trees, reservoirs of water, installation of brāhmaṇas, accumulation of merit — ॥44॥
1.14.45: all this a wealthy man should always do for the attainment of enjoyment. And in time, through the ripening of merit, the attainment of knowledge arises. ॥45॥
1.14.46: O twice-born ones, the man who hears or recites this chapter, and also one who helps others to hear it, would obtain the fruit of worshipping the gods. ॥46॥
1.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The fire-sacrifice and other rites, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
1.15.1: The sages said: O Sūta, foremost among knowers of all matters, tell us in due order about place and the rest. Sūta said: In rites such as worship of the gods, a clean house gives the standard (equal) result. ॥1॥
1.15.2: Ten times that is a cowshed; ten times that, the bank of a water-body; ten times that, the foot of a bilva, tulasī or aśvattha tree. ॥2॥
1.15.3: Then one should know a temple as ten times greater; ten times that, the bank of a holy place; ten times that, the bank of a river; ten times that, of a sacred river. ॥3॥
1.15.4: The holy bank of the seven Gaṅgā-rivers would be ten times that. Gaṅgā, Godāvarī, Kāverī, Tāmraparṇikā, ॥4॥
1.15.5: Sindhu, Sarayū and Revā — these are proclaimed the seven Gaṅgās. Then the seashore is ten times that, and a mountain peak ten times that. ॥5॥
1.15.6: But the place where the mind delights should be known as superior to all. In the Kṛta age, sacrifice, gifts and the like are to be known as yielding full fruit. ॥6॥
1.15.7: In the Tretā age three quarters, and in the Dvāpara half, is always declared; in Kali one quarter is to be known, and in its latter half, that quarter reduced by a quarter. ॥7॥
1.15.8: For one of pure self, a pure day is meritorious and gives the standard result, so they know. Ten times that, O wise ones, is to be known at the sun's transit into a sign. ॥8॥
1.15.9: At the equinox ten times that; at the solstice ten times that is declared; ten times that at the transit into Capricorn (Mṛga); and ten times that at a lunar eclipse. ॥9॥
1.15.10: And beyond that, at a solar eclipse, the supreme time, they know the result to be full. Because the sun, whose form is the world, is joined with poison, that time causes disease. ॥10॥
1.15.11: Therefore, to pacify that poison, one should perform bathing, gifts and japa. Because it is the time for pacifying poison, that time is declared to bestow merit. ॥11॥
1.15.12: On the day of one's birth-star and at the end of a vow, they know the time to be equal to a solar eclipse. And the time of association with great souls they know as equal to an eclipse of ten million suns. ॥12॥
1.15.13: Those steadfast in austerity, those steadfast in knowledge, yogins and renunciants — these indeed are worthy recipients of worship and a cause of the destruction of sin. ॥13॥
1.15.14: Or a brāhmaṇa who has completed twenty-four lakh japa of the Gāyatrī becomes a worthy recipient, granting enjoyment of the complete fruit. ॥14॥
1.15.15: It protects from falling — thus the word pātra is used in scripture. Because it protects the giver from sin, it is called pātra. ॥15॥
1.15.16: She protects the one who chants her from a fall; therefore she is called Gāyatrī. Just as one without wealth in this world does not give wealth to another, ॥16॥
1.15.17: while one who is wealthy here in the world gives wealth to another — so one who is himself pure, of purified self, is able to save men. ॥17॥
1.15.18: One purified by Gāyatrī japa is called a pure brāhmaṇa. Therefore in giving, japa, fire-offering, worship and in every rite, ॥18॥
1.15.19: the brāhmaṇa deserves the status of recipient, so that the gift may be made and the giver protected. For food, the worthy recipient is the hungry person, whether woman or man. ॥19॥
1.15.20: Having invited an excellent, well-composed brāhmaṇa at the proper time, giving for his sake words or wealth that is truly enlightening and fulfils desires — ॥20॥
1.15.21: and giving to one who desires it — they know such giving to yield the full fruit. What is given after being asked, they know to yield half the fruit. ॥21॥
1.15.22: What is given to a servant, they know to yield a quarter of the fruit. O best of the twice-born, to a vipra who is so by birth alone and of wretched livelihood, ॥22॥
1.15.23: wealth given yields enjoyment for ten years on the earthly world; given to a vipra versed in the Veda, ten years in heaven. ॥23॥
1.15.24: Given to one devoted to Gāyatrī japa, ten years in Satyaloka; what is given to a vipra devoted to Viṣṇu, they know to bestow Vaikuṇṭha. ॥24॥
1.15.25: What is given to a vipra devoted to Śiva, they know to bestow Kailāsa. For the enjoyment of those respective worlds, giving is recommended to all. ॥25॥
1.15.26: A man who gives tenfold food to a vipra on Sunday enjoys health for ten years in his next birth. ॥26॥
1.15.27: Great respect, invitation, oil-anointing, service of the feet, clothing, worship with fragrances and the like, food with ghee-cakes and choice juices, ॥27॥
1.15.28: dishes of six flavours, betel, followed by a fee (dakṣiṇā), salutation and accompanying the guest on departure — this is the ten-part gift of good food. ॥28॥
1.15.29: A man who gives tenfold food to ten vipras on Sunday likewise enjoys health for a hundred years. ॥29॥
1.15.30: On Monday and the other days, the fruit of food-giving is to be known as according to the quality of each day, in the earthly world in the next birth. ॥30॥
1.15.31: On all seven days too, having given tenfold food to ten vipras, one enjoys health and the like for a hundred years. ॥31॥
1.15.32: Thus a man who gives to a hundred vipras on Sunday enjoys health for a thousand years in the world of Śarva (Śiva). ॥32॥
1.15.33: Likewise, having given to a thousand, one enjoys it for ten thousand years. Thus it should be understood by the wise for Monday and the other days. ॥33॥
1.15.34: Having given food on Sunday to thousands whose minds are purified by the Gāyatrī, one enjoys health and the like in Satyaloka. ॥34॥
1.15.35: Likewise, having given to ten thousand, one enjoys it in Viṣṇu's world; having given food to lakhs, one enjoys it in Rudra's world. ॥35॥
1.15.36: Men seeking learning should give to boys, regarding them as Brahmā; men desiring sons should give to youths, regarding them as Viṣṇu. ॥36॥
1.15.37: Men seeking knowledge should give to the aged, regarding them as Rudra; the best of men desiring intelligence should give to young girls, regarding them as Bhāratī (Sarasvatī). ॥37॥
1.15.38: The best of men desiring enjoyments should give to young women, regarding them as Lakṣmī; those seeking the Self should give to old women, regarding them as Pārvatī. ॥38॥
1.15.39: What is earned by gleaning ears of grain (śila) or scattered grains (uñcha), or as a teacher's fee, they call pure wealth; they know it yields the full fruit. ॥39॥
1.15.40: What is given out of honest acceptance of gifts is called middling wealth; what is obtained through agriculture and trade is called inferior wealth. ॥40॥
1.15.41: For kṣatriyas and vaiśyas, wealth earned through valour and through trade respectively is said to be the best wealth; for śūdras, it is wealth earned through wage-labour. ॥41॥
1.15.42: For women who seek dharma, proper wealth is that received from the father and likewise from the husband. The twelve gifts, beginning with the cow, should be given in order in the months beginning with Caitra, ॥42॥
1.15.43: or, all together at an auspicious time, one should give them for the flourishing of what one desires: cow, land, sesame, gold, ghee, cloth, grain and jaggery, ॥43॥
1.15.44: silver, salt, pumpkin, and a maiden — these are the twelve. From the gift of a cow, through the cow-products given and through the beneficial cow-dung, ॥44॥
1.15.45: there is removal of sins connected with wealth, grain and the like; and of sins connected with water, oil and the like, removal by cow's urine. ॥45॥
1.15.46: and of the three kinds of sin, bodily and the rest, by milk, curd and ghee; and likewise their nourishment by these should be understood by the wise. ॥46॥
1.15.47: The gift of land, O brahmins, is for a firm foundation here and in the hereafter; the gift of sesame is for strength, and they know it always as conquering death. ॥47॥
1.15.48: Gold increases the digestive fire and gives virility; ghee one should know as nourishing; cloth they know as granting long life. ॥48॥
1.15.49: Grain is for abundance of food; jaggery bestows sweet food; silver is for the increase of semen; and salt is for the six tastes. ॥49॥
1.15.50: All given together are for every kind of prosperity; the pumpkin they know as nourishing. These bestow the attainment of all enjoyments here and hereafter, O brahmins. ॥50॥
1.15.51: The gift of a maiden is declared to bestow enjoyment for as long as life lasts. The fruit of trees such as jackfruit, mango and wood-apple, ॥51॥
1.15.52: and the fruit of plants such as the plantain, and likewise that produced from shrubs; and likewise the produce of māṣa beans and the like and of mudga beans, and vegetables and so on, ॥52॥
1.15.53: and likewise the vegetable condiments, pepper, mustard and the like — whatever fruit is ripe in whatever season, that should be given by the wise. ॥53॥
1.15.54: Satisfaction of the senses, beginning with the ear, should always be given by the wise; for the ten enjoyments beginning with sound, it brings contentment to the deities of the directions and the rest. ॥54॥
1.15.55: The conviction that actions bear fruit, formed by taking up the Veda and śāstra and understanding them oneself from the guru's mouth, is called āstikya (faith). ॥55॥
1.15.56: A conviction arising from fear of relatives or of the king is also faith (śraddhā), but it is inferior. In the absence of all means, a poor man should worship by speech or by bodily action. ॥56॥
1.15.57: One should know verbal worship as mantra, hymns, japa and the like; pilgrimage to sacred places, vows and the like they know as bodily worship. ॥57॥
1.15.58: By whatever means, whether little or much, what is done with the intention of offering it to the deity becomes a source of enjoyment. ॥58॥
1.15.59: Both the practice of austerity and charity should always be performed. A dwelling should be given, befitting one's own class and adorned with good qualities, ॥59॥
1.15.60: it is given by the wise for the abundant satisfaction of the gods and bestows all enjoyments. The wise one obtains an excellent birth here and hereafter and constant enjoyment; but having done it with the intention of offering it to Īśvara, he obtains the fruit of liberation. ॥60॥
1.15.61: The man who reads this chapter, or who always listens to it — in him arise a mind set on dharma and the attainment of knowledge. ॥61॥
1.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named Place, time, recipient and other matters, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
1.16.1: The sages said: O best of the virtuous, tell us the procedure for worshipping an earthen image, the procedure of worship by which every desired thing is obtained. ॥1॥
1.16.2: Sūta said: You have asked very well. This worship always bestows every aim and at once allays sorrow. Listen; I shall tell you. ॥2॥
1.16.3: O brahmins, it removes untimely death and destroys even death at its appointed time; it at once grants wife, sons and the like, wealth and grain. ॥3॥
1.16.4: Since food such as rice, clothing and the like—everything—arises from the earth, therefore worship of an image of clay and the like grants what is desired on earth. ॥4॥
1.16.5: Both men and women certainly have eligibility for this. One should bring clay from beneath the water of a river, a pond or a well. ॥5॥
1.16.6: Having purified it with fragrant powder and had it ground in a good pavilion, one should make the image by hand, well prepared with milk. ॥6॥
1.16.7: Having made it complete with major and minor limbs, furnished with weapons and seated on a lotus seat, one should worship it with reverence. ॥7॥
1.16.8: The twice-born should always worship the images of Vighneśa, Āditya, Viṣṇu, Ambā and Śiva—and, of Śiva, the Śivaliṅga. ॥8॥
1.16.9: He should perform it with the sixteen services to attain its fruit. He should sprinkle water with a flower and perform the ablution with mantras. ॥9॥
1.16.10: The food-offering should be of śāli rice only, all of it measured in kuḍavas. For worship at home a kuḍava is to be known as the measure; for a liṅga set up by men a prastha is prescribed. ॥10॥
1.16.11: For a divinely installed liṅga three prasthas are proper; for a self-manifest one, five prasthas. Thus one should know that full fruit results; two or three times that amount is more fruitful. ॥11॥
1.16.12: By a thousand such worships the twice-born truly attains Satyaloka. A vessel twelve aṅgulas in length, and twice that, and more than that, ॥12॥
1.16.13: with a thickness of one aṅgula and a height of three times five aṅgulas—such a vessel made of iron or wood is called śiva by the wise. ॥13॥
1.16.14: An eighth part of that is a prastha; that is held to be four kuḍavas. Ten prasthas, a hundred prasthas and a thousand prasthas— ॥14॥
1.16.15: —of water, oil and the like, and of fragrances, in measure as is fitting, for liṅgas installed by men, by sages and self-manifest, is called the great worship. ॥15॥
1.16.16: From ablution comes self-purification; from fragrance merit is gained; from the food-offering, long life and satisfaction; from incense, wealth is gained. ॥16॥
1.16.17: From the lamp one gains knowledge; from betel one obtains enjoyment. Therefore one should carefully perform the six beginning with bathing. ॥17॥
1.16.18: Prostration and japa—both grant all desires; they should always be performed at the end of worship by men seeking enjoyment and liberation. ॥18॥
1.16.19: Having first worshipped mentally, a man should always perform each rite. By the worship of the gods one attains the world of each respective god. ॥19॥
1.16.20: And in the intermediate worlds within those, enjoyments are obtained as one wishes. I shall tell the particulars of these; listen with faith, O brahmins. ॥20॥
1.16.21: By proper worship of Vighneśa one gains one's desires in Bhūrloka. On a Friday, on the fourth lunar day of the bright fortnight in Śrāvaṇa and Bhādrapada, ॥21॥
1.16.22: under the asterism Bhiṣak (Śatabhiṣaj), and in the month when the sun is in Dhanus, one should duly worship Vighneśa. One should complete a hundred or a thousand worships over as many days. ॥22॥
1.16.23: Done daily with faith in the deity and the fire, it grants sons and desired things to men, quells all sins and destroys the respective misfortunes. ॥23॥
1.16.24: They know that worship of Śiva and the others on the weekdays grants self-purification; the weekday is the basis of tithis, nakṣatras and yogas, and fulfils all desires. ॥24॥
1.16.25: Likewise, because it has no increase or decrease, they know it to be of the nature of the full Brahman. The weekday runs from sunrise to sunrise for rites such as Vedic ones. ॥25॥
1.16.26: Worship of the gods on tithis and the like grants full enjoyment to men. For the ancestors, the former part of the tithi, joined with night, is commended. ॥26॥
1.16.27: For the gods, the latter part, joined with daytime, is commended. The tithi prevailing at sunrise is to be accepted, if that tithi extends to midday. ॥27॥
1.16.28: Likewise, in rites for the gods, auspicious tithis, asterisms and the like are to be adopted. Having carefully considered the weekdays and so on, one should perform worship, japa and the rest. ॥28॥
1.16.29: Pūr is born by this — such is the construal of the meaning of pūjā in the Vedas: pūr, the accomplishment of the fruit of enjoyment, arises through that act. ॥29॥
1.16.30: Likewise it produces mental dispositions and knowledge through bringing about desired enjoyments and aims. Thus indeed is the meaning of the word pūjā well known in the world and in the Veda. ॥30॥
1.16.31: Regular and occasional rites bear fruit in course of time; an optional rite, when well performed, at once. Performed daily, monthly, fortnightly and yearly, in due order, ॥31॥
1.16.32: there is attainment of the fruit of each respective rite and a corresponding destruction of sin, in order. Worship of Mahāgaṇapati on the fourth day of the dark fortnight ॥32॥
1.16.33: destroys the sins of a fortnight and grants a fortnight's fruit of enjoyment. Worship done on the fourth day in Caitra grants the fruit of a month. ॥33॥
1.16.34: Worship performed in Bhādrapada when the sun is in Siṃha should be known to grant a year's enjoyment. On a Sunday in Śrāvaṇa, on the seventh day, on a day of the Hasta asterism, ॥34॥
1.16.35: and on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, one should perform the worship of Āditya. In Jyeṣṭha and Bhādrapada, on a Wednesday, on the twelfth day, under the Śravaṇa asterism, ॥35॥
1.16.36: worship of Śrī Viṣṇu performed then they know to bring desired prosperity. Worship of Viṣṇu in Śrāvaṇa grants desired things and health. ॥36॥
1.16.37: Whatever fruit comes from giving the twelve objects beginning with cows, together with their accessories, that fruit one obtains by gratifying Viṣṇu on the twelfth day. ॥37॥
1.16.38: On the twelfth day one should worship twelve brahmins with the sixteen services, addressing them by the twelve names of Viṣṇu; thus one obtains his favour. ॥38॥
1.16.39: In the same way, for all the gods, worship of twelve brahmins with the respective twelve names of each god brings about the favour of that god. ॥39॥
1.16.40: One desiring prosperity should worship Ambā, the giver of the fruit of all enjoyments, in the month of Karkaṭa, on a Monday, on the ninth day, under the Mṛgaśīrṣa asterism. ॥40॥
1.16.41: The ninth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvayuja grants the fruit of all desired things. On a Sunday, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, especially, ॥41॥
1.16.42: and under the asterism Ārdrā and the great Ārdrā, the worship of Śiva is especially excellent. On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha it grants the fruit of all desired things; ॥42॥
1.16.43: it bestows long life, removes death and brings every attainment to men. In the month of Jyeṣṭha under the great Ārdrā, and also on the fourteenth day, ॥43॥
1.16.44: or under Ārdrā in Mārgaśīrṣa, having worshipped Śiva in his respective forms with the sixteen services, one obtains indeed the sight of his feet. ॥44॥
1.16.45: The worship of Śiva should be known as granting enjoyment and liberation to men. The worship of the gods of the weekdays and the rest is especially excellent in Kārtika. ॥45॥
1.16.46: When the month of Kārtika has arrived, the wise man should worship all the gods, with gifts, austerity, fire-offerings, recitation and observances, ॥46॥
1.16.47: and with the sixteen services, through images, brāhmaṇas and mantras, and by feeding brāhmaṇas; thus one who is free of desire becomes a remover of afflictions. ॥47॥
1.16.48: Worship of the gods in Kārtika grants all enjoyments; it also removes diseases, and there is destruction of evil spirits and seizing planets. ॥48॥
1.16.49: On the Sundays of Kārtika, through men's worship of the Sun and by gifts of oil and cotton, leprosy and the like are destroyed. ॥49॥
1.16.50: By gifts of myrobalan and pepper, of cloth, milk and the like, and by installing an image of Brahmā, consumption is destroyed. ॥50॥
1.16.51: And by gifts of lamps and mustard, epilepsy is destroyed. On the Mondays of the month of Kṛttikā, men's worship of Śiva ॥51॥
1.16.52: allays great poverty and brings all prosperity, especially with gifts of houses, fields and the like, and of household utensils and so on. ॥52॥
1.16.53: On the Tuesdays of Kṛttikā, by men's worship of Skanda and by gifts of lamps, bells and the like, mastery of speech soon arises. ॥53॥
1.16.54: On the Wednesdays of Kṛttikā, men's worship of Viṣṇu and the gift of curd-rice bring good offspring. ॥54॥
1.16.55: On the Thursdays of Kṛttikā, by worshipping Brahmā with riches and by gifts of honey, gold and ghee, men's enjoyments increase. ॥55॥
1.16.56: On the Fridays of Kṛttikā, by worship of the elephant-faced Gaṇeśa and by gifts of perfume, flowers and food, men's objects of enjoyment increase. ॥56॥
1.16.57: A barren woman obtains a fine son by gifts of gold, silver and the like. On the Saturdays of Kṛttikā, the salutation of the guardians of the quarters, ॥57॥
1.16.58: the worship of the elephants of the quarters, of the Nāgas and of the guardians of the bridges, and of Tryambaka Rudra and of Viṣṇu the remover of sin, ॥58॥
1.16.59: and likewise of Brahmā, and of Dhanvantari and the two Aśvins, bestows knowledge, removes disease and untimely death, and gives immediate relief from illness, ॥59॥
1.16.60: together with gifts of salt, iron and oil, and of black gram and the like; with gifts of the three pungents, fruits and perfumes, and of water and the like; ॥60॥
1.16.61: giving liquids by the prastha and solids by the pala measure, one attains heaven. In the month of Dhanus, worship at dawn ॥61॥
1.16.62: of Śiva and all the others in due order is enjoined for every attainment. An offering of śāli rice prepared as sacrificial food is declared commendable. ॥62॥
1.16.63: An offering of various foods is especially excellent in the month of Dhanus. For one who gives food in Mārgaśīrṣa, every desired fruit comes about. ॥63॥
1.16.64: Destruction of sin, fulfilment of wishes, health and dharma, thorough knowledge of the Veda and good practice, ॥64॥
1.16.65: great enjoyments here and hereafter, eternal union (yoga) at the end, and the attainment of Vedāntic knowledge — these the giver of food in Mārgaśīrṣa obtains. ॥65॥
1.16.66: In Mārgaśīrṣa, at dawn, or else for three days, one who desires enjoyment should worship the gods; he should not be one who neglects the Dhanus month. ॥66॥
1.16.67: The Dhanus-month worship is prescribed up to the saṅgava period of the morning. In the Dhanus month, fasting for the whole month and with senses controlled, ॥67॥
1.16.68: a brāhmaṇa should recite the Gāyatrī, mother of the Vedas, until midday; afterwards he should recite the five-syllable and other mantras until bedtime. ॥68॥
1.16.69: Having gained knowledge, the brāhmaṇa attains liberation at the end of the body. For other men and women, by bathing three times a day and by recitation ॥69॥
1.16.70: of the five-syllable mantra always, pure knowledge is attained. By always reciting the chosen mantras one obtains the destruction of great sins. ॥70॥
1.16.71: In the month of Dhanus especially, one should perform the great food-offering: with a bhāra of śāli rice grains and a prastha of pepper, ॥71॥
1.16.72: everything twelvefold in count, with a kuḍava of honey and ghee, with green gram amounting to a droṇa, and with twelve side-dishes, ॥72॥
1.16.73: with cakes cooked in ghee, sweet balls, śālikā and the like — twelve of each — and with curd and milk to the amount of twelve prasthas, ॥73॥
1.16.74: and coconuts and other fruits likewise by count; furnished with twelve areca nuts and with thirty-six betel leaves, ॥74॥
1.16.75: together with powdered camphor and khura and the five fragrant substances, and accompanied by betel — this is the definition of the great food-offering. ॥75॥
1.16.76: This great food-offering, after first being offered to the deity, should be distributed to his devotees in the order of the varṇas. ॥76॥
1.16.77: Thus by an offering of cooked rice one becomes a ruler of a realm on earth; by giving the great food-offering a man attains heaven. ॥77॥
1.16.78: By giving a thousand great food-offerings, O best of the twice-born, one attains Satyaloka and a full life-span in that world. ॥78॥
1.16.79: By giving thirty thousand great food-offerings, one reaches the world above that and does not again partake of birth. ॥79॥
1.16.80: Thirty-six thousand is declared the lifetime offering; a gift of offerings to that extent is called the great complete (mahāpūrṇa). ॥80॥
1.16.81: The food-offering of the Mahāpūrṇa (great full measure) is held to be the birth-offering (janma-naivedya). By giving the birth-offering there is no rebirth. ॥81॥
1.16.82: In the month of Ūrja (Kārttika), on a holy day that coincides with a saṅkrānti, a vyatīpāta, one's birth-star, the full moon and the like, one should perform the birth-offering. ॥82॥
1.16.83: On one's yearly birthday one should perform the excellent birth-offering, and also in other months on the day when the birth-star coincides with the full moon. ॥83॥
1.16.84: At such a conjunction, or else gradually, one should perform it up to a thousand times. By giving the birth-offering one obtains the fruit of offering up one's very birth. ॥84॥
1.16.85: Pleased by the offering of one's birth, Śiva indeed grants union with himself (sāyujya). This birth-offering should be given to Śiva alone. ॥85॥
1.16.86: In the form of yoni and liṅga, Śiva is the one who determines birth. Therefore, for the cessation of birth, the birth-worship is to be offered to Śiva. ॥86॥
1.16.87: The whole world, moving and unmoving, consists of bindu and nāda. Bindu is Śakti, nāda is Śiva; the world consists of Śiva and Śakti. ॥87॥
1.16.88: This bindu has nāda as its support; this world has bindu as its support. Bindu and nāda stand firmly as the support of the world. ॥88॥
1.16.89: Everything joined with bindu and nāda becomes sakalīkaraṇa (the making-whole). From this sakalīkaraṇa the world undoubtedly attains birth. ॥89॥
1.16.90: The liṅga, consisting of bindu and nāda, is called the cause of the world. Bindu is the Goddess, nāda is Śiva; their union is called the Śivaliṅga. ॥90॥
1.16.91: Therefore, for the cessation of birth, one should worship the Śivaliṅga. The Goddess in the form of bindu is the mother; Śiva in the form of nāda is the father. ॥91॥
1.16.92: When the parents are worshipped there is supreme bliss indeed. To obtain supreme bliss one should worship the Śivaliṅga. ॥92॥
1.16.93: That Goddess is the mother of the worlds, that Śiva is the father of the world. For one who constantly serves the parents, their compassion grows ever greater. ॥93॥
1.16.94: Out of compassion Śiva grants the worshipper inner sovereignty. Therefore, O best of sages, to gain inner bliss— ॥94॥
1.16.95: —one should worship the Śivaliṅga as the form of father and mother. Bharga is said to be of the form of Puruṣa, and Bhargā is said to be Prakṛti. ॥95॥
1.16.96: The womb whose inner abode is unmanifest is called Puruṣa; the womb whose inner abode is clearly manifest is called Prakṛti. ॥96॥
1.16.97: Puruṣa is the primal womb, since he, possessing the womb, is the begetter. What is joined from Puruṣa into Prakṛti is called the first birth. ॥97॥
1.16.98: Its emergence into manifestation from Prakṛti is called the second birth. The creature obtains birth—a birth bound to death—from Puruṣa. ॥98॥
1.16.99: That which is necessarily brought into being from another through māyā is called birth. Because it decays from the time of birth, it is known as jīva. ॥99॥
1.16.100: It is born and stretched out (bound) by fetters—this is the very meaning of the word jīva. For the removal of the fetters of birth, one should worship the birth-liṅga. ॥100॥
1.16.101: From the sense bha, that is, it goes to growth, Prakṛti is called bhaga. Because of the enjoyment, by the natural senses, of natural objects such as the subtle element of sound— ॥101॥
1.16.102: —'this belongs to bhaga, hence bhoga (enjoyment)': this is the meaning of the word chiefly heard in scripture. The principal bhaga is Prakṛti; Śiva is called Bhagavān. ॥102॥
1.16.103: Bhagavān is the giver of enjoyment; there is no other bestower of enjoyment. Being the lord of bhaga, Bhagavān is called Bharga by the wise. ॥103॥
1.16.104: The liṅga accompanied by the bhaga, the bhaga united with the liṅga—for enjoyment here and hereafter, and for everlasting enjoyment— ॥104॥
1.16.105: —one should worship the Śivaliṅga, Bhagavān Mahādeva. The Sun is the progenitor of the world; its sign arises from procreation. ॥105॥
1.16.106: A man should worship, in the liṅga, the bearer of the liṅga who is the maker of procreation. The sign which conveys the meaning of the liṅga is called liṅga. ॥106॥
1.16.107: It is called liṅga because it makes known the meaning, namely Puruṣa, Śiva. And the union of the emblems of Śiva and Śakti is called the liṅga. ॥107॥
1.16.108: Śiva being pleased by the worship of his own emblem, the effect of the emblem does not proceed. The effect of the emblem is birth and the like; thus birth and what follows cease. ॥108॥
1.16.109: With natural and personal offerings, arising from outer and inner means, and with the sixteen upacāras, one should worship the Śivaliṅga. ॥109॥
1.16.110: Thus worship on Sunday ends birth. On Sunday one should worship the great liṅga with the praṇava alone. ॥110॥
1.16.111: On Sunday ablution with the five cow-products is especially recommended. Cow-dung, cow-urine, milk, curd and ghee form the pañcagavya. ॥111॥
1.16.112: Ablution with milk and the rest also separately, with honey and with sugarcane juice; and one should make a food-offering of cooked rice with cow's milk, with the praṇava alone. ॥112॥
1.16.113: The praṇava is the sound-liṅga; the nāda-liṅga is that of the Self-born; the bindu-liṅga is the yantra; the syllable m is the installed liṅga. ॥113॥
1.16.114: The letter u is the movable liṅga; the letter a is the embodied form of the guru. Through constant worship of the six liṅgas one is liberated while living—there is no doubt. ॥114॥
1.16.115: Worship of Śiva with devotion brings men release from birth. By wearing rudrākṣa one gains a quarter, by wearing sacred ash a half, ॥115॥
1.16.116: three quarters by repeating the mantra, and through worship one becomes full of devotion. Having worshipped the Śivaliṅga and the devotee, a man attains liberation. ॥116॥
1.16.117: Whoever reads this chapter or listens to it attentively—his devotion to Śiva grows very firm, O brahmins. ॥117॥
1.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The method of worship of the earthen liṅga and other matters, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
1.17.1: The sages said: O great sage, O lord, tell us in due order the greatness of the Praṇava, of the sixfold liṅga, and the worship due to a devotee of Śiva. ॥1॥
1.17.2: Sūta said: This question has been well put by you who are rich in austerity. Mahādeva knows its answer, and no one else. ॥2॥
1.17.3: Even so, I shall explain it, solely through the grace of Śiva. May Śiva grant abundant protection to us and to you. ॥3॥
1.17.4: Pra refers to the great ocean of saṃsāra born of Prakṛti; nava means a new boat to cross it — thus the wise understand the Praṇava. ॥4॥
1.17.5: Pra is the phenomenal world (prapañca); na — for you it does not exist: so they understand the Praṇava. Because it leads you eminently (prakarṣeṇa) to liberation, they understand it as Praṇava. ॥5॥
1.17.6: For yogins who repeat their own mantra and who worship, having brought about the destruction of all karma, it bestows a divine knowledge that is new. ॥6॥
1.17.7: That knower alone, free from māyā, they call new; the Praṇava makes the great soul eminently new, of pure nature. ॥7॥
1.17.8: Because it makes him new, the wise know it as Praṇava. The Praṇava is said to be twofold, by the distinction of subtle and gross. ॥8॥
1.17.9: One should know the subtle as the single-syllabled Oṃ; the gross they know as the five-syllabled mantra. The subtle has its five letters unmanifest; the other has its letters clearly manifest. ॥9॥
1.17.10: The subtle Praṇava, the essence of all, is for the one liberated while living, for whom it is truly beneficial; he should practise contemplation of its meaning through the mantra until the dissolution of his body. ॥10॥
1.17.11: When his body falls away, he certainly attains the complete Śiva. But one who merely repeats the mantra certainly attains yoga. ॥11॥
1.17.12: One who repeats it thirty-six crore times will certainly attain yoga. The subtle Praṇava too should be known as twofold, by the distinction of short and long. ॥12॥
1.17.13: The letter A, the letter U, and after that the letter M, joined with bindu and nāda, endowed with sound, time and kalā — ॥13॥
1.17.14: — this is the long Praṇava, which abides only in the hearts of yogins. The M, embodying the three principles, is called the short Praṇava. ॥14॥
1.17.15: Śiva, Śakti and their union — the M has this threefold nature. Thus the short Praṇava is to be repeated by those who seek the destruction of all sins. ॥15॥
1.17.16: Earth, wind, fire (kanaka), water and sky, and likewise sound and the rest — these are ten; those bound by desire for these ten are called the pravṛtta (worldly-active). ॥16॥
1.17.17: The short Praṇava is for the pravṛtta, the long for the nivṛtta (renouncers). At the beginning of the vyāhṛtis and of mantras, it is used as desired, endowed with sound and kalā. ॥17॥
1.17.18: It should be employed at the beginning of the Veda and in the worship at the two twilights. Having done nine crore repetitions, a man becomes thoroughly purified. ॥18॥
1.17.19: Again, with nine crore more, he gains mastery over earth; and again with nine crore, he gains mastery over the waters. ॥19॥
1.17.20: Again with nine crore he gains mastery over fire; again with nine crore he gains mastery over wind; and with nine crore repetitions he attains mastery over ether. ॥20॥
1.17.21: Mastery over smell and the other sense-objects in due order, each with nine crore repetitions; and again over ego (ahaṅkāra) with nine crore repetitions. ॥21॥
1.17.22: By repeating the mantra a thousand times daily, a man becomes ever pure. Beyond that, O twice-born, the repetition serves for one's own perfection. ॥22॥
1.17.23: Thus, again, having repeated the Praṇava one hundred and eight crore times, one awakened by it attains pure yoga. ॥23॥
1.17.24: United with pure yoga, he is liberated while living, without doubt — always repeating, always meditating on Śiva in the form of the Praṇava. ॥24॥
1.17.25: Established in samādhi, the great yogin is Śiva himself, without doubt. Having placed (nyāsa) the ṛṣi, metre, deity and the rest on the body, one should then repeat the mantra. ॥25॥
1.17.26: Having placed the Praṇava together with the mātṛkā letters on the body, one becomes a ṛṣi; one obtains the entire fruit of nyāsa, such as that of the ten mātṛs, the six paths and the rest. ॥26॥
1.17.27: For the worldly-engaged and those of mixed disposition, the gross Praṇava is prescribed. Śiva-yogins are of three kinds, engaged respectively in ritual action, austerity and repetition. ॥27॥
1.17.28: One who is engaged in ritual worship with wealth and other resources, with the limbs such as the hands, and with salutations and the like, is called a kriyā-yogin. ॥28॥
1.17.29: One who is engaged in worship, eats moderately, has conquered the outer senses, and is free from harming others and the like, is called a tapo-yogin. ॥29॥
1.17.30: One endowed with these, always pure, free from all desires and the like, always devoted to repetition and tranquil — him they know as a japa-yogin. ॥30॥
1.17.31: By worshipping Śiva-yogins with the sixteen offerings (upacāras), a man becomes pure and attains liberation in the order of sālokya and the rest. ॥31॥
1.17.32: Now I shall describe japa-yoga; listen, O twice-born, as I speak. Japa is declared the means for one who practises austerity, for by repeating the mantra he purifies himself. ॥32॥
1.17.33: The name of Śiva in the dative, preceded by namaḥ, comprising five principles — that, O twice-born, is Śiva's five-syllabled mantra, the form of the gross Praṇava. ॥33॥
1.17.34: By repetition of the five-syllabled mantra alone a man obtains every perfection. One should always repeat the five-syllabled mantra joined at the beginning with the Praṇava. ॥34॥
1.17.35: Having received the teacher's instruction, dwelling in a comfortable abode on good ground, beginning in the bright fortnight and continuing until the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, O twice-born — ॥35॥
1.17.36: Māgha and Bhādrapada are especially distinguished, the very best of all times. Eating moderately once a day, restrained in speech, with senses controlled, ॥36॥
1.17.37: he should daily render service to his own parents, to the king and to the ancestors. By a thousand repetitions alone he becomes pure; otherwise he remains a debtor. ॥37॥
1.17.38: He should repeat the five-syllabled mantra five lakh times, meditating on Śiva — seated in the lotus posture, the giver of welfare, adorned with the Gaṅgā and the crescent moon, ॥38॥
1.17.39: resplendent with Śakti seated on his left thigh and with the great gaṇas, the god holding the deer and the axe, his hands showing the gestures granting boons and fearlessness, ॥39॥
1.17.40: meditating on Sadāśiva, the ever-gracious, having first worshipped him mentally, in the heart or in the orb of the sun. ॥40॥
1.17.41: Facing east and performing pure rites, one should repeat the five-syllabled vidyā. In the morning of the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, after completing the daily rites, ॥41॥
1.17.42: in a pleasant, clean place, self-controlled and pure in mind, one should repeat the five-syllabled mantra twelve thousand times. ॥42॥
1.17.43: He should invite excellent Śaiva brāhmaṇas together with their wives, and choose one cultured, eminent guru as the embodiment of Śiva with Ambā (Sāmba), ॥43॥
1.17.44: and five excellent twice-born devotees of Śiva representing Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva and Sadyojāta. ॥44॥
1.17.45: Having procured the materials of worship, he should begin the worship of Śiva; and having performed Śiva's worship according to rule, he should begin the homa. ॥45॥
1.17.46: Having performed the preliminaries up to the mukha rite according to his own sūtra, he should perform the homa—eleven, or one hundred and one, or one thousand and one oblations. ॥46॥
1.17.47: He should offer them himself, with ghee from a tawny cow only; or the wise man may have Śiva's devotees offer one hundred and eight. ॥47॥
1.17.48: At the end of the homa the sacrificial fee should be given, and likewise a pair of cows to the guru, regarding those brāhmaṇas as the forms of Īśāna and the rest, and the guru as Sāmba (Śiva with Ambā). ॥48॥
1.17.49: He should bathe his own head with the water that has sprinkled their feet; he at once obtains the fruit of bathing in thirty-six crores of holy places. ॥49॥
1.17.50: He should give them, with devotion, food of ten ingredients; and honour the guru's wife with the thought of her as Parā (the Supreme Goddess), and the others' wives in the order of Īśāna and the rest, ॥50॥
1.17.51: having worshipped them with sweet rice-pudding, as lavishly as his means allow, beginning with rudrākṣas and garments, along with vaṭakas and cakes, ॥51॥
1.17.52: Then, having made the bali offering, he should hold an abundant feeding. Then, having prayed to the Lord of the gods, he should thus conclude the japa. ॥52॥
1.17.53: Having performed the puraścaraṇa in this way, a man becomes a master of the mantra. Further, by five lakhs of repetitions all his sins are destroyed. ॥53॥
1.17.54: Beginning from Atala up to Satyaloka in succession, by each five lakhs of japa one attains the lordship of each of those worlds. ॥54॥
1.17.55: If he dies midway, at the end of his enjoyment he is born on earth as a repeater of that mantra. Again, by five lakhs he attains nearness (sāmīpya) to Brahmā. ॥55॥
1.17.56: Again, by five lakhs he attains the lordship of sameness of form (sārūpya). Altogether, by a hundred lakhs he becomes directly equal to Brahmā. ॥56॥
1.17.57: Having thus attained union (sāyujya) with the effected (kārya) Brahmā, he enjoys pleasures as he wishes, as that Brahmā, until the dissolution. ॥57॥
1.17.58: Again, when another kalpa has begun, he is born as a son of Brahmā; and again, shining through austerity, he will gradually be liberated. ॥58॥
1.17.59: The worlds were created in succession from the effected elements beginning with earth: from Pātāla up to Satya are the fourteen worlds of Brahmā. ॥59॥
1.17.60: Above Satya, up to Kṣamā, are the fourteen worlds of Viṣṇu. In the Kṣamā world, in Vaikuṇṭha, the excellent city, the effected (kārya) Viṣṇu ॥60॥
1.17.61: presides there, enjoying great delights with the effected Lakṣmī and providing protection. Above that are situated twenty-eight worlds ending with Śuci. ॥61॥
1.17.62: In the Śuci world, in Kailāsa, dwells Rudra, the destroyer of beings. Above that are fifty-six worlds ending with Ahiṃsā. ॥62॥
1.17.63: Occupying the Ahiṃsā world, in the city of Jñāna-Kailāsa, the effected Lord (Kāryeśvara) presides, having brought about the concealment of all. ॥63॥
1.17.64: At its end is the wheel of time (Kālacakra); beyond that is what transcends time. There Kāla, called Cakreśvara, is presided over by Śiva. ॥64॥
1.17.65: Mounted on Dharma in the form of a buffalo, he yokes all with time. Untruth, impurity, violence and mercilessness— ॥65॥
1.17.66: this buffalo has the four feet of untruth and the rest; it is complete in all parts, assumes forms at will, has the splendour of unbelief, evil company, and always the sound of what is outside the Veda, ॥66॥
1.17.67: attached to anger, black in colour, bearing the form of a great buffalo. Up to that point the Lord is called Maheśvara; the concealment extends only that far. ॥67॥
1.17.68: Below that is the enjoyment of karma; above it, the enjoyment of knowledge. Below that is the māyā of karma; above it, the māyā of knowledge. ॥68॥
1.17.69: Mā is Lakṣmī, the enjoyment of karma; that which goes (yā) to it is therefore called māyā. Mā is Lakṣmī, the enjoyment of knowledge; that which goes to it is called māyā. ॥69॥
1.17.70: Above that is eternal enjoyment; below it, they know, all is perishable. Below that is concealment; above it there is no concealment. ॥70॥
1.17.71: Below that is bondage by the noose; above it there is no bondage at all. Below that revolve those who follow desire-motivated actions. ॥71॥
1.17.72: Above that is declared the enjoyment of desireless action. Below that revolve those devoted to the worship of the bindu. ॥72॥
1.17.73: Desireless worshippers of the liṅga go above it. Below that revolve worshippers of gods and asuras other than Śiva. ॥73॥
1.17.74: Those who are devoted solely to Śiva go beyond it. Below that is the class of individual souls (jīvas); above it are those of the supreme class. ॥74॥
1.17.75: Below that are the worldly ones; those who go above it are indeed the liberated. Below that revolve worshippers using material (prākṛta) substances. ॥75॥
1.17.76: Those who worship with substances of the Puruṣa (spiritual) go above it. Below that is the liṅga of Śakti; above it, the liṅga of Śiva. ॥76॥
1.17.77: Below that the liṅga is covered; above it, it is formless. Below that the liṅga is fashioned; above it, it is not fashioned. ॥77॥
1.17.78: Below that is the external liṅga; above it, the inner one. Below that are the worlds of Śakti, one hundred and twelve in number. ॥78॥
1.17.79: Below that is the form of bindu; beyond it, the form of nāda. Below that is the world of karma; above it, the world of knowledge. ॥79॥
1.17.80: Above that is namaskāra (obeisance), the destroyer of pride and egoism; for from there a man does not return to birth and concealment. ॥80॥
1.17.81: Thus indeed is the meaning of the word knowledge (jñāna), because it removes concealment. Those who worship only the material (ādhibhautika) revolve in saṃsāra below that. ॥81॥
1.17.82: Only the worshippers of the spiritual (ādhyātmika) go beyond that. That much indeed is the altar-portion in the liṅga which is the self of the great world. ॥82॥
1.17.83: The eightfold bond beginning with prakṛti is also known as established there. In this way all such things, worldly and Vedic, should be understood. ॥83॥
1.17.84: Those who are endowed with dharma beginning with truth, and those who are devoted to the worship of Śiva, cross the wheel of time mounted on the buffalo of adharma. ॥84॥
1.17.85: Above that is Dharma as the bull, bearing the form of brahmacarya, endowed with the feet of truth and the rest, standing in front of Śivaloka. ॥85॥
1.17.86: The bull has forbearance as its horns, tranquillity as its ears; it is adorned with the sound of the Vedas, has faith (āstikya) as its eyes, and breath, the guru, intellect and mind as its other faculties. ॥86॥
1.17.87: The bulls beginning with action (kriyā) should always be known to stand in the causal worlds and the rest. The One beyond time presides over that Dharma, the bull of action. ॥87॥
1.17.88: The lifespan of each of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa is called one day. Above that there is no day, no night, no birth, death and the like. ॥88॥
1.17.89: Again, likewise the worlds of the causal Brahmā, ending with the causal Satya-loka, are always fashioned above that from the elements beginning with smell. ॥89॥
1.17.90: These fourteen worlds exist, having the nature of subtle smell. Again, fourteen worlds of the causal Viṣṇu exist. ॥90॥
1.17.91: Again, the worlds of the causal Rudra are held to be twenty-eight; and again, those of the causal Īśa, lying above that, are fifty-six. ॥91॥
1.17.92: Beyond that is the world called Brahmacarya-loka, approved by Śiva. There, in the Jñāna-Kailāsa endowed with five enclosures, ॥92॥
1.17.93: there indeed is the primal liṅga, endowed with five maṇḍalas, possessed of the kalās of the five Brahmans, and united with the Primal Śakti. ॥93॥
1.17.94: This is declared to be the abode of Śiva, the Supreme Self. There itself dwells the Supreme Lord, united with the Supreme Śakti, ॥94॥
1.17.95: Creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment and grace — he is expert in these five acts, his form being being-consciousness-bliss. ॥95॥
1.17.96: He whose dharma is ever meditation, who is ever intent on grace, seated in the posture of samādhi, delighting in his own Self, shines there. ॥96॥
1.17.97: The vision of him is to be attained gradually through ritual action, meditation and the like. By performing the daily and other rites, the mind becomes inclined toward Śiva's rites. ॥97॥
1.17.98: Through Śiva's rites beginning with kriyā one should accomplish knowledge of Śiva. All who have attained his vision are surely liberated; there is no doubt. ॥98॥
1.17.99: Liberation is indeed nothing but delighting in one's own Self, in the form of the Self. One well-established in the dharmas of rite, austerity, japa, knowledge and meditation, ॥99॥
1.17.100: having gained the vision of Śiva, attains indeed the state of delighting in his own Self. Just as the sun with its own rays removes impurity, ॥100॥
1.17.101: so Śambhu, skilled in compassion, removes ignorance. When ignorance ceases, knowledge of Śiva arises. ॥101॥
1.17.102: Through knowledge of Śiva one attains one's own true nature, delight in the Self. When delight in the Self is perfected, a man has accomplished all that is to be done. ॥102॥
1.17.103: And again, by a hundred lakhs of japa one would attain the position of Brahmā; and again, by a hundred lakhs one would attain the position of Viṣṇu. ॥103॥
1.17.104: And again, by a hundred lakhs one would attain the position of Rudra; and again, by a hundred lakhs one would attain the position of Lordship (aiśvarya). ॥104॥
1.17.105: And again, well-concentrated, by japa of just this kind one would attain the wheel of time which forms the beginning of Śivaloka and the rest. ॥105॥
1.17.106: The wheel of time is a fivefold wheel, each one successively higher. Creation and delusion form Brahmā's wheel; enjoyment and delusion form Viṣṇu's. ॥106॥
1.17.107: Anger and delusion form Rudra's wheel; wandering they know as Īśvara's; knowledge and delusion form Śiva's wheel. The wise know these as the five wheels. ॥107॥
1.17.108: And again, by ten crores of japa one attains the position of the causal Brahmā; and again, by ten crores one would attain the lordship of that position. ॥108॥
1.17.109: Thus, having successively obtained the position of the mighty Viṣṇu and the others, and having successively obtained the lordship of that position of the great-souled one, ॥109॥
1.17.110: having untiringly repeated the mantra a hundred and five crores of times, one attains Śivaloka, outside the fifth enclosure. ॥110॥
1.17.111: There is a rājasa pavilion, the excellent abode of Nandin; and right there the bull in the form of austerity is seen. ॥111॥
1.17.112: That place of Sadyojāta is the excellent fifth enclosure; and the place of Vāmadeva, further, is the fourth enclosure. ॥112॥
1.17.113: Next, the abode of Aghora is the excellent third enclosure; the auspicious second enclosure belongs to Tatpuruṣa, Śiva with Ambā (Sāmba). ॥113॥
1.17.114: Then the first enclosure belongs to the supreme Īśāna. Then the place of the dharma of meditation is the fifth pavilion. ॥114॥
1.17.115: There is the abode of Balinātha, bestowing the full nectar. Next is the fourth pavilion, containing the image of Candraśekhara. ॥115॥
1.17.116: The place of Somaskanda is the excellent third pavilion. The faithful call the second pavilion the dance-pavilion. ॥116॥
1.17.117: The first pavilion there is the beautiful place of Mūlamāyā. Beyond that is the sanctum, the supremely auspicious place of the liṅga. ॥117॥
1.17.118: Beyond Nandin's abode, people do not know Śiva's glory. Nandīśvara, standing outside, worships the five-syllabled mantra. ॥118॥
1.17.119: Thus this knowledge was received by me through the succession of gurus and again from Nandīśa. Beyond that is self-knowable, experienced only through Śiva. ॥119॥
1.17.120: Only by Śiva's grace directly can the glory of Śivaloka be known by all, and not otherwise — so say the faithful. ॥120॥
1.17.121: Thus, stage by stage, Brāhmaṇas who have conquered their senses become liberated. I shall also describe the procedure for others; listen attentively to me as I speak. ॥121॥
1.17.122: Through the guru's instruction, the five-syllabled mantra ending in namaḥ is to be repeated by Brāhmaṇas; one should repeat it five lakh times for long life — this is the rule. ॥122॥
1.17.123: To remove womanhood, a woman should again repeat it five lakh times; having become a man through the mantra, the wise one gradually becomes liberated. ॥123॥
1.17.124: A Kṣatriya, by five lakh repetitions, will remove his Kṣatriya-hood; and again by five lakh, the Kṣatriya becomes a Brāhmaṇa. ॥124॥
1.17.125: Through repetition comes perfection in the mantra, and the man gradually becomes liberated. A Vaiśya, by five lakh repetitions, will remove his Vaiśya-hood; ॥125॥
1.17.126: again by five lakh he is called a mantra-Kṣatriya; and again by five lakh he will remove Kṣatriya-hood; ॥126॥
1.17.127: and again by five lakh he is called a mantra-Brāhmaṇa. And a Śūdra, through the mantra ending in namaḥ, by twenty-five lakh repetitions, ॥127॥
1.17.128: attaining the status of a mantra-Brāhmaṇa, afterwards becomes a purified twice-born. Whether woman or man, Brāhmaṇa or anyone else, ॥128॥
1.17.129: one in distress should always repeat the mantra either ending with namaḥ or with namaḥ placed first. In this matter, for women, the guru, having reasoned it out likewise, should show the procedure in due order. ॥129॥
1.17.130: At the completion of five lakh repetitions, the practitioner, solely for Śiva's pleasure, should perform a great ablution and food-offering and should worship the devotees. ॥130॥
1.17.131: By the worship of Śiva's devotee, Śiva becomes more pleased. There is no difference between Śiva and Śiva's devotee; he is indeed Śiva. ॥131॥
1.17.132: By holding the mantra which is Śiva's own form, he is indeed Śiva himself. Toward Śiva present in the body of Śiva's devotee one should be wholly devoted. ॥132॥
1.17.133: Śiva's devotees know all rites, the whole of Vedic ritual. To whatever extent the Śiva mantra has been repeated progressively by someone, ॥133॥
1.17.134: to that extent is Śiva's presence in that body; there is no doubt. Likewise, the form of a woman devoted to Śiva becomes the emblem (liṅga) of the Goddess. ॥134॥
1.17.135: As much as she repeats the mantra of the Goddess, so much is the Goddess's presence in her. The wise one, himself partaking of the form of sound, should worship Śiva fully. ॥135॥
1.17.136: And having himself become Śiva, he should worship the supreme Śakti. Having depicted Śakti, the image and the liṅga, he should worship them without deceit. ॥136॥
1.17.137: Regarding the Śiva-liṅga as Śiva and himself as having the form of Śakti; or regarding the Śakti-liṅga as the Goddess and himself as having the form of Śiva; ॥137॥
1.17.138: regarding the Śiva-liṅga as having the form of nāda, and Śakti as having the form of bindu, together with Śakti — liṅgas mutually united in the relation of subordinate and principal — ॥138॥
1.17.139: he should worship Śiva and Śakti; through meditation on the root mantra he is Śiva. Śiva's devotees, who embody the Śiva mantra and bear Śiva's form, ॥139॥
1.17.140: he should worship with the sixteen services; he will obtain what he desires. The learned one who, by service and the like, gives a Śiva devotee bearing the liṅga ॥140॥
1.17.141: joy — the learned one who produces such joy, Śiva becomes more pleased with him. Śiva's devotees together with their wives, the worshipper with his own wife should always ॥141॥
1.17.142: worship with food and the like — five, or ten, or a hundred. One who is without deceit in wealth, body, mantra and contemplation, ॥142॥
1.17.143: worshipping them as embodiments of Śiva and Śakti, is not born again on earth. Below the navel is Brahmā's portion; up to the throat is Viṣṇu's portion; ॥143॥
1.17.144: the face is the liṅga — thus is the body of Śiva's devotee declared. For the dead, whether they received cremation and other rites or the dead lacking cremation and other rites, ॥144॥
1.17.145: on their behalf one should worship Śiva himself, the primal Father; having also performed worship of the primal Mother, one should worship Śiva's devotees. ॥145॥
1.17.146: The deceased, reaching the world of the ancestors, gradually becomes liberated. One devoted to austerity excels ten devoted to rites; ॥146॥
1.17.147: one devoted to japa excels hundreds devoted to austerity; a knower of Śiva excels thousands devoted to japa; ॥147॥
1.17.148: among lakhs of knowers of Śiva, one devoted to meditation excels; one established in samādhi excels crores of those devoted to meditation. ॥148॥
1.17.149: Because of their successively higher excellence, in worshipping them the fruit is successively higher, of the nature of excellence, and hard to comprehend even for the wise. ॥149॥
1.17.150: Therefore, what man knows the greatness of Śiva's devotee? The worship of Śiva and Śakti and the worship of Śiva's devotee — ॥150॥
1.17.151: the man who performs these with devotion becomes Śiva and prospers in auspiciousness. Whoever reads this chapter, full of meaning and in accord with the Veda, ॥151॥
1.17.152: that Brāhmaṇa becomes a knower of Śiva and rejoices together with Śiva. O lords of sages, one who knows its special significance should make Śiva's devotees hear it; ॥152॥
1.17.153: for him there would be the attainment of Śiva's favour, through Śiva's compassion, O wise ones. ॥153॥
1.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the praṇava and of the five-syllabled mantra, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
1.18.1: The sages said: O best knower of all meanings, tell us the nature of bondage and liberation. Sūta said: I shall describe bondage, liberation, and likewise the means to it; listen attentively. ॥1॥
1.18.2: The jīva bound by the eightfold bond beginning with prakṛti is called bound; freed from the eightfold bond beginning with prakṛti, he is called liberated. ॥2॥
1.18.3: Bringing prakṛti and the rest under control is in itself called liberation. The bound soul, once freed, is called the liberated soul. ॥3॥
1.18.4: Prakṛti first, then buddhi, ahaṅkāra consisting of the guṇas, and the five tanmātras — this they know as the group of eight beginning with prakṛti. ॥4॥
1.18.5: The body is born of the eight beginning with prakṛti; action is said to be born of the body; and again the body is born of action — thus birth and action occur again and again. ॥5॥
1.18.6: The body should be known as threefold: gross, subtle and causal. The gross is said to provide activity; the subtle provides the enjoyment of the senses. ॥6॥
1.18.7: The causal body is for the experience of the self, in accordance with the jīva's karma. Through actions of merit and sin the jīva reaps the fruit, happiness and sorrow. ॥7॥
1.18.8: Therefore, bound by the rope of karma, the jīva is ever whirled again and again like a wheel by the three bodies and karma. ॥8॥
1.18.9: To stop the whirling of the wheel, one should praise the maker of the wheel. The great wheel begins with prakṛti; Śiva is beyond prakṛti. ॥9॥
1.18.10: Maheśa is the maker of the wheel, since he is beyond prakṛti. Just as a child drinks or spits out water at will, ॥10॥
1.18.11: so Śiva, having brought prakṛti and the rest under control, presides over them. Because all is brought under his control, therefore he is known as Śiva. Śiva alone is omniscient, perfectly full and free of desire. ॥11॥
1.18.12: Omniscience, contentment, beginningless awareness, independence, ever-undiminished power and infinite power belong to Maheśvara — this the Veda knows as his mental sovereignty. ॥12॥
1.18.13: Therefore by Śiva's grace prakṛti and the rest come under control. To obtain Śiva's grace, one should worship Śiva alone. ॥13॥
1.18.14: How can there be worship of him who is desireless and full? Action done with Śiva as its aim produces grace. ॥14॥
1.18.15: One should worship, with Śiva in view, in the liṅga, in an image, or in a devotee; one should worship with body, mind, speech and wealth too. ॥15॥
1.18.16: Through worship, Maheśa, Śiva supreme beyond prakṛti, truly bestows grace, especially on the worshipper. ॥16॥
1.18.17: By Śiva's grace, karma and the rest gradually come under one's own control. When everything, from karma up to prakṛti, comes under control, ॥17॥
1.18.18: then he is called liberated and shines, delighting in his own Self. When, by the grace of the Supreme Lord, the karma-body is under control, ॥18॥
1.18.19: then dwelling in Śiva's world is called sālokya. And when the tanmātras have come under control, one attains nearness (sāmīpya) to Sāmba, Śiva with Ambā. ॥19॥
1.18.20: Then comes union with Śiva, with his weapons and the like and his activities and so on. And on gaining great grace, the intellect too comes under control. ॥20॥
1.18.21: The intellect is an effect of prakṛti; that state is called sārṣṭi. Again, by great grace, prakṛti will come under control. ॥21॥
1.18.22: Then Śiva's mental sovereignty will be his without effort. Having gained Śiva's sovereignty beginning with omniscience, he shines in his own Self. ॥22॥
1.18.23: Those devoted to the Vedas and Āgamas call that sāyujya. Thus, step by step, liberation comes of itself through worship in the liṅga and the like. ॥23॥
1.18.24: Therefore, for Śiva's grace, one should worship Śiva with rites and the like: rites for Śiva, austerity for Śiva, constant japa of Śiva's mantra, ॥24॥
1.18.25: knowledge of Śiva and meditation on Śiva — one should practise these, each higher than the last. Until sleep, until death, one should pass the time in thought of Śiva. ॥25॥
1.18.26: He who worships Śiva with the Sadyojāta and other mantras and with flowers will attain Śiva. The sages said: O you of good vows, tell us the procedure of Śiva-worship in the liṅga and the like. ॥26॥
1.18.27: Sūta said: I shall tell the order of the liṅgas; listen properly, O twice-born. The first liṅga is the praṇava itself, which fulfils all desires. ॥27॥
1.18.28: The subtle form is the subtle praṇava, and the subtle form is partless (niṣkala). The gross liṅga is with parts (sakala); it is called the five-syllabled mantra. ॥28॥
1.18.29: Worship of these two is called austerity; both directly grant liberation. And there are very many liṅgas arising from puruṣa and prakṛti. ॥29॥
1.18.30: Śiva knows how to describe them in detail, and no one else. I shall declare to you the known liṅgas that are modifications of earth. ॥30॥
1.18.31: The Svayambhū liṅga is first, the Bindu liṅga second, then the Pratiṣṭhita and the Cara, and the Guru liṅga is the fifth. ॥31॥
1.18.32: Pleased by the austerity of gods and sages, for the sake of his presence there, Śarva, lying within the earth as a seed in the form of nāda, ॥32॥
1.18.33: breaking through the ground like the sprout of a plant, becomes manifest. Because it is born self-existent, they know it as Svayambhū. ॥33॥
1.18.34: By worship of that liṅga, knowledge increases of its own accord. On gold, silver and the like, or on the earth, or on a prepared ground, ॥34॥
