1.18.35: a liṅga drawn with one's own hand, bearing the pure praṇava mantra — having drawn such a yantra-liṅga, one should perform installation and invocation. ॥35॥
1.18.36: The liṅga consisting of bindu and nāda, whether fixed or movable — this is made of mental contemplation and is seen by Śiva; there is no doubt. ॥36॥
1.18.37: Wherever Śambhu is trusted in, there he grants the fruit to that person. In a yantra drawn with one's own hand, or in a natural, fixed object and the like, ॥37॥
1.18.38: having invoked Śambhu, one should worship him with the sixteen services. One attains sovereignty oneself, and knowledge arises through practice. ॥38॥
1.18.39: That liṅga which was made by gods and sages, for their own spiritual accomplishment, with mantra and by their own hand, in a pure maṇḍala, … ॥39॥
1.18.40: A liṅga installed with pure devotion is excellent. They call that liṅga pauruṣa, and it is said to be pauruṣa-installed. ॥40॥
1.18.41: By constant worship of that liṅga one would obtain pauruṣa lordship. Liṅgas installed by great brāhmaṇas and by kings of great wealth as well… ॥41॥
1.18.42: A liṅga fashioned by a craftsman and installed with mantra—that installed liṅga is prākṛta, granting enjoyment of prākṛta lordship. ॥42॥
1.18.43: That which is powerful and lasting is called pauruṣa; that which is weak and transient is called prākṛta. ॥43॥
1.18.44: The genital organ, the navel, the tongue, the tip of the nose and the crown-tuft, in order—located in the three worlds of the body beginning with the hips—constitute the spiritual (ādhyātmika), moving liṅga. ॥44॥
1.18.45: A mountain is declared pauruṣa; the surface of the earth they know as prākṛta. Trees and the like are to be known as pauruṣa; shrubs and the like they know as prākṛta. ॥45॥
1.18.46: Ṣāṣṭika rice is to be known as prākṛta; śāli rice and wheat as pauruṣa. One should know as pauruṣa the lordship that bestows the eight siddhis beginning with aṇimā. ॥46॥
1.18.47: Objects such as good wives and wealth the faithful call prākṛta. First among the moving liṅgas is declared the rasaliṅga (mercury liṅga). ॥47॥
1.18.48: The rasaliṅga would grant all desires to brāhmaṇas; the auspicious bāṇaliṅga grants great kingship to kṣatriyas. ॥48॥
1.18.49: The golden liṅga for vaiśyas grants mastery of great wealth; the auspicious stone liṅga for śūdras brings great purification. ॥49॥
1.18.50: The crystal liṅga and the bāṇaliṅga grant all wishes to everyone. In the absence of one's own, using another's is not forbidden in worship. ॥50॥
1.18.51: For women the earthen liṅga is prescribed, especially for those whose husbands are living; for widows engaged in worldly life the crystal one is declared. ॥51॥
1.18.52: For widows who have renounced, the rasaliṅga is preferred. Whether in childhood, youth or old age, O you of good vows, ॥52॥
1.18.53: a liṅga of pure crystal grants women all enjoyments. For those engaged in worldly life, worship of the pedestal grants all desires on earth. ॥53॥
1.18.54: The one engaged in worldly life should perform all worship with a vessel; after the ablution he should make the food offering with cooked śāli rice. ॥54॥
1.18.55: At the end of worship he should place the liṅga in caskets in a separate room. Renunciants who worship the liṅga on the hand should offer their own food. ॥55॥
1.18.56: For renunciants the supreme subtle liṅga alone is preferred. One should worship with sacred ash and offer sacred ash. ॥56॥
1.18.57: Having performed the worship, one should always bear that liṅga on the head. Sacred ash is declared to be threefold, by worldly, Vedic and Śiva fires. ॥57॥
1.18.58: Ash produced from worldly fire one should use for purifying substances—things made of clay, wood and metal, and grains likewise, ॥58॥
1.18.59: of substances such as sesame, and of cloth and the like likewise, and also of stale things—purification by ash is prescribed. ॥59॥
1.18.60: For things defiled by dogs and the like, too, purification by ash is prescribed. One should apply ash with water or without water, as is fitting. ॥60॥
1.18.61: Likewise, ash produced from Vedic fire one should wear at the conclusion of those rites. Produced by mantra and ritual action, the rite in the fire takes the form of ash. ॥61॥
1.18.62: By wearing that ash, the rite becomes placed upon one's own self. With the Aghora mantra, the mantra of the self, one should burn bilva wood. ॥62॥
1.18.63: That is called Śiva-fire; what is burnt by it is ash born of Śiva-fire. First the dung of a tawny cow, or simply cow-dung alone, ॥63॥
1.18.64: or śamī, aśvattha and palāśa, or vaṭa, āragvadha and bilva wood—one should burn them with Śiva-fire; that pure ash is indeed śivāgnija. ॥64॥
1.18.65: Or one should burn the wood in a fire of darbha grass, chanting the Śiva mantra; having sifted it well through cloth, one should deposit it in a new pot. ॥65॥
1.18.66: It is to be collected for radiance; it is esteemed and also worshipped. Such is the meaning of the word bhasma; Śiva did so in the beginning. ॥66॥
1.18.67: Just as a king in his realm takes the essence, which is the tax, and as men, having burnt crops and the like, enjoy the essence, ॥67॥
1.18.68: and just as the digestive fire, having burnt many and various foods, nourishes its own body with the finer essence drawn from the essence, ॥68॥
1.18.69: so too that Śiva, the Supreme Lord, though the maker of the universe, having burnt the universe over which he presides, took its essence. ॥69॥
1.18.70: Having burnt the universe, Śiva placed that ash upon himself; under the pretext of smearing ash, he took the essence of the world. ॥70॥
1.18.71: He placed his jewel in his own body: he adorned his hair with the essence of ether, his face with the essence of air, ॥71॥
1.18.72: his heart with the essence of fire, his waist with the essence of water, his knee with the essence of earth—and likewise all his limbs. ॥72॥
1.18.73: The tripuṇḍra, the essence of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the Rudras, Maheśvara wears likewise in the form of a tilaka on his forehead. ॥73॥
1.18.74: Through the growth of this ash he regards all this as himself. The entire essence of the universe has been brought under control by him alone. ॥74॥
1.18.75: Therefore there is no other who can control him; he is known as Śiva. Just as the slayer of all beasts is the beast-slayer the lion, ॥75॥
1.18.76: and there is no beast that slays him, he is therefore called siṃha (lion). Śam is eternal happiness and bliss; the letter i is held to be the Puruṣa; ॥76॥
1.18.77: the letter va is Śakti, the nectar; their union is called Śiva. Therefore, having thus made one's own self Śiva, one should worship Śiva. ॥77॥
1.18.78: Therefore one should first smear the body with ash and then wear the tripuṇḍra. At the time of worship it should be with water; for purification, without water. ॥78॥
1.18.79: Whether by day or by night, whether woman or man, one should, for worship, wear ash mixed with water in the form of the tripuṇḍra. ॥79॥
1.18.80: Whoever wears the tripuṇḍra of ash mixed with water and then performs worship, to him alone is the fruit of Śiva-worship, complete in all its parts, surely assured. ॥80॥
1.18.81: Having worn ash with Śiva's mantra, one becomes a member of the highest āśrama. He is called a Śivāśramī, because Śiva alone is supreme for him. ॥81॥
1.18.82: For one wholly devoted to the vow of Śiva there is no impurity from death nor impurity from birth. On the front of the forehead he should wear white ash, or a tilaka with clay. ॥82॥
1.18.83: Applied by one's own hand or by the guru's hand, this is the mark of Śiva's devotee. He restrains the guṇas — this is declared to be the analysis of the word guru. ॥83॥
1.18.84: He checks and removes the guṇas, rajas and the rest, together with their modifications. The supreme Śiva, who is beyond the guṇas, has taken on the form of the guru. ॥84॥
1.18.85: Because, having first removed the triad of guṇas, he awakens the disciple to Śiva, he is called the guru of trusting disciples. ॥85॥
1.18.86: Therefore, the wise know, the guru's body is the guru-liṅga, and worship of the guru-liṅga is service to the guru. ॥86॥
1.18.87: Service (śuśrūṣā) carries out what has been heard, with body, mind and speech: whatever was told earlier by the guru, whether possible or impossible, ॥87॥
1.18.88: the pure-souled one does it, even at the cost of his life and wealth. Therefore one who is fit to be instructed is called a disciple (śiṣya). ॥88॥
1.18.89: The good disciple, having given to the guru everything meant for his own body and the like, and having first offered him the first portion of cooked food, should eat with the guru's permission. ॥89॥
1.18.90: A disciple is called a son because of his constant discipleship. Having poured the semen of the mantra from the liṅga of the tongue into the womb of the ear, ॥90॥
1.18.91: the son so born is a mantra-son; he should worship the guru as his father. The begetting father plunges the son into saṃsāra, ॥91॥
1.18.92: but the guru, the father who awakens, carries him across saṃsāra. Knowing the difference between the two, one should worship the guru as father. ॥92॥
1.18.93: One should honour the guru also by bodily service and with wealth and the like earned by oneself. Since the limbs of the guru, from the feet up to the hair, are liṅgas, ॥93॥
1.18.94: one should worship them fully with offerings in the form of wealth such as sandals, with clasping of the feet and the like, with bathing, ablution and food-offerings, and with meals. ॥94॥
1.18.95: Worship of the guru is itself worship of Śiva, the supreme Self. Service to the guru, whatever it may be, all of it brings about purification of the self. ॥95॥
1.18.96: The guru's leftover is Śiva's leftover; water and things made of food and the like left by him are to be accepted and eaten by disciples who are Śiva's devotees, O brāhmaṇas. ॥96॥
1.18.97: Everything done without the guru's permission is like theft. One should diligently take as guru one who has special knowledge, superior even to an ordinary guru. ॥97॥
1.18.98: Release from ignorance is what is to be achieved, and it is the one with special knowledge who releases. At the beginning, the removal of obstacles should be done for the completion of a rite. ॥98॥
1.18.99: A rite performed without obstacles and complete in its parts becomes fruitful. Therefore at the start of all rites the wise should worship the Lord of Obstacles (Vighneśa). ॥99॥
1.18.100: For the removal of all afflictions the wise should worship all the gods. Fever and the like, tumours and diseases are considered the ādhyātmika (bodily) affliction. ॥100॥
1.18.101: On the appearance of piśācas, jackals and the like, likewise at the rising up of anthills and the like, and at the sudden falling of creatures such as lizards, ॥101॥
1.18.102: and at the sight in the house of a tortoise, a snake, a strange woman or a wicked person, and in cases of unusual births among trees, women, cows and the like, ॥102॥
1.18.103: future sorrow comes; therefore these are considered bhautika (from beings). The falling of impure things and of thunderbolts, and likewise a great plague, ॥103॥
1.18.104: epidemic fever, cholera, cattle-plague and smallpox, transits of planets into one's birth-star and planetary conjunctions in one's own rāśi, ॥104॥
1.18.105: and seeing bad dreams and the like, are considered ādhidaivika. When, through contact with a corpse, a cāṇḍāla or an outcaste, such a one has entered the inner house, ॥105॥
1.18.106: when something of this kind has arisen, a sign of future sorrow, the wise person should perform a pacificatory sacrifice (śānti-yajña) to appease that fault. ॥106॥
1.18.107: In a temple, or a cowshed, or a sacred shrine, or the courtyard of a house, on a raised altar-place two cubits in size and well adorned, ॥107॥
1.18.108: having placed rice grain amounting to one bhāra and spread it around, having drawn a lotus in the middle and likewise drawn lotuses in the directions, ॥108॥
1.18.109: having placed in the middle a great pot wound with thread and fumigated with fresh guggulu, he should likewise set pots in the directions too, ॥109॥
1.18.110: and likewise pitchers with stalked mango leaves, kūrca-bundles and the like in the eight directions; he should fill them with water purified by mantra and mixed with the five substances. ॥110॥
1.18.111: He should put in the nine gems, sapphire and the rest, in order. The wise one should engage an ācārya who knows the rite, along with his wife. ॥111॥
1.18.112: He should place in the pots golden images of Viṣṇu and of Indra and the others; in the central pot, covered with its lid, he should invoke and worship Viṣṇu. ॥112॥
1.18.113: In the east and the other directions he should worship Indra and the others in order, with their respective mantras, using each one's name in the dative ending with namaḥ, in due sequence. ॥113॥
1.18.114: He should have all the rites such as invocation performed by the ācārya himself. Together with the ācārya and the ṛtvij priests he should recite their mantras a hundred times. ॥114॥
1.18.115: At the end of the recitation he should perform a homa on the western side of the pot: ten million, a hundred thousand, a thousand, or a hundred and eight oblations, O wise ones. ॥115॥
1.18.116: He should perform it for one day, or nine days, or for a maṇḍala period, as is suitable, in accordance with time and place. ॥116॥
1.18.117: A homa with śamī wood is for pacification, and with palāśa for livelihood. He should offer oblations with substances—fuel-sticks, cooked food and ghee—with the deity's name or with the mantra. ॥117॥
1.18.118: Whatever substance was used at the beginning, he should continue it to the end of the rite. At the end, having had the puṇyāha recited, on the final day he should sprinkle all with the waters. ॥118॥
1.18.119: Afterwards he should feed brāhmaṇas, as many as the number of oblations. The ācārya and the ṛtvij priests should eat only sacrificial food, O wise ones. ॥119॥
1.18.120: Having worshipped the planets beginning with the Sun, at the very end of all the oblations one should give the officiating priests their fee, the nine gems, in due order. ॥120॥
1.18.121: Then one should perform the ten gifts, and after that the abundant gift; one should give wealth to children, to initiated students, to householders, to forest-dwellers, ॥121॥
1.18.122: to maidens, to married women, and after that to widows. All the ritual implements one should present to the preceptor. ॥122॥
1.18.123: Yama is held to be the lord of the sufferings caused by portents and plagues; therefore, to please Yama, one should have the gift of Kāla given. ॥123॥
1.18.124: One should make it with a hundred niṣkas, or else with ten niṣkas; one should fashion Kāla in human form, holding a noose and a goad. ॥124॥
1.18.125: One should make the gift of that golden image together with a fee. Then one should make a gift of sesame for securing a full span of life. ॥125॥
1.18.126: And for the removal of disease one should make the gift of ghee in which one has looked at one's reflection. One should feed a thousand brāhmaṇas, or, if poor, just a hundred. ॥126॥
1.18.127: A poor man lacking wealth should do as much as he can. For the pacification of spirits and the like, one should perform a great worship of Bhairava. ॥127॥
1.18.128: At the end one should have the great ablution and food-offering made to Śiva; afterwards one should feed brāhmaṇas in the form of a lavish feast. ॥128॥
1.18.129: By a sacrifice performed in this way one obtains pacification of faults. One should perform this pacificatory sacrifice every year in the month of Phālguna. ॥129॥
1.18.130: In case of an ill-omened sight and the like, one should perform it promptly, within a month. When a great sin or the like has befallen, one should perform the worship of Bhairava. ॥130॥
1.18.131: When a grave disease arises, one should again make the resolve and perform the rite. But a poor man lacking everything should then make a gift of lamps. ॥131॥
1.18.132: One unable even to do that should bathe and give whatever gift he can, and should bow to the Sun with a mantra a hundred and eight times. ॥132॥
1.18.133: The wise man may have the prostrations done a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand or ten million times. By the sacrifice consisting of salutation all the deities become pleased. ॥133॥
1.18.134: Contemplating thus: My intellect is offered into your own nature; it takes no delight in what is not filled by you. And the sense of I that was in us is abandoned once you are seen. ॥134॥
1.18.135: I bow down with my own body; O Lord, you are great. My own nature is not void; now I am your servant. ॥135॥
1.18.136: One should, as is fitting, perform salutation as a sacrifice of one's own self. Then, having offered food to Śiva here, one should bring betel. ॥136॥
1.18.137: One should oneself circumambulate Śiva a hundred and eight times; a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand or ten million times one may have done by another. ॥137॥
1.18.138: Through circumambulation of Śiva every sin perishes in an instant. Disease is the root of suffering, and sin is the root of disease. ॥138॥
1.18.139: It is declared that sins are dispelled only by dharma. Dharma performed with Śiva as its aim is able to remove sin. ॥139॥
1.18.140: Circumambulation is declared to be foremost among the rites of Śiva. Circumambulation is, through action, a form of japa — it is the praṇava itself. ॥140॥
1.18.141: Birth and death, the pair of opposites, is called the wheel of māyā. That wheel of Śiva's māyā is said to be the offering-pedestal (balipīṭha). ॥141॥
1.18.142: Starting from the offering-pedestal and moving clockwise, step after step, one should come back to the offering-pedestal. ॥142॥
1.18.143: Then one should make a prostration; this is called circumambulation. Going forth from the pedestal is birth attained; the bow is the offering of the self. ॥143॥
1.18.144: Thus the pair, birth and death, is offered to Śiva's māyā. One who has offered the pair to Śiva's māyā does not again become a partaker of individual selfhood. ॥144॥
1.18.145: As long as he has a body and is subject to action, that soul is called bound. Mastery over the three bodies is called liberation by the wise. ॥145॥
1.18.146: Śiva, the supreme cause, is indeed the driver of the wheel of māyā; and Śiva wipes away the pair that has been offered to Śiva's māyā. ॥146॥
1.18.147: The pair fashioned by Śiva one should offer back to him alone. Know, O wise ones, that circumambulation and prostration are exceedingly dear to Śiva. ॥147॥
1.18.148: Circumambulations and prostrations to Śiva, the supreme Self, and worship done with the sixteen services, bestow their fruit. ॥148॥
1.18.149: There is no sin on earth that cannot be destroyed by circumambulation; therefore one should destroy all sin by circumambulation alone. ॥149॥
1.18.150: Devoted to Śiva's worship, observing silence, endowed with truthfulness and other virtues, one should practise each of ritual action, austerity, japa, knowledge and meditation in turn. ॥150॥
1.18.151: Lordly power, a divine body, knowledge, destruction of ignorance, and nearness to Śiva — this is the fruit of ritual action and the rest. ॥151॥
1.18.152: By performance one attains the fruit, through the removal of darkness and the wiping away of birth, the fruits arising as though produced by the knowing intellect. ॥152॥
1.18.153: The devotee of Śiva should perform ritual action and the rest as is fitting, according to place, time, bodily capacity and wealth. ॥153॥
1.18.154: The wise man should live in a holy place of Śiva on good wealth justly earned, a livelihood free from harm to living beings and the like, and without excessive toil. ॥154॥
1.18.155: Water and food over which the five-syllable mantra has been recited they know to be wholesome. Or, they say, for a poor man alms-food becomes the giver of knowledge. ॥155॥
1.18.156: For a devotee of Śiva, alms-food increases devotion to Śiva. The alms-food of a Śiva-yogin they call Śambhu's sacrificial feast (śambhusattra). ॥156॥
1.18.157: By whatever means, wherever on earth, eating only pure food and always silent, one should not reveal the secret. ॥157॥
1.18.158: But to devotees one should reveal only the greatness of Śiva. The secret of Śiva's mantra Śiva knows, no other. ॥158॥
1.18.159: A devotee of Śiva should always dwell taking refuge in the Śiva-liṅga. By taking refuge in the liṅga of Sthāṇu alone, O brāhmaṇas, one becomes Sthāṇu. ॥159॥
1.18.160: By the worship of a movable liṅga one certainly becomes liberated, in due course. Thus everything has been told in brief: the supreme goal and the means to attain it. ॥160॥
1.18.161: This is what was formerly taught by Vyāsa and what I heard long ago. May there be good fortune for you and for us; may that devotion to Śiva be firm. ॥161॥
1.18.162: The man who always reads this chapter, or who listens to it, obtains knowledge of Śiva by Śiva's grace, O wise ones. ॥162॥
1.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of Śiva's liṅga, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
1.19.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, may you live long. You are blessed and devoted to Śiva. The glory of the liṅga, which bestows good fruit, has been well described by you. ॥1॥
1.19.2: Now tell us again that account in which the glory of the earthen liṅga of Maheśa, supreme above all, was narrated by Vyāsa. ॥2॥
1.19.3: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages, every one of you, with true devotion and reverence: the glory of Śiva's earthen liṅga is being declared by me. ॥3॥
1.19.4: Among these liṅgas that have been mentioned, the earthen liṅga is the best. O brahmins, through its worship many have attained spiritual success. ॥4॥
1.19.5: Hari, Brahmā, the sages and likewise the Prajāpatis, having duly worshipped the earthen liṅga, obtained all they desired, O twice-born ones. ॥5॥
1.19.6: Gods, asuras and humans, Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas, and many others too, having worshipped it, attained the highest success. ॥6॥
1.19.7: In the Kṛta age the liṅga made of gems is best, in the Tretā one made of gold, in the Dvāpara one of mercury is best, but in the Kali age the earthen one. ॥7॥
1.19.8: Among all the eight forms of Śiva, the earthen form is indeed the finest. O brahmins, worshipped with undivided devotion it is itself austerity; hence its fruit is great. ॥8॥
1.19.9: Just as among all gods Maheśvara is the eldest and the best, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥9॥
1.19.10: Just as among all rivers the celestial river Gaṅgā is the eldest and best, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥10॥
1.19.11: Just as among all mantras the Praṇava is regarded as great, so this earthen liṅga is the best, indeed the one to be adored and worshipped. ॥11॥
1.19.12: Just as among all classes the brahmin is said to be the best, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥12॥
1.19.13: Just as among all cities Kāśī is regarded as the very best, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥13॥
1.19.14: Just as among all vows the Śivarātri vow is supreme, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥14॥
1.19.15: Just as among all goddesses Śiva's Śakti is regarded as supreme, so among all liṅgas the earthen one is said to be the best. ॥15॥
1.19.16: Whoever, having made an earthen liṅga, worships another god—that worship becomes futile; his bathing, giving and the rest are futile. ॥16॥
1.19.17: Worship of the earthen liṅga is meritorious, auspicious and life-prolonging; it grants contentment, nourishment and prosperity, and should be performed by the best of practitioners. ॥17॥
1.19.18: Endowed with devotion and faith, one should worship the earthen liṅga, which grants the fulfilment of all desires and aims, with whatever offerings are available. ॥18॥
1.19.19: Whoever makes an earthen liṅga with an auspicious pedestal and worships it becomes wealthy and prosperous in this very life, and at the end is born as Rudra. ॥19॥
1.19.20: Hear the meritorious fruit of one who, having made an earthen liṅga, worships it with bilva at the three junctions of the day for as long as ten times eleven days. ॥20॥
1.19.21: In this very body of his he is honoured in Rudra's world; by being seen and even touched he destroys the sins of all mortals. ॥21॥
1.19.22: He is liberated while living, truly a knower, Śiva himself—there is no doubt. By merely seeing him both enjoyment and liberation arise. ॥22॥
1.19.23: Whoever worships Śiva daily throughout his whole life, having made an earthen liṅga, goes to Śiva's abode. ॥23॥
1.19.24: He dwells with Mṛḍa in Śiva's world for countless years; if he has desires, he returns again and becomes a great king in Bhārata. ॥24॥
1.19.25: One who, free of desire, worships the excellent earthen liṅga daily remains forever in Śiva's world and attains union (sāyujya) with him. ॥25॥
1.19.26: If a brahmin does not worship the earthen Śiva-liṅga, he goes to a terrible, most dreadful hell where beings are impaled on stakes. ॥26॥
1.19.27: One should have a beautiful liṅga made by whatever method; for the earthen one, one need not consider the rule of the five measuring-lines (pañcasūtra). ॥27॥
1.19.28: It must indeed be made undivided; one should not make it in separate parts. One who makes it in parts certainly does not obtain the fruit of worship. ॥28॥
1.19.29: A liṅga made of gems, of gold, of mercury, likewise of crystal, of earth, or of topaz—one should have it made undivided. ॥29॥
1.19.30: An undivided liṅga is regarded as movable, a two-part one as immovable; this distinction of divided and undivided is prescribed with regard to the movable and the immovable. ॥30॥
1.19.31: The pedestal is the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), and the liṅga is the god Maheśvara; therefore for an immovable liṅga the two-part form is regarded as best. ॥31॥
1.19.32: An immovable liṅga should be made in two parts according to rule; a mobile one is declared to be undivided by those who know the Śaiva doctrine. ॥32॥
1.19.33: Those deluded by ignorance make a movable liṅga in two parts—never the sages who know the doctrine and are learned in the scriptures. ॥33॥
1.19.34: Those foolish men who make an immovable liṅga undivided and a movable one in two parts do not share in the fruit of worship. ॥34॥
1.19.35: Therefore, by the method stated in scripture, the liṅga called movable should be made undivided, and the immovable liṅga in two parts, with the greatest joy. ॥35॥
1.19.36: Worship of an undivided movable liṅga bestows complete fruit; worship of a two-part movable one is held to bring great harm. ॥36॥
1.19.37: Worship of an undivided immovable liṅga does not bestow the desired fruit and always causes transgression—so say the knowers of scripture. ॥37॥
1.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the worship of the earthen liṅga of Śiva, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
1.20.1: Sūta said: Now the worship of the earthen liṅga for Vedic devotees is described, performed by the Vedic path alone, which bestows both enjoyment and liberation. ॥1॥
1.20.2: Having bathed according to the rule stated in the sūtras and performed the sandhyā rite as prescribed, having first done the brahmayajña, one should then perform the tarpaṇa (libations). ॥2॥
1.20.3: Having then completed all the daily duties, the man, wearing ash and rudrākṣa, proceeds with remembrance of Śiva first, ॥3॥
1.20.4: should duly worship, with supreme devotion, the excellent earthen liṅga according to the rule stated in the Veda, for the attainment of the complete fruit. ॥4॥
1.20.5: On a river bank, by a pond, on a mountain, and also in a forest, in a Śiva temple, or in a clean place, the worship of the earthen liṅga is prescribed. ॥5॥
1.20.6: Having carefully brought clay originating from a pure spot, one should fashion a Śiva-liṅga attentively, O twice-born ones. ॥6॥
1.20.7: For a brahmin white clay is prescribed, red for a kṣatriya, yellow-coloured for a vaiśya, black for a śūdra — or else whatever clay is found where one is. ॥7॥
1.20.8: Having diligently collected the clay for making the liṅga, one should place that auspicious clay in a very auspicious spot. ॥8॥
1.20.9: Having purified it with water and slowly kneaded it into a lump, an auspicious earthen liṅga should be made according to the Vedic way. ॥9॥
1.20.10: Then one should worship it with devotion to obtain the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. I shall tell the manner of it; listen to it with its procedure. ॥10॥
1.20.11: With the mantra namaḥ śivāya one should sprinkle the materials of worship, and with the mantra bhūr asi one should accomplish the consecration of the ground. ॥11॥
1.20.12: With the mantra āpo 'smān one should perform the purification of the water; with the mantra namas te rudra the sphāṭikā-bandha (protective binding) is said to be done. ॥12॥
1.20.13: With the mantra śambhavāya one should effect the purification of the site, and one should also sprinkle the pañcāmṛta with the mantra preceded by namaḥ. ॥13॥
1.20.14: With the mantra nīlagrīvāya preceded by namaḥ, the devotee should perform the excellent installation of Śaṅkara's liṅga. ॥14॥
1.20.15: Then, with devotion, with the mantra etat te rudrāva, the follower of the Vedic path should offer a beautiful seat. ॥15॥
1.20.16: With the mantra mā no mahāntam one should perform the invocation; with the mantra yā te rudra one should perform the seating. ॥16॥
1.20.17: With the mantra yām iṣum one should perform the nyāsa of Śiva, and with the mantra adhyavocat one should lovingly perform the adhivāsa (consecratory abiding). ॥17॥
1.20.18: With the mantra asau jīva one should perform the nyāsa of the deities, and with asau yo 'vasarpati one should perform the approach. ॥18॥
1.20.19: With the mantra namo 'stu nīlagrīvāya one should offer water for the feet; the arghya with the Rudra-gāyatrī, and the ācamana with the tryambaka mantra. ॥19॥
1.20.20: With the mantra payaḥ pṛthivyām one should perform the bath with milk, and with the mantra dadhikrāvṇaḥ one should have the bath with curd done. ॥20॥
1.20.21: The bath with ghee is done with the mantra ghṛtaṃ ghṛtayāvā; with the triad of verses madhu vātāḥ, madhu naktam, madhumān naḥ— ॥21॥
1.20.22: the bathing with honey and sugar is declared. Thus the pañcāmṛta is taught. Or else the bath with the pañcāmṛta may be given with the mantra for the foot-water. ॥22॥
1.20.23: With the mantra mā nas toke one should lovingly tie the waistband, or with namo dhṛṣṇave one should put on the upper garment. ॥23॥
1.20.24: With the group of four verses beginning yā te hetiḥ, the Vedic devotee should lovingly, according to rule, offer garments to Śiva. ॥24॥
1.20.25: With the verse namaḥ śvabhyaḥ the wise one should lovingly offer fragrance, and with the mantra namas takṣabhyaḥ he should offer unbroken rice grains. ॥25॥
1.20.26: With the mantra namaḥ pāryāya one should offer a flower, and with namaḥ parṇāya is made the offering of bilva leaves. ॥26॥
1.20.27: With namaḥ kapardine one should offer incense according to rule, and with the verse nama āśave one should offer a lamp as prescribed. ॥27॥
1.20.28: With the mantra namo jyeṣṭhāya one should offer excellent food (naivedya); with the mantra tryambakam the ācamana is prescribed again. ॥28॥
1.20.29: With the verse imā rudrāya one should make the offering of fruits; with the verse namo vrajyāya one should offer everything to Śambhu. ॥29॥
1.20.30: With the two mantras mā no mahāntam and then mā nas toke, one should worship the Rudras with eleven unbroken rice grains. ॥30॥
1.20.31: With the triad of verses hiraṇyagarbhaḥ one should offer the fee (dakṣiṇā); with the mantra devasya tvā the wise one should perform the ablution. ॥31॥
1.20.32: Or with the lamp mantra one should perform the rite of waving lights (nīrājana) for Śambhu, and with the triad of verses imā rudrāya one should devotedly offer a handful of flowers. ॥32॥
1.20.33: With mā no mahāntam the wise man should perform circumambulation; with the mantra mā nas toke the wise one should prostrate with all eight limbs. ॥33॥
1.20.34: With the mantra eṣa te one should display the Śiva-mudrā; with yato yataḥ the abhaya mudrā, and with the tryambaka mantra the one called jñāna. ॥34॥
1.20.35: With the mantra namaḥ senā… one should display the mahāmudrā, and with this verse namo gobhyaḥ one should show the dhenu-mudrā (cow gesture). ॥35॥
1.20.36: Having displayed the five mudrās, one should then perform japa of Śiva's mantra; the one versed in the Veda should recite with the Śatarudriya mantra. ॥36॥
1.20.37: Then the one versed in the Veda should do the recitation of the five parts (pañcāṅga), and with the mantra devā gātu… should perform the dismissal (visarjana) of Śambhu. ॥37॥
1.20.38: Thus the Vedic procedure of Śiva's worship has been told in detail. Hear also the excellent Vedic procedure in brief. ॥38॥
1.20.39: With the verse sadyojātam one should fetch the clay; and with vāmadevāya one should pour the water. ॥39॥
1.20.40: With the Aghora mantra one should make the liṅga, and with the mantra tatpuruṣāya one should perform the invocation according to rule. ॥40॥
1.20.41: The wise one should install Hara on the altar with the Īśāna mantra, and should perform all the rest of the procedure in brief. ॥41॥
1.20.42: The wise one should duly perform the worship with the sixteen offerings, using the five-syllable mantra, or likewise the mantra given by the guru. ॥42॥
1.20.43: To Bhava, the destroyer of worldly existence, to Mahādeva we meditate; to Ugra, the destroyer of the fierce, to Śarva, the moon-crested one. ॥43॥
1.20.44: Or the wise one may worship Śaṅkara with this mantra, with true devotion and casting off doubt; for Śiva bestows fruit through devotion alone. ॥44॥
1.20.45: Thus the Vedic sequential worship has been respectfully set forth. Now, O brāhmaṇas, another method is properly explained in its general form. ॥45॥
1.20.46: The worship of the earthen liṅga is prescribed with the names of Śiva. Listen to it, O best of sages, for it grants all desires. ॥46॥
1.20.47: Hara, Maheśvara, Śambhu, Śūlapāṇi, Pinākadhṛk, Śiva, Paśupati and Mahādeva, in this order. ॥47॥
1.20.48: These are for fetching the clay, kneading it, consecration and invocation, bathing, worship, and the dismissal with the words, forgive me. ॥48॥
1.20.49: All these rites should be performed in order with the names beginning with Oṃ, in the dative case and ending with namaḥ, with supreme devotion and joy. ॥49॥
1.20.50: Having properly performed the rite of nyāsa, likewise the six-limbed nyāsa on the hands, with the six-syllable mantra, he should then undertake meditation. ॥50॥
1.20.51: One should meditate on him who is seated in the middle of a throne on the seat of Kailāsa, worshipped by devotees such as Sananda, a forest-fire to the afflictions of his devotees, immeasurable, embraced by Umā, the ornament of the universe. ॥51॥
1.20.52: One should constantly meditate on Maheśa, resembling a silver mountain, with the lovely moon as his crest-ornament, his limbs radiant with jewelled adornments, his hands holding the axe and the deer and showing the boon-giving and fear-dispelling gestures, gracious, seated on a lotus, praised on all sides by hosts of gods, wearing a tiger-skin, the origin of the universe, the seed of the universe, the remover of all fear, five-faced and three-eyed. ॥52॥
1.20.53: Having thus meditated and fully worshipped the excellent earthen liṅga, he should repeat the five-syllable mantra given by the guru, according to rule. ॥53॥
1.20.54: And the wise one, bowing, should praise the Lord of gods with hymns of various names; O best of brāhmaṇas, he should recite the Śatarudriya. ॥54॥
1.20.55: Then, joyfully taking unbroken rice and flowers in his cupped hands, he should entreat Śaṅkara with devotion, with these mantras, out of true devotion. ॥55॥
1.20.56: I am ever yours, O Mṛḍa; your virtues are my very life, my mind is fixed on you. Knowing this, O treasure of compassion, O Lord of beings, be gracious to me. ॥56॥
1.20.57: Whatever japa, worship and the like I have done, whether in ignorance or with knowledge, may it bear fruit by your grace, O Śaṅkara. ॥57॥
1.20.58: Today I am a great sinner, and you are the great purifier. Knowing this, O Lord of Gaurī, do as you wish. ॥58॥
1.20.59: You have not been known, O Mahādeva, by the Vedas, the Purāṇas, the doctrines, or by the various sages; how then could I know you, O Sadāśiva? ॥59॥
1.20.60: Whatever I may be, I am yours with all my being, O Maheśvara. I am surely to be protected by you; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. ॥60॥
1.20.61: Having thus placed the unbroken rice and flowers upon Śiva, he should bow to Śambhu with devotion, with the eight limbs touching the ground, according to rule, O sage. ॥61॥
1.20.62: Then the wise one should perform circumambulation by the prescribed method, and, filled with faith, again praise the Lord of gods with hymns. ॥62॥
1.20.63: Then, making the throat-sound, he should bow with a pure and humble mind; he should respectfully make his petition, and then perform the dismissal. ॥63॥
1.20.64: Thus, O tigers among sages, the worship of the earthen liṅga has been told according to rule; it grants enjoyment and liberation and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥64॥
1.20.65: Whoever reads or even hears this chapter with an attentive mind, his self purified of all sins, will attain all his desires. ॥65॥
1.20.66: This excellent narrative grants long life and health, brings fame and heaven, and gives the happiness of sons, grandsons and the like. ॥66॥
1.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The procedure for worshipping the earthen Śiva-liṅga, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
1.21.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutations to you. Dear one, you have properly explained the procedure for worshipping the earthen linga. ॥1॥
1.21.2: Now, according to the different kinds of desires, kindly tell us, by rule, the number of Śiva's earthen lingas to be made, O you who are tender towards the distressed. ॥2॥
1.21.3: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages, to the procedure of earthen linga worship, by merely performing which a man becomes one who has accomplished his aims. ॥3॥
1.21.4: He who, without making an earthen linga, worships another deity — that worship becomes futile; self-restraint, charity and the rest are futile too. ॥4॥
1.21.5: The number of earthen lingas is told according to each desire; the right number, O best of sages, surely bestows the fruit at once. ॥5॥
1.21.6: There, the initial invocation, the installation and the worship are done separately; the shape of the lingas there should be uniform; everything is to be understood as done for each one separately. ॥6॥
1.21.7: A man seeking learning should lovingly worship a thousand earthen Śiva-lingas; that surely bestows its fruit. ॥7॥
1.21.8: A man seeking wealth should worship half that number of earthen lingas; one seeking a son, fifteen hundred; one seeking clothes, five hundred. ॥8॥
1.21.9: One seeking liberation should worship a crore-fold number; one desiring land, a thousand; one seeking compassion, three thousand; one seeking the merit of pilgrimage, two thousand. ॥9॥
1.21.10: One desiring friends, three thousand; one seeking to subjugate others, eight hundred; one seeking a rite of killing, seven hundred; one seeking to infatuate, eight hundred. ॥10॥
1.21.11: One intent on a rite of driving away an enemy, a thousand, as stated; one seeking to paralyse an enemy, a thousand; one seeking to cause enmity, half that. ॥11॥
1.21.12: One desiring release from fetters, fifteen hundred, the best number; in fear of a great king, five hundred, as the wise should know. ॥12॥
1.21.13: In danger from thieves and the like, two hundred earthen lingas should be known; in fear of ḍākinīs and the like, five hundred earthen lingas are prescribed. ॥13॥
1.21.14: In poverty, five thousand; ten thousand grants all desires. Now I shall tell the daily rite; listen, O best of sages. ॥14॥
1.21.15: One linga is said to remove sin; two lingas grant success in wealth; three lingas are declared the supreme cause of fulfilment of all desires. ॥15॥
1.21.16: Thus the fruit increases progressively, up to the counts stated earlier. Now I shall tell another view on the number, according to the difference among sages. ॥16॥
1.21.17: A wise man, having made ten thousand earthen lingas, surely becomes fearless; he would remove fear of a great king. ॥17॥
1.21.18: For release from prison and the like, the wise man should have ten thousand made; likewise in fear of ḍākinīs and the like, he should have seven thousand made. ॥18॥
1.21.19: One without a son should have fifty-five thousand made; by ten thousand lingas alone one obtains female offspring. ॥19॥
1.21.20: By ten thousand lingas one attains the sovereignty of Viṣṇu and others; by a million lingas one attains incomparable prosperity. ॥20॥
1.21.21: The man on earth who makes one crore of lingas becomes Śiva himself; there need be no doubt about this. ॥21॥
1.21.22: The worship of earthen lingas bestows the fruit of a crore of sacrifices; therefore it always grants enjoyment and liberation to men who seek their desires. ॥22॥
1.21.23: He whose time passes daily without worship of the linga — great loss befalls that ill-behaved, wicked-souled man. ॥23॥
1.21.24: On one side are all gifts, the various vows, pilgrimages, observances and sacrifices; and on the other side is linga worship — so it is held. ॥24॥
1.21.25: In the Kali age, linga worship is the best, as is seen in the world; there is nothing else like it — this is the settled conclusion of the scriptures. ॥25॥
1.21.26: Worshipping daily the linga, which grants enjoyment and liberation and wards off various calamities, a man attains union with Śiva. ॥26॥
1.21.27: The linga, consisting of Śiva's name, is always to be worshipped by the great sages; and since it is foremost among all lingas, it is therefore to be worshipped according to rule. ॥27॥
1.21.28: The linga is declared to be of three kinds by measure — superior, middling and inferior, O tigers among sages; listen to that, I shall tell it. ॥28॥
1.21.29: A linga four finger-breadths high, beautiful and furnished with a pedestal, is called superior by sages versed in the scriptures. ॥29॥
1.21.30: Half of that is called middling; half of that is held to be inferior. Thus the threefold linga is described, each preceding one superior to the next. ॥30॥
1.21.31: He who, endowed with devotion and faith, daily worships many lingas obtains the desires wished for in his mind. ॥31॥
1.21.32: In the four Vedas there is no merit other than that of linga worship; this alone is the conclusion of all scriptures. ॥32॥
1.21.33: Abandoning all this net of rituals entirely, the wise man should worship the one linga with supreme devotion. ॥33॥
1.21.34: When the linga is worshipped, the whole world, moving and unmoving, is worshipped. For those sunk in the ocean of saṃsāra there is no other means of crossing. ॥34॥
1.21.35: For those blinded by the darkness of ignorance, whose minds are attached to sense-objects, there is no other raft in the world apart from linga worship. ॥35॥
1.21.36: The gods headed by Hari and Brahmā, the sages, Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, Cāraṇas, Siddhas, Daityas and Dānavas likewise, ॥36॥
1.21.37: the Nāgas headed by Śeṣa, likewise the birds headed by Garuḍa, and others along with the Prajāpatis, the Manus, Kinnaras and men — ॥37॥
1.21.38: having worshipped with great devotion the linga that grants accomplishment of all aims, they obtained all those various cherished desires abiding in their hearts. ॥38॥
1.21.39: A Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra, or one born of a pratiloma union should constantly worship the linga with reverence, using the mantra appropriate to each. ॥39॥
1.21.40: What is the use of saying much, O sages? Women too, and likewise others — all have the right to worship the Śiva-linga, O twice-born ones. ॥40॥
1.21.41: For the twice-born, worship even by the Vedic path is excellent; but for other beings, worship by the Vedic path is not approved. ॥41॥
1.21.42: For the twice-born who follow the Veda, worship should be performed by the Vedic path, not by any other path — so declared Lord Śiva. ॥42॥
1.21.43: In the twice-born whose minds have been scorched by the curse of Dadhīci, Gautama and others, faith in Vedic rites does not arise at all. ॥43॥
1.21.44: The mortal who, disregarding the Vedic or even the Smārta rite, practises something else, does not obtain the fruit of his resolve. ॥44॥
1.21.45: Having thus performed the worship of Śambhu according to rule up to the food-offering, one should worship right there the eight forms that constitute the three worlds. ॥45॥
1.21.46: Earth, water, fire, wind, ether, the sun and the moon, and the sacrificer — these are declared to be the eight forms. ॥46॥
1.21.47: Śarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhīma, Īśvara, Mahādeva and Paśupati — one should worship these along with the eight forms. ॥47॥
1.21.48: Then, with deep devotion, one should worship Śambhu's retinue there, in order beginning from Īśāna (the north-east), with sandal paste, unbroken rice and leaves. ॥48॥
1.21.49: Īśāna, Nandin, Caṇḍa, Mahākāla, Bhṛṅgin, Vṛṣa, Skanda, Kapardīśa, Soma and Śukra, in that order. ॥49॥
1.21.50: In front, Vīrabhadra, and behind, Kīrtimukha; then one should worship the eleven Rudras according to rule. ॥50॥
1.21.51: Then, having recited the five-syllable mantra and the Śatarudriya, having offered hymns of various kinds, and likewise the recitation of the Pañcāṅga, ॥51॥
1.21.52: then, having circumambulated and bowed, one should dismiss the deity of the liṅga. Thus the entire worship of Śiva has been told with care. ॥52॥
1.21.53: At night one should always perform divine rites facing north; likewise one should always, being pure, perform Śiva's worship facing north. ॥53॥
1.21.54: Not the east, which is in front of Śambhu; not the north, which is joined with Śakti; not the west, since it is his back; therefore one should resort to the acceptable direction. ॥54॥
1.21.55: Without the tripuṇḍra of ash, without a rosary of rudrākṣa, and without bilva leaves, the wise man should never worship Śaṅkara. ॥55॥
1.21.56: O best of sages, if ash is not available when the worship of Śiva has begun, then the tripuṇḍra should be made on the forehead even with clay. ॥56॥
1.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The worship of the earthen liṅga, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
1.22.1: The sages said: Earlier we heard the statement that Śiva's food-offering (naivedya) is not to be accepted. O good sage, tell us the decision on that, and also the greatness of the bilva. ॥1॥
1.22.2: Sūta said: Listen now attentively, all you sages. I will tell you everything with great pleasure. You are blessed, you who are devoted to Śiva's vows. ॥2॥
1.22.3: A devotee of Śiva who is pure and clean, keeps good vows and has firm resolve should eat Śiva's food-offering and give up the idea that it must not be accepted. ॥3॥
1.22.4: Even on seeing Śiva's food-offering, sins go far away; and when Śiva's food-offering is eaten, merits arrive by the crore. ॥4॥
1.22.5: Enough of a thousand sacrifices, enough even of a hundred million sacrifices: when Śiva's food-offering is eaten, one attains union with Śiva (sāyujya). ॥5॥
1.22.6: The house in which even the distribution of Śiva's food-offering takes place becomes wholly purifying, and a cause of purification for others. ॥6॥
1.22.7: When Śiva's food-offering arrives, one should receive it joyfully on one's head and eat it with care, while remembering Śiva. ॥7॥
1.22.8: If, when Śiva's food-offering has arrived, a man thinks it can be taken at another time, then through that delay he indeed becomes tainted with sin. ॥8॥
1.22.9: One in whom no desire arises to receive Śiva's food-offering is the most sinful, the heaviest with sin, and surely goes to hell. ॥9॥
1.22.10: The offering made to a liṅga in the heart, and to one of moonstone or made of gold, silver and the like — it is declared that this is to be eaten by a devotee who has received Śiva-initiation. ॥10॥
1.22.11: A devotee who has Śiva-initiation should eat the auspicious food-offering, called the great grace (mahāprasāda), of all liṅgas. ॥11॥
1.22.12: Now hear gladly the ruling on eating Śiva's food-offering for men who hold other initiations but whose minds delight in devotion to Śiva. ॥12॥
1.22.13: O twice-born, on a liṅga arising from a śālagrāma, on a mercury liṅga (rasaliṅga), on one of stone, silver or gold, on one installed by gods and siddhas, ॥13॥
1.22.14: on one of saffron, of crystal, of gems, and on all the jyotirliṅgas — eating Śambhu's food-offering from these is declared equal to the cāndrāyaṇa vow. ॥14॥
1.22.15: Even a slayer of a brahmin who, having become pure, bears the remains of Śiva's offerings (nirmālya) — by eating it, all his sin is quickly destroyed. ॥15॥
1.22.16: Where Caṇḍa has the right to the offering, it should not be eaten by men; where Caṇḍa has no right, it should be eaten with devotion. ॥16॥
1.22.17: On a bāṇaliṅga, on a metal one, on a siddha-liṅga, on a self-manifested one, and on all images, Caṇḍa has no right. ॥17॥
1.22.18: Whoever, having bathed the liṅga according to rule, drinks the liṅga's bathing water three times — his threefold sin quickly perishes here. ॥18॥
1.22.19: Śiva's food-offering, leaf, flower, fruit and water that are not to be accepted — all of it becomes pure through contact with a śālagrāma stone. ॥19॥
1.22.20: O lords of sages, whatever substance is upon the liṅga is not to be accepted; but what is outside the liṅga's contact should be known as very pure. ॥20॥
1.22.21: Thus the ruling on the food-offering has been told to you, O best of sages. Now hear attentively and respectfully the greatness of the bilva. ॥21॥
1.22.22: This bilva is a form of Mahādeva, praised even by the gods. How can its greatness be known in any way at all? ॥22॥
1.22.23: All the holy pilgrimage places that are renowned in the worlds — all those tīrthas indeed dwell at the root of the bilva. ॥23॥
1.22.24: The meritorious soul who worships the imperishable Mahādeva in liṅga form at the root of the bilva surely attains Śiva. ॥24॥
1.22.25: One who sprinkles his head with water at the root of the bilva becomes as one bathed in all tīrthas; he alone is a purifier on earth. ॥25॥
1.22.26: Then, seeing the excellent water-basin around the root of this bilva filled with water, Mahādeva becomes fully pleased. ॥26॥
1.22.27: The man who worships the bilva's root with sandal-paste, flowers and the like attains Śiva's world, and his lineage grows in happiness. ॥27॥
1.22.28: One who reverently arranges a row of lamps at the bilva's root becomes endowed with knowledge of reality and is absorbed into Maheśa. ॥28॥
1.22.29: One who takes a bilva branch in hand, takes its fresh sprout and worships the bilva is freed from sins. ॥29॥
1.22.30: Whoever with devotion feeds at the bilva's root a person devoted to Śiva — even just one — his merit becomes multiplied ten-million-fold. ॥30॥
1.22.31: One who gives a devotee of Śiva, at the bilva's root, food mixed with milk and ghee is never born poor. ॥31॥
1.22.32: Thus the worship of the Śiva-liṅga with all its main and subsidiary parts has been described. O twice-born, it is of two kinds, according to the distinction between those engaged in worldly life (pravṛtta) and those who have withdrawn from it (nivṛtta). ॥32॥
1.22.33: For those engaged in worldly life, worship on a pedestal (pīṭha) grants all desired things on earth. The worldly worshipper should perform the entire worship using a vessel. ॥33॥
1.22.34: At the end of the ritual bath (abhiṣeka) he should make the food-offering with śāli rice. At the end of the worship he should place the liṅga in a clean casket in a separate room. ॥34॥
1.22.35: Withdrawn worshippers, who worship the liṅga in the hand, should offer their own food. For the withdrawn, the supreme subtle liṅga alone is preeminent. ॥35॥
1.22.36: He should worship with sacred ash (vibhūti) and offer sacred ash; and having thus performed the worship, he should always bear the liṅga on his head. ॥36॥
1.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The food-offering to Śiva, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
1.23.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, greatly fortunate one, disciple of Vyāsa, salutations to you. Tell us, just as you heard it from Vyāsa, the supreme glory of the sacred ash, ॥1॥
1.23.2: and likewise the glory of the rudrākṣa and the supreme glory of the Name. Tell us this triad with great affection and gladden my mind. ॥2॥
1.23.3: Sūta said: Well have you asked this, beneficial to all the worlds. You are indeed greatly blessed, pure, the ornaments of your lineages, ॥3॥
1.23.4: you for whom Śiva himself is the supreme, auspicious deity; the stories of Sadāśiva are ever dear to you in the world. ॥4॥
1.23.5: Those who worship Śiva are blessed and have fulfilled their purpose; their bearing of a body is fruitful, and their family is uplifted. ॥5॥
1.23.6: He in whose mouth is the name of Śiva, always saying Śiva, Śiva — sins do not touch him at all, just as no one touches a glowing coal of khadira wood. ॥6॥
1.23.7: When the mouth utters, salutation to you, O glorious Śiva, that mouth is a purifying holy place (tīrtha), destroying all sins. ॥7॥
1.23.8: And likewise, the man who looks with love upon that mouth obtains the fruit born of visiting a tīrtha — this is firmly established. ॥8॥
1.23.9: O twice-born ones, where these three always abide, that is most auspicious; by the mere sight of such a person one gains the fruit of bathing at the Veṇī (the confluence). ॥9॥
1.23.10: The name of Śiva, the sacred ash, and the rudrākṣa — this triad is greatly meritorious and is held to be equal to the Triveṇī. ॥10॥
1.23.11: He on whose body these three are constantly present — the very sight of him is rare in the world and removes sin. ॥11॥
1.23.12: The sight of him is like the Veṇī; there is not the slightest difference between the two. He who does not understand this is most sinful, without doubt. ॥12॥
1.23.13: He who has no ash on his forehead, no rudrākṣa worn on his body, and no speech full of Śiva in his mouth — one should shun him as one shuns a base person. ॥13॥
1.23.14: Śiva's name is like the Gaṅgā, the ash is regarded as the Yamunā, and the rudrākṣa is declared to be the daughter of Vidhi (Sarasvatī), destroyer of all sins. ॥14॥
1.23.15: The fruit of one on whose body the three are present was placed on one side, and on the other side the fruit born of bathing at the Veṇī, by the wise; ॥15॥
1.23.16: thus it was weighed long ago by the benevolent Brahmā, and it turned out equal. Therefore the three should always be worn by the wise. ॥16॥
1.23.17: From that day onward, this triad is worn by the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and others; and by its mere sight it removes sin. ॥17॥
1.23.18: The sages said: Such fruit has been declared to arise from the triad beginning with the Name. O you of excellent vows, please describe its glory in detail. ॥18॥
1.23.19: Sūta said: O sages, you are greatly wise, true devotees of Śiva, the best among the knowers. O twice-born ones, listen respectfully, with true devotion, to its glory. ॥19॥
1.23.20: Though it is well hidden in the śāstras, the Purāṇas and even the Vedas, O brāhmaṇas, out of affection for you I now bring it to light. ॥20॥
1.23.21: O best of the twice-born, who in the universe fully knows the glory of that triad, apart from Maheśvara, who is beyond being and non-being? ॥21॥
1.23.22: I shall tell, according to my devotion and in brief, the glory of the Name. Listen gladly, O brāhmaṇas, to this supreme account that removes all sins. ॥22॥
1.23.23: By the forest fire of the name Śiva, mountains of great sins are reduced to ashes effortlessly — this is true, true, without doubt. ॥23॥
1.23.24: O Śaunaka, the sorrows rooted in sin, though of many kinds, are destroyed by the name of Śiva alone, and by nothing else at all. ॥24॥
1.23.25: The man on earth who is constantly devoted to repeating Śiva's name is regarded as a true follower of the Veda, a meritorious soul, blessed and wise. ॥25॥
1.23.26: O sage, for those who have faith in the japa of Śiva's name, the various religious duties immediately become ready to bear fruit. ॥26॥
1.23.27: O sage, as many sins as are destroyed by the name of Śiva — so many sins men cannot even commit on earth. ॥27॥
1.23.28: O sage, the name of Śiva, uttered by men, swiftly destroys all the immeasurable heaps of sins such as the killing of a brāhmaṇa. ॥28॥
1.23.29: Those who, having obtained the boat of Śiva's name, cross the ocean of saṃsāra — their sins, which are the root of saṃsāra, perish without doubt. ॥29॥
1.23.30: O great sage, the sins that form the root of saṃsāra are certainly destroyed by the axe of Śiva's name. ॥30॥
1.23.31: The nectar of Śiva's name should be drunk by those tormented by the forest fire of sin; for those scorched by the forest fire of sin there is no relief without it. ॥31॥
1.23.32: Those drenched in the streaming shower of the nectar of the name Śiva never grieve, even in the midst of the forest fire of saṃsāra. ॥32॥
1.23.33: For those great souls in whom great devotion to Śiva's name has arisen, for such people liberation comes swiftly and in every way. ॥33॥
1.23.34: O lord of sages, only in one who has practised austerity through many births would there arise devotion to Śiva's name, which removes all sins. ॥34॥
1.23.35: For him alone who has extraordinary, unbroken devotion to the name of Śambhu is liberation easy to attain, and not for another — such is my view. ॥35॥
1.23.36: Even after committing many sins, one who is devoted to the japa of Śiva's name becomes completely freed from all sins, without doubt. ॥36॥
1.23.37: Just as trees in a forest burnt by a forest fire are reduced to ashes, so are all those sins burnt by the name of Śiva. ॥37॥
1.23.38: He whose limbs are always purified with ash and who is devoted to the japa of Śiva's name surely crosses saṃsāra, O Śaunaka, however terrible it may be. ॥38॥
1.23.39: Even having stolen a brāhmaṇa's property and having killed many brāhmaṇas, a man devoted to the japa of Śiva's name is not tainted by sins. ॥39॥
1.23.40: Having examined all the Vedas, the ancients concluded that the japa of Śiva's name is the supreme means of crossing saṃsāra. ॥40॥
1.23.41: What is the use of saying much, O best of sages? With a single verse I shall tell the greatness of Śiva's name, which removes all sins. ॥41॥
1.23.42: Indeed, as great as is the power of Śambhu's name in removing sins, so much sin a man is never able to commit anywhere. ॥42॥
1.23.43: By the power of Śiva's name, O sage, King Indradyumna of old, though laden with great sins, attained the highest good destiny. ॥43॥
1.23.44: Likewise, O sage, a certain brahmin woman, who was greatly sinful, attained the highest good destiny by the power of Śiva's name. ॥44॥
1.23.45: Thus, O best of brahmins, the supreme greatness of the name has been told to you. Now hear the greatness of the holy ash (bhasma), the purifier of all purifiers. ॥45॥
1.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The greatness of Śiva's name, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
1.24.1: Sūta said: Ash is declared to be of two kinds, supreme and bestowing every auspiciousness. I shall describe its varieties; listen attentively. ॥1॥
1.24.2: The first should be known as the great ash (mahābhasma), the second as that called the minor. The great ash is said to be supreme and of many kinds. ॥2॥
1.24.3: That great ash is said to be threefold: Śrauta, Smārta and Laukika. The ash called minor is indeed described as of many kinds. ॥3॥
1.24.4: The Śrauta and Smārta ash are prescribed only for the twice-born; for all others there is the other, the Laukika ash. ॥4॥
1.24.5: The eminent sages have declared that for the twice-born the wearing of ash is with mantras; for others it should be known as mere wearing, without mantras. ॥5॥
1.24.6: Ash arising from burnt cow-dung is called fiery (āgneya). That too is declared a material for the tripuṇḍra, O great sage. ॥6॥
1.24.7: For wearing the tripuṇḍra, the wise should collect ash arising from the Agnihotra, or else ash arising from other sacrifices. ॥7॥
1.24.8: Smearing should be done with ash, mixed with water, using the seven mantras beginning agnir iti found in the Jābāla Upaniṣad. ॥8॥
1.24.9: For all varṇas and āśramas, smearing and the tripuṇḍra, with mantras or even without mantras, have been taught with reverence by the Jābālas. ॥9॥
1.24.10: Smearing with ash and the horizontal tripuṇḍra, once adopted, should not be abandoned even through negligence by one who seeks liberation; so says the Śruti. ॥10॥
1.24.11: The horizontal tripuṇḍra has been worn by Śiva and by Viṣṇu, and by the goddess Umā and by Lakṣmī, and is praised constantly by others. ॥11॥
1.24.12: Ash has been worn in the form of the tripuṇḍra and smearing by Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and also by those of mixed birth and by outcastes. ॥12॥
1.24.13: Those who do not practise smearing and the tripuṇḍra with faith have no proper conduct in accordance with varṇa and āśrama. ॥13॥
1.24.14: Those who do not practise smearing and the tripuṇḍra with faith have no release from saṃsāra even through crores of births. ॥14॥
1.24.15: Those who do not practise smearing and the tripuṇḍra with faith have no knowledge of Śiva even in hundreds of crores of kalpas. ॥15॥
1.24.16: Those who do not practise smearing and the tripuṇḍra with faith are tainted with great sins; this is the verdict of the scriptures. ॥16॥
1.24.17: Those who do not practise smearing and the tripuṇḍra with faith—everything they do yields contrary results. ॥17॥
1.24.18: In creatures tainted with great sins and hostile to all, a firm hatred of the tripuṇḍra and smearing arises, O sage. ॥18॥
1.24.19: The self-knowing man who, having performed the fire-rite for Śiva, applies the ash with the tryāyuṣa mantra, is freed from all sins by the touch of that ash. ॥19॥
1.24.20: Whoever makes the tripuṇḍra with white ash at the three junctions of the day is freed from all sins and rejoices with Śiva. ॥20॥
1.24.21: He who makes the tripuṇḍra on the forehead with white ash attains the beginningless worlds and becomes immortal. ॥21॥
1.24.22: Without bathing in ash one should not repeat the six-syllabled mantra; having duly made the tripuṇḍra with ash, one should repeat it. ॥22॥
1.24.23: Be he pitiless or base, or laden with all sins, or with minor sins, or a fool, or fallen— ॥23॥
1.24.24: —in whatever region he constantly dwells, bearing the mark of ash, there all the holy places and sacrifices are ever present. ॥24॥
1.24.25: A being bearing the tripuṇḍra is to be honoured by all gods and asuras; even if laden with sin he is pure-souled — how much more one endowed with faith. ॥25॥
1.24.26: To whatever region a knower of Śiva bearing the mark of ash goes, even by chance, there even now the holy places assemble. ॥26॥
1.24.27: What use is saying much here? The wise should always wear ash, always worship the liṅga, and repeat the six-syllabled mantra. ॥27॥
1.24.28: The greatness of wearing ash cannot be fully described even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, the sages or the gods. ॥28॥
1.24.29: Thus one who keeps the conduct of varṇa and āśrama, and even one whose rites of varṇa have lapsed—he too is freed from sin by wearing the tripuṇḍra even once. ॥29॥
1.24.30: Those men who perform rites while shunning one who wears ash have no release from saṃsāra even through crores of births. ॥30॥
1.24.31: The brāhmaṇa who has made the tripuṇḍra on his head with ash has learnt everything from the teacher and has performed everything. ॥31॥
1.24.32: Men who, seeing a wearer of ash, strike him—their birth should be inferred by the learned to be from a caṇḍāla, O brāhmaṇa. ॥32॥
1.24.33: A devout Brāhmaṇa or Kṣatriya should wear ash consecrated with the mantra mā nas toke on the prescribed limbs. ॥33॥
1.24.34: A Vaiśya should wear it with the Tryambaka mantra, a Śūdra with the five-syllabled mantra; for other women and widows the rule is declared to be as for Śūdras. ॥34॥
1.24.35: For a householder it is prescribed with the Pañcabrahma and other mantras; for a celibate student the rule is with the Tryambaka mantra. ॥35॥
1.24.36: For the forest-dweller the rule is with the Aghora mantra; an ascetic should make the tripuṇḍra and the rest with the Praṇava alone. ॥36॥
1.24.37: One beyond varṇa and āśrama should wear it constantly through the supreme contemplation, I am Śiva; and the Śiva-yogin should regularly wear it with the Īśāna mantra. ॥37॥
1.24.38: The excellent wearing of ash should never be abandoned by any of the varṇas, nor likewise by other beings; this is Śiva's command. ॥38॥
1.24.39: As many particles as settle on one's limbs through the ash-bath, so many Śiva-liṅgas does the wearer bear on his body. ॥39॥
1.24.40: Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras and those of mixed birth, women, widows, children, and likewise heretics, all are entitled to it. ॥40॥
1.24.41: A celibate student, a householder, a forest-dweller, a renunciant, or one under a vow, and women too: those marked with the tripuṇḍra of ash are surely liberated. There is no doubt. ॥41॥
1.24.42: Just as fire burns whether one touches it knowingly or unknowingly, so ash worn knowingly or unknowingly purifies a man completely. ॥42॥
1.24.43: One should not take water or food, even a little, without wearing ash and rudrākṣa. If he does eat, whether he is a householder, a forest-dweller, an ascetic, a student, or one of mixed birth, he becomes an eater of sin and goes to hell. For the members of the varṇas, release from that comes through japa of the Gāyatrī; for the ascetic it comes through japa of the principal praṇava. ॥43॥
1.24.44: Those who revile the tripuṇḍra revile Śiva himself, and those who wear it with devotion wear him himself. ॥44॥
1.24.45: Shame on a forehead without ash, shame on a village without a temple of Śiva, shame on a life without worship of the Lord, shame on learning that does not rest on Śiva. ॥45॥
1.24.46: Those who revile Maheśvara Hara, the support of the three worlds, and those who revile one who wears the tripuṇḍra: there is sin even in seeing them. They are like mixed-caste people, swine, asuras, donkeys, dogs, jackals and worms. Once born, they are utterly sinful and fit only for hell. ॥46॥
1.24.47: After seeing them, one should look at the moon or the sun, by night or by day, and not only when awake but even in a dream. One is freed by reciting the Vedic Rudra-sūkta, if one does it with care. By conversing with them a man would surely go to hell, even if he stands on the path of deliverance. Those who revile a man who wears ash and the like are fools indeed. ॥47॥
1.24.48: O sage, a Tāntrika is not qualified for the Śiva-sacrifice, nor is one who wears the vertical mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra). One branded with the heated discus mark is excluded here from the Śiva-sacrifice. ॥48॥
1.24.49: On this subject there are many verses taught in the Bṛhajjābāla Upaniṣad. They should be studied with care, and then one should become devoted to ash. ॥49॥
1.24.50: Even where sandal paste is applied, what is worn mixed with the sandal should be ash alone, as the ash of the tripuṇḍra. If one has any understanding, nothing at all should ever be worn over a forehead marked with vibhūti. ॥50॥
1.24.51: Women should wear the tripuṇḍra of ash up to the hairline, as should the twice-born and others, and widows likewise. In the same way, those who belong to the āśramas should always wear pure vibhūti, which grants the fruit of liberation and destroys all sins. ॥51॥
1.24.52: Whoever makes the tripuṇḍra with ash according to the rule is freed from heaps of great sins and from minor sins as well. ॥52॥
1.24.53: Whether a celibate student, a householder, a forest-dweller or an ascetic; brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas, vaiśyas and śūdras, and also others who are fallen and lowly — ॥53॥
1.24.54: — by smearing the body with ash (uddhūlana) and wearing the tripuṇḍra properly, according to the rule for ash, they cast off their mass of sins and become pure. ॥54॥
1.24.55: The wearer of ash, above all, is freed from sins such as killing a woman or a cow, and from killing a hero or a horse. There is no doubt about this. ॥55॥
1.24.56: Stealing another's property, violating another's wife, reviling others, seizing another's field, harming others, ॥56॥
1.24.57: seizing crops, gardens and the like, deeds such as burning houses, accepting cows, gold, buffaloes and the like, sesame, blankets, clothes, ॥57॥
1.24.58: food, grain, water and the like, when accepted from base people; intercourse with fisherwomen, prostitutes, Mātaṅga women, śūdra women and actresses, ॥58॥
1.24.59: intercourse with menstruating women, unmarried girls and widows; the sale of meat, hides, juices and the like, and of salt, ॥59॥
1.24.60: slander, deceitful speech, and the sins of those who seek false testimony: these and countless other sins of many kinds are destroyed at once by wearing the tripuṇḍra. ॥60॥
1.24.61: Stealing Śiva's property, reviling Śiva at any time, and reviling Śiva's devotees: one guilty of these is not purified by any expiation. ॥61॥
1.24.62: He who has rudrākṣa on his limbs and the tripuṇḍra on his forehead is to be honoured even if he is a cāṇḍāla; he is the very best among all the varṇas. ॥62॥
1.24.63: He who bears the tripuṇḍra on his forehead has, in effect, bathed in every tīrtha in this world and in every river, the Gaṅgā and the rest. ॥63॥
1.24.64: Seven crores of great mantras headed by the five-syllabled mantra, and other mantras by the crore that lead to Śaiva liberation (kaivalya), ॥64॥
1.24.65: and the other mantras of the gods that bring every kind of happiness, O sage: all of them come under the control of one who bears the tripuṇḍra. ॥65॥
1.24.66: One who makes the tripuṇḍra uplifts a thousand kinsmen of his line already born and a thousand yet to be born. ॥66॥
1.24.67: Having enjoyed every pleasure here, long-lived and free from disease, at the end of life he meets death with ease. ॥67॥
1.24.68: Having gained an auspicious divine body endowed with the eight powers, and mounting a divine aerial car attended by celestial gods, ॥68॥
1.24.69: in the worlds of all the Vidyādharas, of the mighty Gandharvas, and of Indra and the other world-guardians, in due order, ॥69॥
1.24.70: and also in the realms of the Prajāpatis, he enjoys abundant pleasures. Then, reaching the realm of Brahmā, he sports there with a hundred maidens. ॥70॥
1.24.71: There, after enjoying pleasures of many kinds for the span of Brahmā's life, he enjoys pleasure in Viṣṇu's world until a hundred Brahmās have passed away. ॥71॥
1.24.72: Then, reaching Śiva's world and gaining the imperishable fulfilment of his wishes, he attains union with Śiva (śivasāyujya). No doubt arises about this. ॥72॥
1.24.73: After examining the essence of all the Upaniṣads again and again, this alone has been settled: the tripuṇḍra is the highest good. ॥73॥
1.24.74: A brāhmaṇa who reviles vibhūti was fathered by another; he goes to a terrible hell for as long as four-faced Brahmā lasts. ॥74॥
1.24.75: At śrāddha, sacrifice, japa, homa, the vaiśvadeva rite and the worship of the gods, a man who wears the tripuṇḍra is pure in spirit and conquers death. ॥75॥
1.24.76: Bathing in water removes dirt; bathing in ash makes one always pure; bathing in mantras removes sin; in bathing in knowledge lies the supreme state. ॥76॥
1.24.77: Whatever merit and whatever fruit come from all the tīrthas, a man who bathes in ash obtains that fruit. ॥77॥
1.24.78: Bathing in ash is the supreme tīrtha; it equals bathing in the Gaṅgā day after day. Śiva himself is present in the form of ash, and ash purifies the three worlds. ॥78॥
1.24.79: Whatever a brāhmaṇa performs without the tripuṇḍra is not true bathing, not meditation, not giving, nor japa. ॥79॥
1.24.80: For a forest-dweller, for unmarried girls, and likewise for uninitiated men, the ash is applied mixed with water before midday and without water after it. ॥80॥
1.24.81: Whoever applies the tripuṇḍra in this way every day with a controlled mind should be known as a devotee of Śiva. He obtains both enjoyment and liberation. ॥81॥
1.24.82: If on someone's body there is not even a single rudrākṣa, which bestows great merit, and if he is also without the tripuṇḍra, his birth is meaningless. ॥82॥
1.24.83: Thus I have told you in brief the greatness of the tripuṇḍra. This secret should be kept from all creatures; it must be guarded by you. ॥83॥
1.24.84: O eminent sages, three lines are indeed made on all the places, beginning with the forehead, as prescribed by the wise, O sage. ॥84॥
1.24.85: Starting from the middle of the eyebrows and extending to where the eyebrows end, the tripuṇḍra should be worn on the forehead to that length. ॥85॥
1.24.86: Lines drawn with the middle and ring fingers, and in the middle a line drawn in the reverse direction with the thumb—this is called the tripuṇḍra. ॥86॥
1.24.87: Taking the ash carefully with the three middle fingers, one should devoutly wear the supreme tripuṇḍra, which grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥87॥
1.24.88: Each of the three lines has nine deities, on the limbs everywhere. I shall tell them; listen attentively. ॥88॥
1.24.89: The letter A, the Gārhapatya fire, the earth (bhūḥ), dharma, the rajas quality, the Ṛgveda, the power of action, and the morning soma-pressing, ॥89॥
1.24.90: and Mahādeva—these are the deities of the first line, O tigers among sages, to be known by those devoted to Śiva-initiation. ॥90॥
1.24.91: The letter U, the Dakṣiṇa fire, the principle of the sky, likewise the Yajurveda, the midday soma-pressing, the power of will and the inner self, ॥91॥
1.24.92: and Maheśvara—these are the deities of the second line, O tiger among sages, to be known by those devoted to Śiva-initiation. ॥92॥
1.24.93: The letter M and the Āhavanīya fire, the supreme self, tamas and heaven, the power of knowledge, the Sāmaveda, and likewise the third soma-pressing, ॥93॥
1.24.94: and Śiva—these are the deities of the third line, O tiger among sages, to be known by those devoted to Śiva-initiation. ॥94॥
1.24.95: Having thus daily saluted with true devotion the deities of the places, one who is pure should wear the tripuṇḍra; he obtains enjoyment and liberation. ॥95॥
1.24.96: Thus the deities of the places on all the limbs have been told, O lords of sages. Now hear with devotion the places connected with them. ॥96॥
1.24.97: One should apply the mark on thirty-two places, or on half that—sixteen places—or likewise on eight places, or even on five places. ॥97॥
1.24.98: On the head, the forehead, the two ears and likewise the two eyes, on the nose, mouth and throat, then on both hands, ॥98॥
1.24.99: on the elbows, wrists, heart, both sides, the navel, the two testicles, the thighs, ankles and knees, ॥99॥
1.24.100: on the two shanks and the two feet — these are the excellent thirty-two places. Their deities are Agni, water, earth, wind, the directions, the regions, the guardians of the directions, together with the Vasus. ॥100॥
1.24.101: Dharā, Dhruva, Soma, Āpa, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāta are declared to be the eight Vasus. ॥101॥
1.24.102: O wise ones, one should wear the tripuṇḍra merely by uttering the names of these; or, with a collected mind, one may make the tripuṇḍra on sixteen places: ॥102॥
1.24.103: on the head, the forehead, the throat, the two shoulders, the arm, the elbow, the wrist, the heart, the navel, the sides, ॥103॥
1.24.104: and on the back. Having placed the mark thus, one should worship there the two Aśvin deities, Śiva, Śakti, likewise Rudra, Īśa and Nārada, ॥104॥
1.24.105: and the nine Śaktis beginning with Vāmā—these are the sixteen deities. Nāsatya and Dasra are declared to be the two Aśvins. ॥105॥
1.24.106: Or else: on the crown, on the hair, the two ears, likewise the face, the two arms, the heart, the navel, likewise the pair of thighs, ॥106॥
1.24.107: the two knees, the feet and the back — sixteen places. Their deities are Śiva, Candra, Rudra, Ka (Brahmā), Vighneśa, or Viṣṇu, ॥107॥
1.24.108: and Śrī; in the heart Śambhu, likewise at the navel Prajāpati; the Nāga and the Nāga maidens, and on the two thighs the daughters of the sages, ॥108॥
1.24.109: on the feet the oceans, and on the broad back the holy places (tīrthas). Such are the sixteen places; now the eight places are described. ॥109॥
1.24.110: The private part, the forehead, the excellent pair of ears, the two shoulders, the heart and the navel—this is the group of eight. ॥110॥
1.24.111: Brahmā and the seven sages are declared to be the deities here. So it has been taught by the knowers of the ash, O lords of sages. ॥111॥
1.24.112: Or else, the head, the two arms, the heart and the navel—those who know the ash declare these to be the five places for wearing it. ॥112॥
1.24.113: One should do as is possible, according to place, time and other circumstances. If one is unable even to smear the whole body with ash, one should apply the tripuṇḍra and the like. ॥113॥
1.24.114: Remembering Śiva, the three-eyed, the support of the three guṇas, the begetter of the three gods, one should apply the tripuṇḍra on the forehead, saying namaḥ śivāya. ॥114॥
1.24.115: Saying īśābhyāṃ namaḥ, one should apply the tripuṇḍra on the two sides; saying bījābhyāṃ namaḥ, one should wear it on the two forearms. ॥115॥
1.24.116: Below, one should apply it saying pitṛbhyāṃ namaḥ (to the two parents), and above, umeśābhyāṃ namaḥ (to Umā and Īśa); then on the back and likewise on the back of the head, saying bhīmāya namaḥ. ॥116॥
1.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The wearing of ash, in the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
1.25.1: Sūta said: O sage Śaunaka, greatly wise one, embodiment of Śiva, great lord, listen: I shall narrate briefly the glory of the rudrākṣa. ॥1॥
1.25.2: The rudrākṣa should be known as most dear to Śiva and supremely purifying; through seeing it, touching it, and doing japa with it, it is held to remove all sins. ॥2॥
1.25.3: Formerly, O sage, the glory of the rudrākṣa was told in the presence of the Goddess by Śiva, the Supreme Self, for the benefit of the world. ॥3॥
1.25.4: Śiva said: Listen, O Maheśānī, O Śivā, to the greatness of the rudrākṣa; I tell it out of love for you and from a wish for the welfare of the devotees. ॥4॥
1.25.5: Long ago, O Maheśānī, as I was performing penance for thousands of divine years, having restrained my mind, my mind became agitated. ॥5॥
1.25.6: O Parameśānī, I, the independent Supreme Lord who works for the good of the worlds, playfully opened my eyes. ॥6॥
1.25.7: From the lids of my beautiful eyes drops of water fell; from those teardrops arose the trees called rudrākṣa. ॥7॥
1.25.8: Having become immobile trees, for the sake of showing grace to devotees, they were given to the devotees of Viṣṇu and to the four classes. ॥8॥
1.25.9: On earth I caused the rudrākṣas, beloved of Śiva, to grow in Gauḍa, and likewise in Mathurā, Ayodhyā, Laṅkā and Malaya, ॥9॥
1.25.10: and on the Sahya mountain, in Kāśī, and in other regions too — rudrākṣas that are supreme, that shatter masses of unbearable sins, and are enjoined by the Veda. ॥10॥
1.25.11: By my command rudrākṣas were born on earth as Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas and Śūdras — auspicious beads belonging to those classes. ॥11॥
