1.25.12: The wise should know their colours in order as white, red, yellow and black. People should wear the rudrākṣa of their own class, according to colour, in due order. ॥12॥
1.25.13: That fruit should be worn by the classes desiring the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, and especially by Śiva's devotees, always for the pleasure of Śiva and Śivā. ॥13॥
1.25.14: One that is the size of an āmalaka fruit is declared the best; one only the size of a jujube fruit is called middling. ॥14॥
1.25.15: One the size of a chickpea is the lowest; this is the excellent rule stated. Listen, O Pārvatī, with great love, for the welfare of the devotees. ॥15॥
1.25.16: Even one that is only the size of a jujube fruit, O Maheśvarī, still bestows fruit in the world and increases happiness and good fortune. ॥16॥
1.25.17: One equal to an āmalaka fruit destroys all misfortunes; one like a guñjā seed accomplishes the fruit of all aims. ॥17॥
1.25.18: The smaller it is, the greater the fruit it gives. The wise declare the fruit of each one, in turn, to be greater by a tenth. ॥18॥
1.25.19: Wearing the rudrākṣa is declared to be for the destruction of sin; therefore it should certainly be worn, as it surely accomplishes all aims. ॥19॥
1.25.20: As the rudrākṣa is seen in the world to be auspicious and fruit-giving, no other rosary is seen to be so, O Parameśvarī. ॥20॥
1.25.21: Rudrākṣas that are even, glossy, firm, large and furnished with thorn-like ridges are auspicious, O Goddess; they grant desires and always bestow enjoyment and liberation. ॥21॥
1.25.22: One should reject six kinds of rudrākṣas: worm-eaten, cut, broken, lacking thorn-like ridges, having cracks, and not round. ॥22॥
1.25.23: A rudrākṣa with a naturally formed hole is the best here; one in which the hole is made by human effort is middling. ॥23॥
1.25.24: Wearing rudrākṣas is declared to destroy great sins. Having worn a hundred times the number of the Rudras eleven hundred, a man becomes of Rudra's form. ॥24॥
1.25.25: The fruit obtained here by wearing eleven hundred cannot be described even in hundreds of years. ॥25॥
1.25.26: A crown is prescribed of five hundred plus half a hundred, that is, five hundred and fifty; the excellent, devoted man should properly fashion it from rudrākṣas. ॥26॥
1.25.27: Likewise, one intent on devotion should make a sacred thread of three hundred and sixty rudrākṣas, in three strands. ॥27॥
1.25.28: Three rudrākṣas are prescribed for the topknot, O Maheśvarī, and six each for the ears, left and right. ॥28॥
1.25.29: A hundred and one at the neck; on the arms, by the number of the Rudras eleven; likewise at the elbow joints and again at the wrist. ॥29॥
1.25.30: Men devoted to Śiva should wear three on the sacred thread, and should wear the remaining leftover ones, five in number, at the waist. ॥30॥
1.25.31: O Parameśvarī, one who has worn rudrākṣas in this number — that form is to be bowed to and praised by all, like Maheśa. ॥31॥
1.25.32: When one sees such a person, seated on a seat, absorbed in meditation and uttering Śiva, one is released from sins. ॥32॥
1.25.33: This rule for eleven hundred has been declared; in its absence, I now describe another auspicious method. ॥33॥
1.25.34: One should wear one rudrākṣa on the topknot, thirty on the head, fifty on the neck, and sixteen on each arm; ॥34॥
1.25.35: twelve at the wrist; on the two shoulders he should wear five hundred; and he should make a garland-like sacred thread of a hundred and eight. ॥35॥
1.25.36: He who, firm in his vow, wears a thousand rudrākṣas in this way — all the gods bow to him; as Rudra is, so is he. ॥36॥
1.25.37: Another way: one rudrākṣa on the topknot, forty on the head, thirty-two at the throat, and a hundred and eight on the chest; ॥37॥
1.25.38: one or six each on the ears, sixteen each on the arms, and on the hands twice the number of the Suns twenty-four, O lord of sages. ॥38॥
1.25.39: He who lovingly wears this number is also a supreme Śaiva; he is to be worshipped like Śiva and constantly revered by all. ॥39॥
1.25.40: The rudrākṣa should be worn on the head with the Īśāna mantra, on the ear with the Tatpuruṣa, on the neck with the Aghora, and with that same mantra on the heart as well. ॥40॥
1.25.41: With the Aghora seed-mantra the wise man should wear rudrākṣas on his two hands, and with the Vāmadeva mantra a string threaded with fifteen beads on the belly. ॥41॥
1.25.42: With the five Brahma mantras and the aṅga mantras he should wear a triple garland, or garlands of five and of seven; or else he should wear all the beads with the root mantra. ॥42॥
1.25.43: Then he should avoid eating liquor, meat, garlic, onion, drumstick, śleṣmāntaka fruit, and the village pig. ॥43॥
1.25.44: A white rudrākṣa is prescribed here for those born as brāhmaṇas; a deep red one delights kṣatriyas, O Umā; a yellow one should be worn constantly, every day, by vaiśyas — it is indeed obligatory; and likewise a black one by śūdras. This is the path declared by the Veda, O daughter of the mountain. ॥44॥
1.25.45: The celibate student, the forest-dweller, the householder and the ascetic should wear it regularly; one devoted to this supreme secret should never remain without it. This wearing of rudrākṣa is attained through good deeds; abandoning it, people go to all the hells. ॥45॥
1.25.46: First come those the size of an āmalaka, then smaller ones. Those that are broken, those damaged in their spikes, those eaten by worms, and likewise those lacking the hole for the thread should not be worn by those who seek auspiciousness — nor, finally, a rudrākṣa as small as a chickpea. The rudrākṣa is my auspicious emblem, O Umā; the fine one is always praised. ॥46॥
1.25.47: By Śiva's command, rudrākṣas are always to be worn by people of all stages of life and all classes, by women and śūdras; by ascetics, indeed, with the praṇava (Oṃ). ॥47॥
1.25.48: Wearing it by day, one is freed from sins committed at night; wearing it at night, from sins committed by day; wearing it at morning, noon and evening, one is freed from all sins. ॥48॥
1.25.49: Those in the world who bear the tripuṇḍra, those who wear matted hair, and those who wear rudrākṣa — they indeed do not go to the world of Yama. ॥49॥
1.25.50: He who wears a single rudrākṣa on his head and likewise the tripuṇḍra in the middle of the forehead — those who repeat the five-syllable mantra are surely to be honoured by you, for they are holy men. ॥50॥
1.25.51: He on whose body there is no rudrākṣa, no tripuṇḍra on the forehead, and no five-syllable mantra in his mouth — bring him to the abode of Yama. ॥51॥
1.25.52: Knowing well its power, those who wear ash and rudrākṣa are always to be honoured by us; they are never to be brought here. ॥52॥
1.25.53: Thus did even Kāla (Yama) command his own servants. Accepting it and saying, so be it, they all remained silent, greatly amazed. ॥53॥
1.25.54: For this very reason, O Great Goddess, the rudrākṣa is a destroyer of sin; its wearer is dear to me and pure, even if exceedingly sinful, O Pārvatī. ॥54॥
1.25.55: Whoever wears rudrākṣa on the hand, the arm and the head cannot be slain by any being, and moves about on earth in the form of Rudra. ॥55॥
1.25.56: He is always to be revered by all gods and demons, worthy of worship, and, when seen, a destroyer of sin, just like Śiva. ॥56॥
1.25.57: Even one devoid of meditation and knowledge, if he wears rudrākṣa, is freed from all sins and attains the supreme goal. ॥57॥
1.25.58: For one repeating a mantra with a rudrākṣa the merit becomes ten-million-fold; by wearing it a man obtains merit a hundred-million-fold. ॥58॥
1.25.59: As long as it remains on the body of a living being, so long, O Goddess, untimely death does not afflict him. ॥59॥
1.25.60: On seeing one marked with the tripuṇḍra, his limbs adorned with rudrākṣa, and repeating the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, one obtains the fruit of Rudra worship. ॥60॥
1.25.61: The devotee who loves the five deities, and likewise one who loves all the gods, may repeat all mantras with a rudrākṣa rosary, O beloved. ॥61॥
1.25.62: Devotees of Viṣṇu and other gods should also wear them, no doubt; a devotee of Rudra should especially and always wear rudrākṣas. ॥62॥
1.25.63: Rudrākṣas are said to be of many kinds; I shall tell their varieties, which grant the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. Listen, O Pārvatī, with true devotion. ॥63॥
1.25.64: The one-faced rudrākṣa is Śiva himself, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation; by its mere sight it removes the sin of killing a brāhmaṇa. ॥64॥
1.25.65: Where it is worshipped, there Lakṣmī is never far away; all calamities perish and all desires are fulfilled. ॥65॥
1.25.66: The two-faced is the Lord of the gods of gods, granting the fruit of all desires; that rudrākṣa especially destroys the sin of cow-slaying swiftly. ॥66॥
1.25.67: The rudrākṣa that is three-faced always directly grants accomplishment; by its power all branches of learning become firmly established. ॥67॥
1.25.68: The four-faced is Brahmā himself; it removes the sin of homicide; by sight and touch it at once grants the fruit of the four aims of life. ॥68॥
1.25.69: The five-faced is Rudra himself, the Lord named Kālāgni; it grants every liberation and the fruit of all desires. ॥69॥
1.25.70: The sin of intercourse with a forbidden woman, eating what is forbidden — all such sins the five-faced removes. ॥70॥
1.25.71: The six-faced is Kārttikeya; by wearing it on the right arm one is freed from sins such as brāhmaṇa-slaying — there is no doubt here. ॥71॥
1.25.72: The seven-faced, O Great Goddess, is named Anaṅga; by wearing it, O Queen of the gods, even a poor man becomes a lord. ॥72॥
1.25.73: The eight-faced rudrākṣa is Vasumūrti and Bhairava; by wearing it one enjoys a full lifespan and after death becomes the Trident-bearer (Śiva). ॥73॥
1.25.74: The nine-faced is regarded as Bhairava and the sage Kapila; or its presiding deity is Durgā, the Great Goddess of nine forms. ॥74॥
1.25.75: One intent on devotion should wear that rudrākṣa on the left hand; he surely becomes lord of all, equal to me — there is no doubt. ॥75॥
1.25.76: The ten-faced, O Great Goddess, is the god Janārdana himself; by wearing it, O Queen of the gods, one obtains all desires. ॥76॥
1.25.77: The rudrākṣa that is eleven-faced, O Supreme Goddess, is Rudra; by wearing it one becomes victorious everywhere. ॥77॥
1.25.78: One should wear the twelve-faced rudrākṣa in the region of the hair; all the twelve Ādityas are present in it. ॥78॥
1.25.79: The thirteen-faced is Viśvedeva; by wearing it a man obtains all desires and gains good fortune and auspiciousness. ॥79॥
1.25.80: The rudrākṣa that is fourteen-faced is the supreme Śiva; one should wear it on the head with devotion — all sin perishes. ॥80॥
1.25.81: Thus the kinds of rudrākṣa have been described according to the number of their faces. Now, O daughter of the lord of mountains, listen with affection to their respective mantras in order. ॥81॥
1.25.82: The mantras are: 1. Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; 2. Oṃ namaḥ; 3. Oṃ klīṃ namaḥ; 4. Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; 5. Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; 6. Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ namaḥ; 7. Oṃ huṃ namaḥ; 8. Oṃ huṃ namaḥ; 9. Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ namaḥ; 10. Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; 11. Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ namaḥ; 12. Oṃ krauṃ kṣauṃ rauṃ namaḥ; 13. Oṃ hrīṃ namaḥ; 14. Oṃ namaḥ. Endowed with devotion and faith, and free from sloth, O Goddess, one should wear the rudrākṣas with these mantras for the attainment of all desires and aims. ॥82॥
1.25.83: The man on earth who wears a rudrākṣa without a mantra goes to a terrible hell for as long as fourteen Indras reign. ॥83॥
1.25.84: On seeing one wearing a rudrākṣa garland, the bhūtas, pretas and piśācas, the ḍākinīs and śākinīs, and whatever other malevolent beings there are — ॥84॥
1.25.85: and whatever artificial spell there is, and whatever black magic and the like — all that flees far away on seeing one whose body inspires fear. ॥85॥
1.25.86: On seeing one wearing a rudrākṣa garland, Śiva and Viṣṇu are pleased, as are the Goddess, Gaṇapati, Sūrya and the other gods too, O Pārvatī. ॥86॥
1.25.87: Knowing thus the greatness of the rudrākṣa, O Great Goddess, they should be worn properly, with mantras and with devotion, for the increase of dharma. ॥87॥
1.25.88: Thus did Śiva, the Supreme Self, declare before Girijā the greatness of sacred ash and rudrākṣa, which bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥88॥
1.25.89: Those who wear ash and rudrākṣa should be known as exceedingly dear to Śiva; by the power of wearing them come enjoyment and liberation, without doubt. ॥89॥
1.25.90: He who wears ash and rudrākṣa is called a devotee of Śiva; devoted to repetition of the five-syllable mantra, he is fully perfected in Śiva's presence. ॥90॥
1.25.91: Without the tripuṇḍra of ash and without a rudrākṣa garland, Mahādeva, even when worshipped, does not grant the desired fruit. ॥91॥
1.25.92: All that you asked, O lord of sages, has been fully explained: the greatness of ash and rudrākṣa, which grants the fulfilment of all desires. ॥92॥
1.25.93: Whoever listens daily with devotion to this supreme and auspicious greatness of rudrākṣa and ash will obtain all desires. ॥93॥
1.25.94: Having enjoyed every happiness here, accompanied by sons, grandsons and others, he will attain true liberation hereafter and become exceedingly dear to Śiva. ॥94॥
1.25.95: This Vidyeśvara Saṃhitā has been told to you, O lords of sages; by Śiva's command it always bestows every accomplishment and grants liberation. ॥95॥
1.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The greatness of the rudrākṣa, in the Sādhyasādhana-khaṇḍa of the first saṃhitā, the Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
